people.name: Brooke Rollins
people.politics: Conservative policy advocate; as Secretary has supported corn ethanol and pledged relief for farmers amid tariff uncertainty.
people.description: Brooke Rollins is the U.S. Secretary of Agriculture, in office since February 13, 2025 after a 72-28 Senate confirmation vote. She previously led the Texas Public Policy Foundation and the America First Policy Institute and served in the first Trump administration as director of the Office of American Innovation and acting director of the Domestic Policy Council.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Second_Portrait_of_Secretary_Rollins.jpg
people.educationNote: B.S. in agricultural development, Texas A&M University (cum laude); J.D., University of Texas School of Law

people.name: Chris Wright
people.politics: His Department of Energy biography says he is focused on unleashing American energy dominance, accelerating innovation and advancing all energy sources that are affordable, reliable and secure.
people.description: Chris Wright is an American energy executive who has served as the 17th U.S. Secretary of Energy since February 3, 2025. He founded Pinnacle Technologies and Liberty Energy (originally Liberty Oilfield Services) and was Liberty's chairman and chief executive before his cabinet appointment.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Secretary_Chris_Wright_Official_Portrait.png
people.educationNote: Bachelor's in mechanical engineering and master's in electrical engineering, MIT; graduate study at UC Berkeley without degree

people.name: Condoleezza Rice
people.politics: Republican; served in the George W. Bush administration as National Security Advisor and Secretary of State.
people.description: Condoleezza Rice served as the 66th United States Secretary of State from January 2005 to January 2009, after serving as National Security Advisor from 2001 to 2005. She has directed the Hoover Institution at Stanford University since September 1, 2020.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Condoleezza Rice cropped.jpg

people.name: Doug Burgum
people.politics: Described himself in 2016 as a social moderate and fiscal conservative; supports expanded domestic oil, gas and coal production and energy independence.
people.description: Doug Burgum is the 55th U.S. Secretary of the Interior, in office since February 1, 2025, and chairs the National Energy Dominance Council established by Executive Order 14213. He was the 33rd governor of North Dakota from December 2016 to December 2024 and earlier led Great Plains Software until its 2001 sale to Microsoft.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Doug_Burgum_2025_DOI_portrait_(cropped)(b).jpg

people.name: Doug Collins
people.politics: Opposes abortion and the Affordable Care Act, voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, and is an ally of President Trump.
people.description: Doug Collins is the 12th United States Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in office since February 5, 2025, following a 77-23 Senate confirmation vote. He previously represented Georgia's 9th congressional district in the U.S. House (2013-2021) and is a chaplain in the U.S. Air Force Reserve.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official_portrait_of_Douglas_Collins,_U.S._Secretary_of_Veterans_Affairs.jpeg

people.name: Gina Raimondo
people.politics: Former Governor of Rhode Island and venture capitalist who served as Secretary of Commerce under President Biden.
people.description: Gina Raimondo served as the 40th United States Secretary of Commerce from March 2021 to January 2025 under President Joe Biden. She was previously the 75th Governor of Rhode Island from 2015 to 2021 and oversaw implementation of the CHIPS and Science Act at the Commerce Department.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Secretary Gina Raimondo.jpg

people.name: Hillary Clinton
people.politics: Democrat; U.S. Senator from New York 2001-2009 and the 2016 Democratic presidential nominee.
people.description: Hillary Clinton served as the 67th United States Secretary of State from January 2009 to February 2013, after representing New York in the U.S. Senate from 2001 to 2009. She was the Democratic Party's nominee for president in 2016 and later joined the faculty of Columbia University.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Hillary Clinton official Secretary of State portrait crop.jpg

people.name: Howard Lutnick
people.politics: Republican since 2016 (previously Democratic); co-chaired Donald Trump's 2024 presidential transition team and, as Commerce Secretary, has publicly defended the administration's tariff policy.
people.health: Disclosed in October 2021 a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (diffuse large B-cell), with a planned course of six chemotherapy treatments running through January 2022.
people.description: Howard Lutnick is an American financier who has served as United States Secretary of Commerce since February 21, 2025. He was previously chairman and chief executive of Cantor Fitzgerald and a co-chair of Donald Trump's 2024 presidential transition team.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Howard_Lutnick_2025.jpg

people.name: James Mattis
people.politics: Independent; retired Marine Corps general who served as Defense Secretary in the first Trump administration.
people.description: James Mattis, a retired four-star U.S. Marine Corps general, served as the 26th United States Secretary of Defense from January 20, 2017 to January 1, 2019. He announced his resignation on December 20, 2018, citing policy differences with President Trump over the Syria troop withdrawal.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:James Mattis official photo.jpg (Monica King, U.S. Department of Defense, CC BY 2.0)
people.educationNote: B.A. in history, Central Washington University (1971); M.A. in international security affairs, National War College (1994)

people.name: Jamieson Greer
people.politics: Has supported President Trump's tariff policy, seeking to implement it legally and to negotiate trade agreements; opposes digital service taxes and favors stricter economic policies toward China.
people.description: Jamieson Greer is an American trade attorney and former U.S. Air Force judge advocate who has served as United States Trade Representative since February 2025. He was chief of staff to USTR Robert Lighthizer from 2017 to 2020 and a partner at King & Spalding before his nomination.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official portrait of U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer (cropped 2).jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in international studies, Brigham Young University; joint master's degree in global business law, Sciences Po and Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne (2006); J.D., University of Virginia School of Law

people.name: Janet Yellen
people.politics: Economist who served in Democratic administrations as Council of Economic Advisers chair, Federal Reserve Chair and Treasury Secretary.
people.description: Janet Yellen served as the 78th United States Secretary of the Treasury from January 2021 to January 2025 and was the first woman to hold the post. She was previously Chair of the Federal Reserve from 2014 to 2018 and is the first person to have led the Council of Economic Advisers, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury Department.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Secretary Janet Yellen portrait.jpg

people.name: Jay Clayton
people.politics: Registered independent; has donated to Barack Obama's and Mitt Romney's presidential campaigns and, in 2015, to Jeb Bush's 2016 campaign.
people.description: Walter Joseph "Jay" Clayton III is an American attorney who has served as the ninth Director of National Intelligence since August 3, 2026, after the Senate confirmed him 51-47 on July 28, 2026. He was previously U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York (2025-2026) and Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission (2017-2020).
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official_portrait_of_Jay_Clayton_(2026).jpg
people.educationNote: B.S. in engineering, University of Pennsylvania (1988); B.A. in economics, University of Cambridge (1990); J.D., University of Pennsylvania Law School (1993)

people.name: Jeff Sessions
people.politics: Conservative Republican who championed conservative social and economic issues and took hardline positions on immigration and drug sentencing.
people.religion: United Methodist (member of Ashland Place United Methodist Church, Mobile, Alabama)
people.description: Jeff Sessions is an American Republican lawyer and politician who served as the 84th U.S. Attorney General from February 2017 until his resignation in November 2018. He previously represented Alabama in the U.S. Senate from 1997 to 2017 and lost the July 2020 Republican Senate runoff to Tommy Tuberville.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Jeff_Sessions,_official_portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A., Huntingdon College (1969); J.D., University of Alabama School of Law (1973)

people.name: John Kerry
people.politics: Democrat; U.S. Senator from Massachusetts 1985-2013 and the 2004 Democratic presidential nominee.
people.description: John Kerry served as the 68th United States Secretary of State from February 2013 to January 2017, following 28 years as a U.S. Senator from Massachusetts. He later served as the first Special Presidential Envoy for Climate, from January 2021 until March 2024.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:John Kerry official Secretary of State portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A., Yale University (1966); J.D., Boston College (1976)

people.name: John Ratcliffe
people.office: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency
people.politics: Ran as a libertarian conservative in opposition to broad government spending in 2014 and is considered a Trump ally.
people.description: John Ratcliffe is an American attorney and politician who has served as Director of the Central Intelligence Agency since January 23, 2025. He previously served as Director of National Intelligence (2020-2021) and represented Texas's 4th congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives from 2015 to 2020.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:John_Ratcliffe_official_photo.jpg
people.educationNote: Bachelor's degree, University of Notre Dame (1986); J.D., Southern Methodist University School of Law (1989)

people.name: Keith Sonderling
people.politics: Registered Republican appointed by Donald Trump to the EEOC (2020) and as Deputy Secretary of Labor (2025); as an EEOC commissioner he advocated federal guidance on employer use of artificial intelligence.
people.description: Keith Sonderling is an American lawyer who has served as United States Secretary of Labor since October 2, 2026, after serving as acting secretary from April 20, 2026. He previously served as Deputy Secretary of Labor and as a commissioner of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Deputy_Secretary_Sonderling.jpg
people.educationNote: B.S., University of Florida (magna cum laude); J.D., Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad College of Law (2008, magna cum laude)

people.name: Kelly Loeffler
people.office: Administrator of the Small Business Administration
people.politics: Describes herself as conservative; as a senator she voted with President Trump's stated position about 80% of the time, opposed abortion, supported repeal of the Affordable Care Act and opposed assault-weapons bans.
people.description: Kelly Loeffler is an American businesswoman and Republican politician who has served as Administrator of the Small Business Administration since February 2025. She was appointed U.S. Senator from Georgia in 2020 and served until January 2021, and previously was chief executive of Bakkt.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kelly Loeffler, official portrait (2025).jpg

people.name: Kristi Noem
people.description: Kristi Noem served as the 8th United States Secretary of Homeland Security from January 25, 2025 until March 24, 2026, when Markwayne Mullin was sworn in as her successor. She previously served as Governor of South Dakota (2019-2025) and as South Dakota's at-large U.S. Representative (2011-2019), and became Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas in March 2026.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official Portrait of Secretary Kristi Noem.jpg (DHS photo by Tia Dufour)

people.name: Lee Zeldin
people.office: Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
people.politics: Republican who voted largely along party lines in Congress; opposes abortion and has called for repeal of New York's bail reform.
people.religion: Jewish (raised in Conservative and Reform Judaism; member of B'nai Israel Reform Temple in Oakdale, New York)
people.description: Lee Zeldin is an American politician and lawyer who has served as the 17th Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency since January 29, 2025. He previously served in the New York State Senate (2011-2014) and the U.S. House of Representatives for New York's 1st district (2015-2023), and was the Republican nominee for Governor of New York in 2022.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Lee-Zeldin-EPA-Official-Portrait.jpg

people.name: Linda McMahon
people.politics: Supports school choice and charter schools and has said the Department of Education is not needed.
people.religion: Roman Catholic (raised in a Baptist family; converted to Roman Catholicism)
people.description: Linda McMahon is the 13th United States Secretary of Education, in office since March 3, 2025, following a 51-45 Senate confirmation vote. She previously served as Administrator of the Small Business Administration (2017-2019) and co-founded and led World Wrestling Entertainment.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:ED_Sec_Linda_McMahon_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Lloyd Austin
people.politics: Retired four-star U.S. Army general who served as Secretary of Defense; listed as an independent with no party affiliation.
people.description: Lloyd Austin served as the 28th United States Secretary of Defense from January 2021 to January 2025 and was the first African American to hold the post. A retired four-star Army general, he previously commanded U.S. Central Command from 2013 to 2016.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin, official portrait, 2023.jpg
people.educationNote: B.S., United States Military Academy (1975); M.A. in counselor education, Auburn University (1986); M.B.A., Webster University (1989)

people.name: Lori Chavez-DeRemer
people.description: Lori Chavez-DeRemer served as the 30th United States Secretary of Labor from March 11, 2025, after a 67-32 Senate confirmation, until she resigned on April 20, 2026. Deputy Secretary Keith Sonderling became acting secretary; before joining the Cabinet she represented Oregon's 5th congressional district (2023-2025) and was mayor of Happy Valley, Oregon.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer official portrait 2025 (54382448706).jpg (U.S. Department of Labor)

people.name: Marco Rubio
people.politics: Republican described as conservative, with a record of hawkish positions on China and a focus on Latin America policy.
people.description: Marco Rubio is the 72nd United States Secretary of State, sworn in on January 21, 2025, and has also served as National Security Advisor since May 1, 2025. He was a U.S. Senator from Florida from 2011 to 2025 and Speaker of the Florida House of Representatives from 2006 to 2008.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official portrait of Secretary Marco Rubio (cropped)(2).jpg

people.name: Markwayne Mullin
people.politics: Supports President Trump's immigration policies and a border wall, backs expanded domestic oil and gas production, and opposed federal student loan forgiveness.
people.description: Markwayne Mullin is the 9th United States Secretary of Homeland Security, sworn in on March 24, 2026 after a 54-45 Senate confirmation vote on March 23. He previously served as U.S. Senator from Oklahoma (2023-2026) and as U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 2nd congressional district (2013-2023).
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:DHS_Secretary_Markwayne_Mullin_Official_Portrait_(55166865268).jpg
people.educationNote: Associate in Applied Science in plumbing, Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology (2010)

people.name: Merrick Garland
people.politics: Former federal appellate judge nominated to the Supreme Court by President Obama in 2016 and later served as Attorney General under President Biden.
people.description: Merrick Garland served as the 86th United States Attorney General from March 2021 to January 2025 under President Joe Biden. He was a judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit from 1997 to 2021 and returned to the law firm Arnold & Porter in May 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Attorney General Merrick Garland.jpg

people.name: Mike Pompeo
people.description: Mike Pompeo is an American Republican politician who served as the 70th U.S. Secretary of State from April 2018 to January 2021. He previously directed the Central Intelligence Agency (2017-2018) and represented Kansas's 4th congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives (2011-2017).
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Mike_Pompeo_official_photo_(cropped)(2).jpg

people.name: Mike Waltz
people.office: United States Ambassador to the United Nations
people.politics: Described in his Wikipedia biography as a China hawk who endorsed Donald Trump for the 2024 presidential race.
people.description: Mike Waltz is the U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations, confirmed by the Senate 47-43 on September 19, 2025 and sworn in the next day. He previously served as National Security Advisor from January 20 to May 1, 2025 and as U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th congressional district from 2019 to 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official Portrait of UN Ambassador Mike Waltz (cropped 1).jpg

people.name: Pam Bondi
people.office: Former Attorney General of the United States
people.description: Pam Bondi served as the 87th United States Attorney General from February 5, 2025, after her Senate confirmation and swearing-in, until President Trump removed her on April 2, 2026. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche became acting attorney general and was later confirmed as her successor.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Pam Bondi official portrait (cropped)(2).jpg (U.S. Department of Justice)
people.educationNote: B.A. in criminal justice, University of Florida (1987); J.D., Stetson University College of Law (1990)

people.name: Pete Buttigieg
people.politics: Former mayor of South Bend, Indiana, and 2020 presidential candidate who served as Secretary of Transportation under President Biden.
people.description: Pete Buttigieg served as the 19th United States Secretary of Transportation from February 2021 to January 2025 under President Joe Biden. He was mayor of South Bend, Indiana, from 2012 to 2020 and a candidate for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Pete Buttigieg, Secretary of Transportation.jpg

people.name: Pete Hegseth
people.office: Secretary of War (statutory title: Secretary of Defense)
people.politics: Republican whose views are described as strongly conservative, with a focus on military culture and veterans' policy.
people.religion: Christian; family attends Pilgrim Hill Reformed Fellowship (Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches)
people.description: Pete Hegseth is the United States Secretary of Defense, sworn in on January 25, 2025, who also uses the title Secretary of War under Executive Order 14347 of September 5, 2025. He previously co-hosted Fox & Friends Weekend on Fox News from 2017 to 2024 and served in the U.S. Army and Army National Guard.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Pete Hegseth Official Portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in politics, Princeton University (2003); Master of Public Policy, Harvard Kennedy School (2013)

people.name: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
people.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
people.politics: Independent since 2023 (previously Democratic); chairs the President's Make America Healthy Again Commission created by Executive Order 14212.
people.health: Disclosed in a 2012 deposition (reported by The New York Times in May 2024) that doctors in 2010 attributed a brain abnormality to a parasite, and that he was diagnosed with mercury poisoning; his campaign confirmed the parasite and said the issue was resolved more than 10 years earlier.
people.description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is an American lawyer, environmental advocate and author who has served as United States Secretary of Health and Human Services since February 13, 2025. He previously worked as a senior attorney at Riverkeeper and was president of the Waterkeeper Alliance.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.,_official_portrait_(2025)_(cropped_3-4)_(b).jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in American history and literature, Harvard (1976); J.D., University of Virginia School of Law (1982); LL.M., Pace University (1987)

people.name: Russell Vought
people.office: Director of the Office of Management and Budget
people.politics: Fiscal conservative; a primary architect of the Heritage Foundation's Project 2025 and a self-described Christian nationalist.
people.religion: Baptist (a deacon of a Baptist church)
people.description: Russell Vought is an American political advisor who has served as Director of the Office of Management and Budget since February 2025, having previously held the post from 2020 to 2021. He has also served as acting director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and as acting administrator of USAID, and led the Heritage Foundation's Project 2025 transition project.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Russell_Vought,_official_portrait_(2025)_(cropped1).jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in history and political science, Wheaton College; J.D., George Washington University Law School (2004)

people.name: Scott Bessent
people.politics: Republican who supports a strong-dollar policy, tariffs, lower interest rates and cryptocurrency regulation, and opposes a U.S. central bank digital currency.
people.description: Scott Bessent is the 79th United States Secretary of the Treasury, sworn in on January 28, 2025, and served as acting Commissioner of Internal Revenue from August 8, 2025 to March 6, 2026. Before taking office he was chief investment officer at Soros Fund Management and founded the hedge fund Key Square Group.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official portrait of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.jpg

people.name: Scott Turner
people.office: Secretary of Housing and Urban Development
people.politics: Republican who told the Senate Banking Committee on January 16, 2025 that the U.S. needs millions more homes of all kinds and pledged to continue and expand first-term Opportunity Zones policies.
people.religion: Baptist (associate pastor, Prestonwood Baptist Church, Plano, Texas)
people.description: Scott Turner is an American politician and former NFL cornerback who has served as the 19th U.S. Secretary of Housing and Urban Development since February 5, 2025. He represented Texas House District 33 from 2013 to 2017 and was Executive Director of the White House Opportunity and Revitalization Council from 2019 to 2021.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Scott_Turner,_official_portrait_(2025).jpg

people.name: Sean Duffy
people.politics: Republican who, as a U.S. Representative (2011-2019), proposed a five-member oversight panel for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and sponsored the Puerto Rico debt-oversight law PROMESA.
people.description: Sean Duffy is an American politician and former television personality who has served as U.S. Secretary of Transportation since January 28, 2025. A Republican, he represented Wisconsin's 7th congressional district in the U.S. House from 2011 to 2019 and served as acting NASA Administrator from July 9 to December 18, 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Secretary_of_Transportation_Sean_Duffy_Official_Portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in marketing, Saint Mary's University of Minnesota (1994); J.D., William Mitchell College of Law (1999)

people.name: Steven Mnuchin
people.description: Steven Mnuchin is an American financier who served as the 77th U.S. Secretary of the Treasury from February 2017 to January 2021 in President Donald Trump's first administration. After leaving office he founded the private equity firm Liberty Strategic Capital.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Steven_Mnuchin_official_photo.jpg

people.name: Susie Wiles
people.health: Disclosed an early-stage breast cancer diagnosis in March 2026; on 2026-09-16 she wrote that after a Mayo Clinic appointment her pathology results came back clear and that she is cancer free.
people.description: Susie Wiles is the White House Chief of Staff, serving since January 20, 2025, and the first woman to hold the position. She was a co-chair of Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and earlier worked in Florida politics, including as chief of staff to Jacksonville Mayor John Delaney.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Susie Wiles 2025 (edited crop).jpg

people.name: Todd Blanche
people.politics: Registered Republican since 2024 (previously a registered Democrat); served as President Trump's defense attorney in criminal cases brought in 2023 and 2024.
people.description: Todd Blanche is the Attorney General of the United States, sworn in on August 10, 2026 after a 50-49 Senate confirmation vote on August 8; he had served as Acting Attorney General from April 2, 2026 and as Deputy Attorney General from March 6, 2025. Before that he was an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the Southern District of New York and a defense attorney whose clients included Donald Trump.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:AG_Todd_Blanche_Official_Portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: Bachelor's, American University (1996); law degree, Brooklyn Law School (2003)

people.name: Tulsi Gabbard
people.religion: Hindu (Vaishnava tradition); has said she grew up with Hindu values
people.description: Tulsi Gabbard served as the 8th Director of National Intelligence from February 12, 2025, resigning in May 2026 with her last day moved up from June 30 to June 19, 2026. She previously represented Hawaii's 2nd congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives from 2013 to 2021.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Director Tulsi Gabbard Official Portrait.jpg (Office of the Director of National Intelligence)

people.description: William Barr is an American lawyer who served as the 77th U.S. Attorney General from 1991 to 1993 and again as the 85th Attorney General from February 2019 to December 2020. people.name: Nancy Pelosi
people.office: United States Representative from California's 11th congressional district
people.politics: A Democrat, Pelosi led the House Democratic Caucus for about two decades (2003-2023) and is widely considered a liberal; she was a founding member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and left it in 2003 after becoming Minority Leader. Her office describes her priorities as health care, climate and energy, equal pay, LGBTQ equality and voting rights.
people.health: On December 14, 2024, spokesperson Ian Krager stated that Pelosi had undergone a successful hip replacement at a U.S. military hospital in Germany after being injured and hospitalized during a congressional delegation trip to Luxembourg, and was recovering well.
people.description: Nancy Pelosi (born Nancy Patricia D'Alesandro, March 26, 1940, in Baltimore, Maryland) is an American politician who has represented San Francisco in the U.S. House of Representatives since a June 1987 special election as a Democrat. She was House Democratic Whip from 2002, Democratic leader from 2003 to 2023, and Speaker of the House from 2007 to 2011 and from 2019 to 2023, the first woman to hold the office. She represented California's 5th (1987-1993), 8th (1993-2013), 12th (2013-2023) and 11th (2023-present) districts. In November 2022 she stepped aside from Democratic leadership and was named Speaker Emerita. On November 6, 2025 she announced she would not seek reelection in 2026.

people.name: Abigail Spanberger
people.politics: Her first executive orders, signed January 17, 2026, addressed cost savings, healthcare costs and housing supply, and rescinded the prior administration's Executive Order 47.
people.description: Abigail Spanberger is an American politician and former CIA operations officer who became Governor of Virginia on January 17, 2026. She previously represented Virginia's 7th congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives from 2019 to 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Rep. Abigail Spanberger - 118th Congress.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A., University of Virginia (2001); M.B.A. (joint program of GISMA Business School and Purdue Krannert School of Management)

people.name: Andy Beshear
people.politics: Democrat who vetoed HB 3, a 15-week abortion ban, in April 2022 and chairs the Democratic Governors Association in 2026.
people.description: Andy Beshear is a Democrat who has been Governor of Kentucky since December 10, 2019. He previously served as Kentucky Attorney General from January 2016 to December 2019.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Andy_Beshear_in_April_2026_(cropped_2).jpg
people.educationNote: B.A., Vanderbilt University (2000); J.D., University of Virginia School of Law (2003)

people.name: Bill Lee
people.politics: Described himself as a social conservative when he announced his 2018 campaign for governor.
people.description: Bill Lee is the 50th governor of Tennessee, serving since January 19, 2019. A Republican, he was president and chief executive officer of the family-owned Lee Company from 1992 to 2016 before entering politics.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Hob Nob on the State Line with Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, Bristol (cropped).2.jpg

people.name: Bob Ferguson
people.politics: His first-day executive orders, signed January 15, 2025, addressed access to reproductive health care, a review of housing-related regulations, and permitting reform.
people.description: Bob Ferguson is an American attorney and politician who became Governor of Washington on January 15, 2025. He previously served as Washington's attorney general from 2013 to 2025 and on the King County Council from 2004 to 2013.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Bob Ferguson at his 2023 Shrimp Feed 02 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Brad Little
people.politics: His 2018 campaign called for a phased-in $350 million reduction in the state income tax and elimination of the Idaho grocery tax.
people.description: Brad Little is a Republican who has served as the 33rd governor of Idaho since January 7, 2019. He previously served as Idaho's lieutenant governor from 2009 to 2019 and as a state senator from 2001 to 2009.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Brad Little official photo.jpg

people.name: Brian Kemp
people.politics: Has been called "staunchly" conservative for signing strict anti-abortion laws, expanding gun rights and changing election rules.
people.description: Brian Kemp is a Republican who has served as the 83rd governor of Georgia since January 14, 2019. He was Georgia's secretary of state from 2010 to 2018 and a state senator from 2003 to 2007, after operating businesses in agriculture, financial services and real estate.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Brian Kemp portrait, 2024 (cropped).jpg (Governor's Photographer, Office of Governor Brian P. Kemp, public domain)

people.name: Dan McKee
people.politics: Supports gun control and has said he would support an assault weapons ban.
people.description: Dan McKee is the 76th governor of Rhode Island, a Democrat who assumed office on March 2, 2021, after Gina Raimondo resigned to become U.S. Secretary of Commerce. He lost renomination to Helena Foulkes in the September 2026 Democratic primary and remains in office for the rest of his term.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:RI_Governor_Daniel_McKee.jpg

people.name: Gavin Newsom
people.politics: Democratic governor whose administration has focused on infrastructure, housing, climate, gun control and LGBTQ rights, and who imposed a moratorium on executions in 2019.
people.health: He has publicly said he was diagnosed as dyslexic as a child.
people.description: Gavin Newsom, a member of the Democratic Party, has served as the 40th governor of California since January 7, 2019, and was reelected in 2022. He previously served as lieutenant governor from 2011 to 2019 and as mayor of San Francisco from 2004 to 2011.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor of California Gavin Newsom (cropped 3x4).jpg

people.name: Greg Abbott
people.politics: Has promoted a strongly conservative agenda as governor, including maintaining Texas's abortion ban, loosening gun laws, and increasing law enforcement funding.
people.health: Paralyzed by a falling tree while jogging shortly after law school, as stated in his official governor biography.
people.description: Greg Abbott is the 48th governor of Texas, serving since January 20, 2015. A Republican, he previously served as Texas attorney general from 2002 to 2015 and as a justice of the Texas Supreme Court from 1996 to 2001.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Greg Abbott at NASA 2024 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Greg Gianforte
people.politics: Republican who signed 2021 bills on constitutional carry, a sanctuary-city ban, abortion restrictions and limits on transgender athletes in girls' school sports.
people.religion: Christian (nondenominational); attends Grace Bible Church in Bozeman, raised Presbyterian
people.description: Greg Gianforte is a Republican who has served as the 25th Governor of Montana since January 4, 2021, and was re-elected in 2024. He previously represented Montana's at-large district in the U.S. House from 2017 to 2021 and has chaired the Republican Governors Association since November 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Greg_Gianforte_in_2025_(cropped).jpg (Gage Skidmore, CC BY-SA 4.0)

people.name: Gretchen Whitmer
people.politics: Democrat who signed the 2023 repeal of Michigan's 1931 abortion ban and of the state's 2012 right-to-work law.
people.description: Gretchen Whitmer is an American lawyer and Democratic politician who has served as governor of Michigan since January 2019. She previously served in the Michigan House of Representatives and Senate and as Ingham County prosecutor.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:8R4A9872_(53367444225)_(Whitmer1).jpg

people.name: Henry McMaster
people.politics: An early supporter of Donald Trump's 2016 campaign, he gave a nominating speech for Trump at the 2016 Republican National Convention.
people.description: Henry McMaster is the governor of South Carolina, a Republican who took office on January 24, 2017, when Nikki Haley resigned to become U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, and who was elected in 2018 and 2022. He previously served as U.S. Attorney for South Carolina, state attorney general and lieutenant governor, and became the state's longest-serving governor in January 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Henry_McMaster_in_2026_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Janet Mills
people.politics: Democrat who signed an executive order implementing Medicaid expansion in Maine on her first week in office (Executive Order 1, January 3, 2019).
people.description: Janet Mills is a Democrat who has been Governor of Maine since January 2, 2019. She previously served as Maine Attorney General in two stints (2009-2011 and 2013-2019) and in the Maine House of Representatives from 2002 to 2009.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Maine_congressional_delegation_meets_with_Gov_Janet_Mills_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Jared Polis
people.politics: Described as both progressive and libertarian-leaning; he has called himself a libertarian while supporting abortion rights, school choice and cannabis legalization.
people.description: Jared Polis is a Democrat who has served as the 43rd governor of Colorado since January 8, 2019, and represented Colorado's 2nd congressional district in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2019. Before entering politics he co-founded the greeting-card site bluemountain.com, founded the online florist ProFlowers and was among the founders of Techstars.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Jared Polis official photo.jpg (US House Office of Photography, public domain)

people.name: JB Pritzker
people.politics: A progressive Democrat who has signed laws legalizing adult-use cannabis, raising the state minimum wage to $15 an hour and expanding abortion access.
people.health: In a September 21, 2026 CBS interview he said he has taken a GLP-1 medication for about two years after his doctor diagnosed him with diabetes, and that he has lost about 80 pounds.
people.description: JB Pritzker is a Democrat who has served as the 43rd governor of Illinois since January 14, 2019, and was reelected in 2022. Before taking office he chaired the Illinois Human Rights Commission from 2003 to 2006.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:JB Pritzker 2026 (less cropped).jpg

people.name: Jeff Landry
people.politics: Republican who signed a 2024 law requiring display of the Ten Commandments in Louisiana public school classrooms (HB 71).
people.description: Jeff Landry is a Republican who has been Governor of Louisiana since January 8, 2024. He previously served as a U.S. Representative from 2011 to 2013 and as Louisiana Attorney General from 2016 to 2024.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Jeff_Landry_2025.jpg

people.name: Jim Pillen
people.politics: Republican who campaigned against abortion and critical race theory in the 2022 governor's race.
people.description: Jim Pillen is a Republican who has served as the 41st Governor of Nebraska since January 5, 2023. A veterinarian and chair of Pillen Family Farms, he served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents before taking office.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor_Pillen_of_Nebraska.jpg (Maj. Scott Ingalsbe, Nebraska National Guard, public domain)

people.name: Joe Lombardo
people.politics: Describes himself as a "moderate Republican"; in 2023 he signed abortion-protection and transgender-rights bills and vetoed a bill strengthening protections for providers of gender-affirming care.
people.description: Joe Lombardo is a Republican who has served as Governor of Nevada since January 2, 2023. He was Sheriff of Clark County from 2015 to 2023 after a 26-year career with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:CES_2026_-_Joe_Lombardo_06(cropped).jpg (Xuthoria, CC BY-SA 4.0)

people.name: Josh Green
people.politics: In his December 2022 inaugural address he pledged to address Hawaii's rising cost of living through affordable housing initiatives and tax reforms.
people.description: Josh Green is a physician and Democrat who has served as the ninth governor of Hawaii since December 5, 2022. He previously served as lieutenant governor from 2018 to 2022 and in the Hawaii Senate and House of Representatives.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Josh Green Official Photo 2022 (cropped) 1cropped).jpg

people.name: Josh Shapiro
people.politics: Supports unions and has vowed to veto any "right to work" legislation.
people.description: Josh Shapiro is the 48th governor of Pennsylvania, a Democrat sworn in on January 17, 2023, after serving as state attorney general from 2017 to 2023. In January 2026 he announced that he would seek a second term.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Josh_Shapiro_2023_(3x4).jpg

people.name: Josh Stein
people.politics: Democrat who signed the 2026 state budget (SB 257) while stating objections to its cuts of more than 1,000 state government positions and to provisions that shift power away from the executive branch.
people.description: Josh Stein is the 76th governor of North Carolina, in office since January 1, 2025. A Democrat, he previously served as the state's attorney general from 2017 to 2025 and in the North Carolina Senate from 2009 to 2016.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Josh_Stein.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in history, Dartmouth College (1988); degrees from Harvard Law School (J.D.) and the Kennedy School of Government (M.P.P.)

people.name: Kathy Hochul
people.politics: Democrat who paused New York City congestion pricing in June 2024, then proposed a reduced-toll version in November 2024 that began charging on January 5, 2025.
people.health: Basal cell carcinoma on her nose, which she disclosed herself in September 2024; it was removed under local anesthesia.
people.description: Kathy Hochul is the governor of New York, in office since August 24, 2021, when she succeeded Andrew Cuomo after his resignation. A Democrat, she previously served as lieutenant governor from 2015 to 2021 and as a U.S. representative from 2011 to 2013.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kathy_Hochul_official_portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in political science, Syracuse University (1980); J.D., Catholic University of America Columbus School of Law (1984)

people.name: Katie Hobbs
people.politics: Democratic governor who set an Arizona record with 63 vetoes in her first legislative session and signed the 2024 repeal of the state's 1864 abortion ban.
people.description: Katie Hobbs, a member of the Democratic Party, has served as the 24th governor of Arizona since January 2, 2023, after narrowly defeating Kari Lake in the 2022 election. She previously served as Arizona Secretary of State from 2019 to 2023 and as a state legislator, including as Senate minority leader.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Katie Hobbs 2026.jpg
people.educationNote: Bachelor's in social work, Northern Arizona University (1992); master's in social work, Arizona State University (1995)

people.name: Kay Ivey
people.politics: Republican governor who signed the 2019 Alabama abortion ban (HB 314) and has opposed Medicaid expansion.
people.religion: Baptist (member of First Baptist Church of Montgomery)
people.health: In September 2019 she announced a diagnosis of early-stage lung cancer and said it was found early and was very treatable.
people.description: Kay Ivey, a member of the Republican Party, has served as the 54th governor of Alabama since April 10, 2017, when she succeeded Robert Bentley upon his resignation. She previously served as Alabama state treasurer from 2003 to 2011 and lieutenant governor from 2011 to 2017.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kay Ivey (2026).jpg

people.name: Kelly Armstrong
people.politics: Republican who signed a 2025 property-tax relief package (HB 1176) funded with Legacy Fund earnings, raising the primary-residence credit from $500 to $1,600.
people.description: Kelly Armstrong is the 34th governor of North Dakota, in office since December 15, 2024, when he succeeded Doug Burgum. A Republican, he previously represented North Dakota's at-large district in the U.S. House from 2019 to 2024.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kelly_Armstrong_(3x4_cropped)_(2).jpg

people.name: Kelly Ayotte
people.politics: Republican who called herself a "strong conservative" in the 2024 campaign; described as both conservative and centrist during her Senate term.
people.description: Kelly Ayotte is a Republican who has served as the 83rd Governor of New Hampshire since January 9, 2025. She previously served as New Hampshire Attorney General and as a U.S. Senator from 2011 to 2017.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:NH_Governor_Kelly_Ayotte_(December_11,_2025).jpg (Staff Sgt. David Marquis, public domain)
people.educationNote: B.A. in political science, Pennsylvania State University; J.D., Villanova University School of Law (1993)

people.name: Kevin Stitt
people.politics: Said when signing SB 612 in April 2022 that he wants Oklahoma to be "the most pro-life state in the country".
people.description: Kevin Stitt is the 28th governor of Oklahoma, a Republican who took office on January 14, 2019, after a business career as founder and chief executive of Gateway Mortgage. He chaired the National Governors Association from July 2025 to August 2026.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kevin_Stitt_(55103789989)_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Kim Reynolds
people.politics: Has signed private-school education savings accounts, permitless handgun carry and a six-week abortion limit into law, and has called for an amendment stating the Iowa constitution does not protect abortion rights.
people.description: Kim Reynolds is a Republican who has served as the 43rd governor of Iowa since May 24, 2017, after serving as lieutenant governor from 2011 to 2017. She announced on April 11, 2025 that she would not seek reelection in 2026.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kim Reynolds by Gage Skidmore 2.jpg
people.educationNote: Bachelor of Liberal Studies, Iowa State University (December 2016)

people.name: Larry Rhoden
people.politics: Described himself as a "conservative voice for limited government" in his 2014 U.S. Senate campaign.
people.description: Larry Rhoden is the 34th governor of South Dakota, serving since January 25, 2025, when he succeeded Kristi Noem after her resignation to become U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security. A Republican and rancher, he previously served in the South Dakota Legislature and as lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Larry Rhoden 2025 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Laura Kelly
people.politics: Democrat who has repeatedly proposed Medicaid expansion in Kansas; as of the cited article it had not passed.
people.description: Laura Kelly is a Democrat who has been Governor of Kansas since January 14, 2019. She previously represented the 18th district in the Kansas Senate from 2005 to 2019.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Laura_Kelly_official_photo.jpg

people.name: Mark Gordon
people.politics: The Wyoming Republican Party's central committee passed a no-confidence resolution against him on November 4, 2023, over his remarks about carbon-negative goals.
people.health: Tested positive for COVID-19 on November 25, 2020; his office said he had minor symptoms and would keep working remotely.
people.description: Mark Gordon is an American rancher and politician who has been Governor of Wyoming since January 7, 2019. He previously served as Wyoming State Treasurer from 2012 to 2019.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Wyoming Governor Mark Gordon expands partnership with Tunisia to enhance agriculture and civil protection (4) (cropped).jpg

people.name: Matt Meyer
people.politics: In 2025 he described himself as "a pretty progressive Democrat".
people.description: Matt Meyer is a Democrat who became the 76th governor of Delaware on January 21, 2025, succeeding John Carney. He previously served as New Castle County executive from 2017 to 2025 and worked as an attorney and as an economic adviser to Governor Jack Markell.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:(02-19-2025) Matt Meyer.jpg (Simone Sampson, Delaware National Guard, public domain)

people.name: Maura Healey
people.politics: Democrat who, as Massachusetts attorney general, joined multistate lawsuits against President Trump's 2017 immigration executive orders.
people.description: Maura Healey is an American lawyer and Democratic politician who has served as governor of Massachusetts since January 2023. She was Massachusetts Attorney General from 2015 to 2023.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Maura_Healey,_official_portrait,_governor.jpg

people.name: Michelle Lujan Grisham
people.politics: Democrat who has argued her party should focus on voters' everyday concerns and avoid 'purity tests'; term-limited, with her final year in office in 2026.
people.description: Michelle Lujan Grisham is the governor of New Mexico, in office since January 1, 2019. A Democrat, she represented New Mexico's 1st congressional district in the U.S. House from 2013 to 2019.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Michelle_Lujan_Grisham_2026.jpg

people.name: Mike Braun
people.politics: Ran for governor in 2024 on a "Freedom and Opportunity" platform promising to address rising property taxes, make healthcare more obtainable and affordable, and implement universal school choice.
people.description: Mike Braun is a Republican who has served as the 52nd governor of Indiana since January 13, 2025. He was a U.S. senator from Indiana from 2019 to 2025 and a member of the Indiana House of Representatives from 2014 to 2017.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor Mike Braun DHS.jpg

people.name: Mike DeWine
people.politics: Republican who said on June 16, 2026 that Ohio should abolish the death penalty, reversing his earlier support for it.
people.description: Mike DeWine is the 70th governor of Ohio, in office since January 14, 2019. A Republican, he previously served as Ohio attorney general from 2011 to 2019, a U.S. senator from 1995 to 2007 and lieutenant governor from 1991 to 1994.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Gov-Mike-DeWine.jpg

people.name: Mike Dunleavy
people.politics: Republican governor who has pushed for full statutory Permanent Fund Dividend payments and opposes state-funded elective abortions.
people.description: Mike Dunleavy, a member of the Republican Party, has served as the 12th governor of Alaska since December 3, 2018 and was reelected in 2022. He previously served in the Alaska State Senate from 2013 to 2018 and worked as a teacher, principal and school superintendent in northwest Alaska.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor Mike J. Dunleavy - Official Portrait.jpg

people.name: Mike Kehoe
people.politics: Republican who has advocated removing capital gains and income taxes from Missouri state revenue.
people.description: Mike Kehoe is an American Republican politician who has served as governor of Missouri since January 2025. He previously served in the Missouri Senate from 2011 to 2018 and as lieutenant governor from 2018 to 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Mike_Kehoe_2025_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Mikie Sherrill
people.politics: Democrat who has positioned herself as a moderate (New Democrat Coalition, formerly Blue Dog Coalition), emphasizing affordability, property tax relief and clean energy.
people.description: Mikie Sherrill is a Democrat who has served as the 57th Governor of New Jersey since January 20, 2026. A former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and federal prosecutor, she represented New Jersey's 11th congressional district from 2019 to 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Gov._Mikie_Sherrill_Official_Portrait.jpg (State of New Jersey, public domain)
people.educationNote: B.S., United States Naval Academy (1994); M.Sc. international and world history, London School of Economics (2003); J.D., Georgetown University Law Center (2007)

people.name: Ned Lamont
people.politics: Democrat who signed laws legalizing adult-use cannabis and sports betting and creating paid family and medical leave; his first two biennial budgets did not raise personal income tax rates.
people.description: Ned Lamont is a Democrat who has served as the 89th governor of Connecticut since January 9, 2019 and is seeking a third term in November 2026. Before becoming governor he founded the campus cable and satellite services company Campus Televideo and was the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in 2006.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor Ned Lamont of Connecticut, official portrait.jpg (Office of Governor Ned Lamont, CC BY-SA 4.0)
people.educationNote: Master of Business Administration; Bachelor of Arts

people.name: Nikki Haley
people.description: Nikki Haley served as the 116th Governor of South Carolina from 2011 to 2017 and then as U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations until December 31, 2018. She sought the 2024 Republican presidential nomination, withdrew in March 2024, and has since been the Walter P. Stern Chair at the Hudson Institute.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Nikki_Haley_official_photo.jpg

people.name: Patrick Morrisey
people.politics: On January 14, 2025 he signed executive orders allowing religious exemptions for school vaccines, ordering the cessation of DEI initiatives, and setting school choice as an administration priority.
people.description: Patrick Morrisey is an American attorney and politician who became Governor of West Virginia on January 13, 2025. He previously served as the state's attorney general from 2013 to 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Patrick Morrisey 2026 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Phil Scott
people.politics: Often described as a moderate Republican; pro-choice, and signed a 2019 bill protecting abortion rights.
people.description: Phil Scott is the 82nd governor of Vermont, serving since January 5, 2017. A Republican, he previously served in the Vermont Senate from 2001 to 2011 and as lieutenant governor from 2011 to 2017.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Phil Scott 2019.png

people.name: Ron DeSantis
people.politics: Has generally governed as a conservative; he was a founding member of the House Freedom Caucus in 2015.
people.description: Ron DeSantis is a Republican who has served as the 46th governor of Florida since January 8, 2019 and is not eligible to run for a third term in 2026. He represented Florida's 6th congressional district in the U.S. House from 2013 to 2018, served as a U.S. Navy judge advocate, and sought the 2024 Republican presidential nomination before withdrawing in January 2024.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Ron DeSantis official photo.jpg (Government of Florida, public domain)

people.name: Sarah Huckabee Sanders
people.politics: Republican governor whose signature policy is the 2023 LEARNS Act, which expanded school choice through Educational Freedom Accounts and raised starting teacher pay to $50,000.
people.health: In September 2022 she announced a thyroid cancer diagnosis and surgery to remove her thyroid and nearby lymph nodes; her statement said she was cancer-free afterward.
people.description: Sarah Huckabee Sanders, a member of the Republican Party, has served as governor of Arkansas since January 10, 2023, the first woman to hold the office. She was White House press secretary from July 2017 to July 2019 and is the daughter of former Arkansas governor Mike Huckabee.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders 2026.jpg

people.name: Spencer Cox
people.politics: Frequently described as a moderate Republican; describes himself as pro-life.
people.religion: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
people.description: Spencer Cox is the 18th governor of Utah, serving since January 4, 2021. A Republican, he previously served as lieutenant governor from 2013 to 2021 and chaired the National Governors Association from 2023 to 2024.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Spencer Cox - 54856206905 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Tate Reeves
people.politics: Republican who has advocated eliminating the Mississippi state income tax.
people.religion: United Methodist (attends Galloway Memorial United Methodist Church)
people.description: Tate Reeves is an American Republican politician who has served as governor of Mississippi since January 2020. He previously served as state treasurer from 2004 to 2012 and lieutenant governor from 2012 to 2020.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Gov._Tate_Reeves_Signs_House_Bill_1486_(cropped)_(2).jpg

people.name: Tim Walz
people.politics: DFL governor who was the Democratic nominee for vice president in 2024 and signed the 2023 Protect Reproductive Options Act and cannabis legalization.
people.description: Tim Walz is an American politician of the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party who has served as governor of Minnesota since January 2019. He represented Minnesota's 1st congressional district in the U.S. House from 2007 to 2019 and was the Democratic vice-presidential nominee in 2024.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Governor_Tim_Walz_2026.jpg
people.educationNote: Bachelor of Science; Master of Science

people.name: Tina Kotek
people.politics: Has made housing production and homelessness a top priority, setting a statewide goal of 36,000 new housing units a year.
people.religion: Lapsed Catholic; attends an Episcopal church
people.description: Tina Kotek is the governor of Oregon, a Democrat sworn in on January 9, 2023, after serving in the Oregon House of Representatives from 2007 to 2022, including nine years as Speaker. She won the May 2026 Democratic primary for governor and is seeking a second term.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Tina_Kotek_official_portrait_2021(3x4_cropped).jpg
people.educationNote: B.S. in religious studies, University of Oregon (1990); master's degree in international studies and comparative religion, University of Washington

people.name: Tony Evers
people.politics: Has used the veto more frequently than any governor in Wisconsin history and announced in July 2025 that he would not seek reelection in 2026.
people.description: Tony Evers is an American educator and politician who has been Governor of Wisconsin since January 7, 2019. He previously served as Wisconsin's State Superintendent of Public Instruction from 2009 to 2019.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Tony Evers - 2022 (a).jpg
people.educationNote: Doctor of Philosophy; Bachelor of Science; Master of Science

people.name: Wes Moore
people.politics: Democrat who signed HB 932 (2025), requiring future Maryland governors to place assets in a blind trust or sign a non-participation agreement.
people.description: Wes Moore is a Democrat who has been Governor of Maryland since January 18, 2023. Before taking office he served in the U.S. Army and was chief executive of the Robin Hood Foundation from 2017 to 2021.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Wes_Moore_Official_Governor_Portrait.jpg
people.educationNote: Associate degree, Valley Forge Military College (1998); B.A. international relations and economics, Johns Hopkins University (2001); master's in international relations, Wolfson College, Oxford (2004, Rhodes Scholar)

people.name: Karoline Leavitt
people.description: Karoline Leavitt served as the 36th White House Press Secretary from January 20, 2025 until her last day on August 27, 2026, the youngest person to hold the role. She was national press secretary for the 2024 Trump campaign and was the Republican nominee for New Hampshire's 1st congressional district in 2022.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Official portrait of Karoline Leavitt, 2025 (cropped)(2).jpg (White House Office of the Press Secretary)

people.name: Bernard Arnault
people.office: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of LVMH
people.description: Bernard Arnault has been chairman and chief executive of LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton since 1989 and also chairs Christian Dior SE. LVMH shareholders raised the age limit for the chairman and chief executive to 85 in April 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Bernard Arnault (3) - 2017 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Bill Gates
people.office: Chair of the Gates Foundation; co-founder of Microsoft
people.description: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft in 1975 and is sole chair of the Gates Foundation, which has said it will spend down and close by 31 December 2045. He also founded Breakthrough Energy and chairs Cascade Investment and TerraPower.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Bill_Gates_at_the_European_Commission_-_P067383-987995_(cropped)_5.jpg

people.name: Elon Musk
people.office: Chief Executive of Tesla and SpaceX
people.description: Elon Musk is chief executive of Tesla and chief executive, chief technical officer and chairman of SpaceX, which acquired his AI company xAI in February 2026. Born in Pretoria, South Africa, he previously co-founded Zip2 and X.com and was Senior Advisor to the President for the Department of Government Efficiency from 20 January to 30 May 2025.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Elon_Musk_-_54820081119_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Jeff Bezos
people.office: Founder and Executive Chair of Amazon; founder of Blue Origin; co-CEO of Project Prometheus
people.description: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in 1994 and has been its executive chair since July 2021, after serving as chief executive since 1996. He also founded the spaceflight company Blue Origin, owns The Washington Post and, per media reports in November 2025, became co-CEO of the AI start-up Project Prometheus.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:260202-D-PM193-2205_SECWAR_Arsenal_of_Freedom_Tour_-_Florida_(3x4_cropped_on_Bezos_and_rotated).jpg

people.name: Jensen Huang
people.office: Founder, President and Chief Executive Officer of NVIDIA
people.description: Jensen Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and has served as its president and chief executive officer and a member of its board since the company began. NVIDIA is a designer of graphics processors and accelerated-computing platforms.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Jen-Hsun Huang 2025.jpg

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.office: Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive of Meta Platforms
people.religion: Raised Jewish; has said he believes religion is very important
people.description: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is founder, chairman and chief executive of Meta Platforms, which he controls through its voting shares. He is also co-founder of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative with Priscilla Chan.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:P20260929DT-1655_(55561811540)_(cropped_2).jpg

people.name: Sam Altman
people.description: Sam Altman is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been chief executive of OpenAI since 2019 and was president of Y Combinator from 2014 to 2019. He co-founded OpenAI in 2015 and the location-sharing startup Loopt, and has said he holds no equity in OpenAI.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Meeting_with_Masayoshi_Son_and_Sam_Altman_(February_3,_2025)_(3x4_cropped_on_Altman).jpg

people.name: Satya Nadella
people.office: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft
people.description: Satya Nadella became chief executive of Microsoft in February 2014 and added the role of chairman of the board in 2021. Microsoft lists him as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer in its fiscal 2026 annual report.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:MS-Exec-Nadella-Satya-2017-08-31-22 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Sundar Pichai
people.office: Chief Executive Officer of Alphabet and Google
people.description: Sundar Pichai joined Google in 2004, became chief executive of Google in 2015 and chief executive of its parent company Alphabet in December 2019. He also serves on Alphabet's board of directors.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Sundar Pichai - 2023 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Tim Cook
people.office: Executive Chair of Apple (Chief Executive Officer 2011-2026)
people.description: Tim Cook succeeded Steve Jobs as chief executive of Apple in August 2011 and became executive chair of its board on 1 September 2026, when John Ternus took over as chief executive. As executive chair he engages with policymakers worldwide and helps with selected company matters.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Tim Cook in New York City - 2026 (cropped).jpg

people.name: Warren Buffett
people.office: Chairman Emeritus and director of Berkshire Hathaway
people.health: Disclosed in April 2012 that he had been diagnosed with stage I prostate cancer, which he described as not life-threatening; he completed a course of radiation treatment in September 2012.
people.description: Warren Buffett led Berkshire Hathaway as chairman from 1970 and chief executive until Greg Abel succeeded him on 1 January 2026. On 18 September 2026 he became Chairman Emeritus and remains a director, with his son Howard G. Buffett elected chairman.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Warren_Buffett_at_the_2015_SelectUSA_Investment_Summit_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Adele
people.description: Adele Laurie Blue Adkins, known mononomously as Adele, is an English singer and songwriter. Regarded as a British cultural icon, she is known for her mezzo-soprano vocals and sentimental songwriting.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Adele_2016.jpg
people.educationNote: Graduated from the BRIT School for Performing Arts & Technology, Croydon (2006); no degree stated

people.name: Bad Bunny
people.description: Bad Bunny (Benito Antonio Martinez Ocasio) is a Puerto Rican rapper, singer and record producer who helped bring Spanish-language rap to a mainstream global audience. Forbes ranked him No. 10 among the world's highest-paid musicians of 2025 and he headlined the Super Bowl LX halftime show in February 2026.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Bad_Bunny_2019_by_Glenn_Francis_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Beyoncé
people.description: American singer, songwriter, actress and businesswoman who rose to prominence with Destiny's Child and holds a record 35 Grammy Awards. Forbes estimated her 2025 pre-tax earnings at $148 million and counted her as a billionaire.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Beyoncé - Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - 1st June 2023 (10 of 118) (52946364598) (best crop).jpg

people.name: Dwayne Johnson
people.office: Actor, producer and former professional wrestler
people.description: American actor and former professional wrestler, known as The Rock, whose films have grossed over $11.4 billion. Forbes estimated his 2024 earnings at $88 million after fees, the most of any actor that year.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Dwayne Johnson-1764 (4x5 cropped with moderate headroom).jpg

people.name: Ed Sheeran
people.description: Ed Sheeran is an English singer-songwriter born in Halifax, West Yorkshire, and raised in Framlingham, Suffolk. His Mathematics Tour grossed an estimated $875.7 million between 2022 and 2025, according to Forbes.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Ed_Sheeran_2022_(3x4_crop).jpg

people.name: Leonardo DiCaprio
people.description: Leonardo DiCaprio is an American actor and film producer who won the Academy Award for Best Actor for The Revenant. Forbes put his 2025 earnings at about $25 million after representation fees.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:LeoPTABFI191125-28_(cropped).jpg

people.name: Meryl Streep
people.description: Mary Louise "Meryl" Streep is an American actress. Widely regarded by peers and critics as the greatest actress of her generation, and by many with the affectionate epitaph "Greatest of All Time", she is recognized as one of the most versatile performers in cinema, noted for her technical precision, nuanced emotional depth, command of dialects, and professional longevity.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Meryl_Streep-_Press_conference_for_the_film_"The_Devil_Wears_Prada_2"_-_55194765350_(cropped1).jpg
people.educationNote: A.B. in drama, cum laude, Vassar College (1971); M.F.A. in drama, Yale School of Drama (1975)

people.name: Rihanna
people.description: Rihanna is a Barbadian singer, songwriter, businesswoman and actress, estimated to have sold more than 250 million records. Her wealth derives mainly from her co-ownership of the Fenty Beauty brand with LVMH and a stake in Savage X Fenty; Forbes listed her net worth at about $1 billion on 10 October 2026.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Rihanna_Fenty_2018.png

people.name: Steven Spielberg
people.description: Steven Allan Spielberg is an American filmmaker. A major figure of the New Hollywood era and pioneer of the modern blockbuster, Spielberg is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential filmmakers in the history of cinema and is the highest-grossing film director of all time, with his films having earned almost $11 billion worldwide.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:MKr25402_Steven_Spielberg_(Berlinale_2023)_(3x4_cropped).jpg

people.name: Taylor Swift
people.description: American singer-songwriter known for autobiographical songwriting; her Eras Tour (2023-2024) grossed an estimated $2.077 billion across 149 shows. Forbes estimated her 2025 pre-tax earnings at $202 million and her net worth at about $2 billion.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Taylor Swift at the 2023 MTV Video Music Awards (3).png

people.name: Tom Hanks
people.health: Has type 2 diabetes, which he disclosed on the Late Show with David Letterman in October 2013.
people.description: American actor and filmmaker who won consecutive Academy Awards for Best Actor for Philadelphia and Forrest Gump. He voices Woody in the Toy Story films, including Toy Story 5 (2026).
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:TomHanksPrincEdw031223 (11 of 41) (cropped).jpg

people.name: Zendaya
people.description: Zendaya is an American actress and singer known for the HBO series Euphoria, for which she won two Primetime Emmy Awards, and for starring roles in the Spider-Man and Dune film series. Time named her one of the world's 100 most influential people in 2022.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Zendaya-byPhilipRomano.jpg

people.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
people.office: Professional footballer, forward and captain of Al-Nassr and Portugal
people.description: Portuguese forward who is an active player and captains both Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr and the Portugal national team; in an August 2026 Vogue interview he said the 2026-27 season will probably be his last. He holds the men's international records for appearances (234) and goals (146) and appeared on Forbes' 2026 billionaires list with a $1.2 billion net worth.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Cristiano Ronaldo 2018.jpg

people.name: LeBron James
people.description: American forward who joined the Philadelphia 76ers in July 2026 after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers and is entering his 24th NBA season. He is the NBA's all-time leading scorer, a four-time NBA champion and four-time Finals MVP.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:LeBron James (51959977144) (cropped).jpg

people.name: Lewis Hamilton
people.description: Sir Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula 1 driver and seven-time world champion who drives car number 44 for Scuderia Ferrari. On 14 June 2026 he won the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, his first win for Ferrari, and Formula1.com listed him third in the 2026 drivers' standings with 221 points as of 10 October 2026.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Prime Minister Keir Starmer meets Sir Lewis Hamilton (54566928382) (cropped).jpg

people.name: Lionel Messi
people.office: Professional footballer, forward and captain of Inter Miami CF
people.description: Argentine forward who plays for and captains Inter Miami CF in Major League Soccer, where he signed a contract extension through 2028 in October 2025. He won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina and holds a record eight Ballons d'Or.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Lionel Messi 20180626.jpg

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.description: Michael Jeffrey Jordan, also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman, former professional basketball player, and former baseball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Michael_jordan_admad_rashad_(51276390562)_(cropped).jpg
people.educationNote: B.A. in geography, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1986)

people.name: Novak Djokovic
people.description: Novak Djokovic is a Serbian professional tennis player who holds the men's record of 24 Grand Slam singles titles and 428 weeks ranked world No. 1. He is still active on the ATP Tour in 2026, where the ATP profile lists 102 career singles titles and Forbes ranked him sixth among the highest-paid tennis players.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Novak Djokovic Paris 2024 Olympic Games (cropped).jpg

people.name: Patrick Mahomes
people.health: In the Chiefs game against the Los Angeles Chargers on 14 December 2025 he tore the ACL and LCL in his left knee; he had surgery on 15 December 2025 in Dallas, and the Chiefs' vice president of sports medicine put the expected recovery at about nine months.
people.description: Patrick Mahomes is an American football quarterback for the Kansas City Chiefs of the NFL and a three-time Super Bowl champion and Super Bowl MVP. After tearing his ACL and LCL in December 2025 he returned for the 2026 season, with the Chiefs roster page listing 4 games played and 4 starts through Week 4.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons, File:Patrick Mahomes (51615475056).jpg

people.name: Serena Williams
people.office: Former world No. 1 professional tennis player (retired 2022; limited return in 2026)

people.name: Peter Wolff
people.office: Dermatology nurse practitioner; writer and investor
people.description:
Peter Wolff is a dermatology nurse practitioner, business owner, writer and investor. SummitMD Dermatology’s staff biography verifies his master’s degree in nursing from South University and national board certification as a nurse practitioner. His clinical career has specialized in dermatology.

In his July 2024 introduction, Wolff described overseeing clinics in California, Nevada and Arizona as director of advanced practice providers. He explained that his professional corporation primarily earned revenue from dermatology and that he also maintained a business brokerage account. He began publishing on Substack to develop his thinking about medicine, history, finance and other subjects. His Autopilot portfolios span technology, healthcare, digital assets and diversified allocations; their client capital is separate from his personal income.

people.name: InTheMoney
people.office: Investor, options trader and financial educator publishing as InTheMoney
people.description:
InTheMoney is the public identity of Adam, an investor, options trader and financial educator. His own channel and membership descriptions focus on explaining stocks and equity options, and he publishes tutorials and commentary for retail audiences. A verified surname, degree history and exact birth date are not supplied by the sources used here.

His Autopilot lineup separates actively managed equity exposure, defensive allocations, inverse-market strategies and sentiment-based models. These products have different risks and methods; they are not one uniform personal portfolio. His creator disclosure explains that Autopilot compensates him for publishing strategies. No personal annual earnings amount is inferred from subscriptions or client capital.

people.description:
Michael Sikand is a business-media entrepreneur and investor. He began interviewing executives and startup founders while a University of Michigan student, building Our Future first as a podcast and then as a short-form business-news brand. Its videos distributed business stories to younger audiences on social platforms.

He received Forbes 30 Under 30 recognition in media, and Our Future was acquired by Morning Brew in 2023. His later work includes investment research, video interviews, newsletters and thematic public-equity portfolios on Autopilot. The profiles below distinguish his media-company milestones from the start of each investment strategy’s return record.

people.name: Daniel Koss
people.description:
Daniel Koss is an entrepreneur and investor focused on public companies supplying AI infrastructure. His Autopilot biography identifies him as founder of Edelbridge Capital and describes a background in competitive gaming and business building. His public investing thesis emphasizes the physical compute, power and infrastructure required by increasingly intensive AI systems.

In July 2026 he announced that his Substack was becoming Edelbridge Alpha, a collaborative project with Alasdair Mann and Babyfolio. The post explicitly distinguished the newly shared model portfolio from each contributor’s personal holdings. His Autopilot AI Infrastructure strategy is separately documented with its own return-record start date.

He later worked in hedge-fund research at Coatue, a Tiger-related firm and Citadel.

He founded Covey in March 2020 to create a community for testing investment ideas and identifying investors.
