Randy Harris is the creator of Dual Momentum Systems, a personal research project in tactical asset allocation. His own biography describes a background in finance, accounting and financial reporting, with some IT work, at businesses of different sizes. He says his interest in Gary Antonacci’s Global Equities Momentum research helped shape the project.

DMS publishes portfolio rules, backtests, live records and allocation tools. Its strategies use momentum and defensive rotations, with leverage in selected variants. Harris also publishes portfolios on Autopilot. A long simulated history is distinguished from the later live return record, and neither is treated as personal income.
people.photoCredit: Randy Harris / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: The Rabbit Hole
people.description:
The Rabbit Hole is a pseudonymous public commentator and Autopilot portfolio creator. The creator’s own biography says the account began on X as a way to test ideas and participate in public discussion, later expanding into published investment portfolios.

The portfolio themes include data-intensive technology, American companies and businesses associated with PayPal alumni. Those themes describe investment selection, rather than the creator’s own biography or an endorsement by the executives referenced. The profile preserves the published alias and does not infer a private identity.
people.photoCredit: The Rabbit Hole / Autopilot; public creator avatar

people.name: Ronnie Shah
people.office: Quantitative investor, researcher and finance educator
people.description:
Ronnie Shah is a quantitative investment researcher, portfolio manager and finance educator. His professional conference biography documents degrees in economics and systems engineering at the University of Pennsylvania, an MSc at the London School of Economics, and graduate finance degrees including a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin.

His career includes portfolio management at BlackRock, research at Dimensional Fund Advisors and Gerstein Fisher, and quantitative-equity leadership at Deutsche Bank and FORT. The AICPA biography identifies him as an M2M Capital co-founder and data/analytics strategist, as well as an adjunct finance teacher at UT Austin. On Autopilot he publishes a generative-AI earnings strategy.
people.photoCredit: Ronnie Shah / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image
people.educationNote: PhD and MA in finance, University of Texas at Austin; MSc in finance/economics, LSE; BS economics and BAS systems engineering, University of Pennsylvania.

people.name: Gannon Breslin
people.description:
Gannon Breslin is an investor and financial-newsletter creator. In a published interview he described beginning to trade during his last year of high school and developing a longer-term investment approach while attending the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy. His early public writing included the Rebel Markets newsletter.

His later creator biography emphasizes technology and growth businesses, including companies he says he began following years before launching his Autopilot strategy. He publishes Gannon’s AI Fund and financial-market education. Attendance at a service academy is not used here to infer an unverified degree, military rank or exact graduation date.
people.photoCredit: Gannon Breslin / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Prima Lux
people.description:
Prima Lux is the public identity of an investor whose Autopilot biography describes experience in commodity analysis and AI strategy. The account publishes the HARD Assets Fund, focusing on AI infrastructure, rare earths, defense and industrial businesses.

The disclosed approach favors larger established companies within each theme, with selective smaller-company positions. No real-world identity, former employer, degree institution or personal financial record is established. Corporate registries listing similarly named entities are not evidence that those companies operate this account.
people.photoCredit: Prima Lux / Autopilot; public creator avatar

people.name: Tom Heberle
people.office: Fundamental investor; former transportation and logistics professional
people.description:
Tom Heberle is an investor whose public biography describes more than thirty years in markets and a prior career in transportation and logistics. He reports moving to full-time investing in 2022.

His stated process draws on filings, fund letters and analyst research, with an emphasis on capital preservation, valuation and potential business inflections. He has a particular interest in energy, commodities and shipping. The public record supports that professional description and his Autopilot strategy, but does not establish a university degree, exact birth date or personal financial disclosures.
people.photoCredit: Tom Heberle / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Garth Friesen
people.office: Investor, financial author and former III Capital CEO/co-CIO
people.description:
Garth Friesen is an investor and financial author whose career began in interest-rate markets. He started at Merrill Lynch in London in 1994, moved to UBS’s proprietary-trading group, and joined III Capital Management in 1998. His trading covered rates, mortgages, credit and related derivatives.

He helped establish III’s credit business in 2005, became co-chief investment officer after later fund launches, and served as CEO from 2017 before returning to portfolio management in 2019. He also served on the New York Fed’s Investor Advisory Committee on Financial Markets. His later work includes writing for financial publications and the book Bite the Ass Off a Bear.
people.photoCredit: Garth Friesen / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image
people.educationNote: MBA, Ivey Business School, University of Western Ontario; verified by his professional biography.

people.name: Glenn Turner
people.office: Investor and founder of Glenn Turner Investments
people.description:
Glenn Turner is an investor and founder of Glenn Turner Investments. His creator biography describes nearly a decade of portfolio management, participation in Marketocracy, investment-community writing and appearances on CNNfn. These statements are published by the creator and are not treated as independently audited investment returns.

His current Autopilot strategy, the Armatura Fund, focuses on identifying where investment capital is moving before an associated theme becomes widely recognized. Searches also return other professionals named Glenn Turner; their legal histories, executive appointments and qualifications are not attributed to this profile.
people.photoCredit: Glenn Turner / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Gregory Scott
people.description:
Gregory Scott is the creator of the Phoenix Fund on Autopilot. His public biography describes about twenty-five years of trading and investing, and study toward a finance degree at an unnamed university. The source does not provide the institution, qualification title or completion date.

His published process combines long-term chart analysis, company fundamentals, position-risk management and technology themes. He describes an objective of growth alongside capital preservation. This is a statement of investment process and goals, rather than an independently verified performance award or guarantee.
people.photoCredit: Gregory Scott / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Derek Kahn
people.description:
Derek Kahn is an entrepreneur and founder of MindHyv. His public creator biography describes operating work across a software platform, construction services and a health-company partnership, with responsibilities in strategy, financial analysis, deal review and operations.

He says that experience shapes an operator-focused approach to public companies: assessing business drivers, financial statements and risks, then documenting decisions and reasons for passing on investments. He publishes the 1 Hour Work Week strategy on Autopilot. The sources do not name all of the businesses, his degree history or personal earnings.
people.photoCredit: Derek Kahn / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Tristan Thompson
people.description:
Tristan Trevor James Thompson is a Canadian-American basketball player, entrepreneur and investor. Born in Brampton, Ontario, he played at several high schools before spending the 2010–2011 season at the University of Texas. Cleveland selected him fourth overall in the 2011 NBA draft.

A rebounder and frontcourt player, Thompson was a member of the Cavaliers’ 2016 championship team and later played for Boston, Sacramento, Indiana, Chicago and the Los Angeles Lakers before returning to Cleveland. He also represented Canada internationally. His public charitable work includes the Amari Thompson Fund supporting people affected by epilepsy. His Autopilot portfolio is a separate investment project, not a basketball salary disclosure.
people.photoCredit: Tristan Thompson / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Jay Patel
people.office: Physician and White Coat Wealth creator
people.description:
Jay Patel is a practicing physician who publishes the White Coat Wealth portfolio on Autopilot under the name Dr. Jay Patel. His public biography frames investing around the limited time available to busy professionals.

His stated approach favors broad-market index funds, low expenses, long holding periods and controlled rebalancing. It avoids presenting frequent trading as a necessary part of investing. The source does not identify his medical specialty, medical school, clinic or licensing jurisdiction, so those details cannot safely be taken from the many other doctors with the same name.
people.photoCredit: Dr. Jay Patel / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Jordan Evans
people.description:
Jordan Evans is an investor and creator of Jev’s Flagship on Autopilot. His public biography describes playing Division I basketball and preparing for overseas professional opportunities before the COVID-19 pandemic changed his plans. He says he subsequently concentrated on investing.

His process combines trend confirmation, scheduled earnings risk, unusual options activity and dealer positioning data. He focuses on growth-related industries including technology, semiconductors and infrastructure. The biography does not name his college team, qualification or overseas club, so those details remain unverified.
people.photoCredit: Jordan Evans / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Harold Tan
people.office: Technology entrepreneur; Santiago Canyon College instructor; investor
people.description:
Harold Tan is an entrepreneur, educator and investor working across Bitcoin, renewable energy and technology. His professional biography identifies him as a co-founder of GigaWatt, a solar-energy business, an instructor at Santiago Canyon College and a consultant in web strategy.

He earned a UCLA bachelor’s degree in cognitive science and mathematics with computing in 2004 and a Harvard ALM in information systems in 2010. His public speaking includes a TEDx presentation about money and Bitcoin. On Autopilot he publishes strategies focused on AI infrastructure bottlenecks and government spending. The academic and professional credentials below are sourced separately from portfolio marketing.
people.photoCredit: Prof. Harold Tan / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image
people.educationNote: ALM in information systems, Harvard University, 2010; BS in cognitive science and mathematics with computing, UCLA, 2004.

people.name: Ross Pomerantz
people.office: Corporate Bro creator; entrepreneur, comedian and investor
people.description:
Ross Pomerantz is an entrepreneur, comedian and investor known as Corporate Bro. His work draws on experience in enterprise technology sales at companies including Oracle and Glassdoor. He earned an MBA at Stanford before moving into full-time media creation.

As Corporate Bro, he writes and performs sketches about sales and office life, creates material for corporate clients and speaks at company events. His work also includes startup advising and investment activity through Corp Capital. The Autopilot portfolio bearing his brand focuses on AI-related public companies; it is distinct from his entertainment work and private startup investments.
people.photoCredit: Ross Pomerantz / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image
people.educationNote: MBA, Stanford University; documented in the published Corporate Bro profile.

people.name: Colin Kolano
people.description:
Colin Kolano is an investor and creator of Agentic AI Backbone on Autopilot. His public thesis concerns a transition from AI systems answering questions to agents carrying out coding, analysis and other workflows.

The published portfolio methodology evaluates companies across silicon, infrastructure, power and security, using AI agents to score a defined stock universe against news, filings and market updates. The approach and its live return-record start are documented separately below. His prior employment, education and exact birth date are not established by the connected sources.
people.photoCredit: Colin Kolano / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Patrick Figueroa
people.description:
Patrick Figueroa is an investor publishing the Set It and Forget It Growth Fund on Autopilot. His stated approach combines broad growth themes with positions in companies supplying AI, semiconductors, cloud systems, data-center power, cybersecurity and defense.

He describes long-term ownership, periodic rebalancing and business fundamentals as central to the strategy. Despite the portfolio’s name, the published process involves active security selection and review. The available biography does not establish a complete employment or education history, exact birth date or personal annual income.
people.photoCredit: Patrick Figueroa / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Ryan Schilhab
people.office: Engineer and Cliff Radar Capital creator
people.description:
Ryan Schilhab is an engineer and investor publishing on Autopilot as Ryan Schilhab, P.E. His biography describes developing Cliff Radar Capital with a CPA partner and using a shared, rules-based system for their own investing before offering it publicly.

The Tactical Radar Foundation strategy uses a macroeconomic engine and allocation models to vary market exposure. Its source describes eight risk bands and a broader stack of complementary portfolios. A professional-engineering credential is self-reported on the profile; it should not be confused with a namesake CPA or used to infer a degree institution.
people.photoCredit: Ryan Schilhab, P.E. / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Jordan Grayson
people.office: Outpoint Capital founder; investor and startup adviser
people.description:
Jordan Grayson is an investor and founder of Outpoint Capital. His public professional profile lists a University of Pennsylvania bachelor’s degree in 1999 and earlier experience at firms including Credit Suisse First Boston, DLJ and Alson Capital. A contemporaneous SEC-hosted shareholder presentation identifies Outpoint as a long/short equity fund founded by him in 2005.

His published investment approach focuses on research, business change and catalysts that could close a gap between market price and assessed value. His later work includes startup advising and an Autopilot strategy following biotechnology-fund disclosures. This history is separate from the generic promotional claim of a guaranteed investment edge.
people.photoCredit: Jordan Grayson / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image
people.educationNote: BS, University of Pennsylvania, 1999; his public professional profile lists finance and computer science.

people.name: Jeffrey M. Welch
people.office: Researcher, educator and quantitative portfolio creator
people.description:
Jeffrey M. Welch is a researcher, educator and technologist whose public biography describes a doctorate focused on data-driven outcomes and more than twenty years of personal portfolio management. The source does not name the institution or exact doctoral field.

He applies research methods, backtesting and market-regime models to a strategy using sentiment from the All-In podcast alongside quantitative signals. The published model switches among seven portfolio structures according to market conditions. His use of the podcast as data does not imply that the hosts manage or endorse the strategy.
people.photoCredit: Jeffrey M. Welch / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image
people.educationNote: Doctorate, as reported in the creator’s public biography; institution and field not specified.

people.name: Zack Fincher
people.description:
Zack Fincher is an investor whose public biography describes former brokerage and trade-desk work at E*TRADE and Morgan Stanley. He says he also worked in brokerage operations and developed his investing approach through more than a decade of experience.

His Cruise Control retirement strategy combines global equities, Treasuries and a small allocation to gold. It is intended for long holding periods and is described for tax-advantaged accounts. These published strategy details are distinct from a verified retirement-planning credential or a current broker registration.
people.photoCredit: Zack Fincher / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Jay Plourde
people.description:
Jay Plourde is a financial-services executive, investor and adviser. His professional biographies describe leadership across institutional equities and broker-dealer businesses, including service as CEO of CLSA Americas. His published Autopilot biography also describes work with private companies, technology startups and intellectual-property businesses.

Rothswell Asset Management’s American Legacy Fund page identifies him as its fund manager and chief investment officer while explicitly describing the fund as being structured and not open for investment. His public Autopilot strategy focuses on companies positioned around AI-related industrial demand. The sources do not establish a completed degree or exact birth date.
people.photoCredit: Jay Plourde / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Jim Cramer
people.office: CNBC broadcaster, author and former hedge-fund manager
people.description:
James Joseph Cramer is an American broadcaster, author and former hedge-fund manager. He graduated from Harvard College in 1977 and Harvard Law School in 1984. After work in journalism and at Goldman Sachs, he founded his own investment firm in 1987.

Cramer co-founded TheStreet in 1996 and shifted toward a public career in financial commentary. He became the host of CNBC’s Mad Money in 2005 and a co-host of Squawk on the Street. His books address personal investing and his experience in markets. Autopilot’s Inverse Cramer strategy takes positions contrary to selected public recommendations; Cramer does not operate that portfolio.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Cramer

people.name: Jim Simons
people.office: Mathematician; founder of Renaissance Technologies; co-founder of the Simons Foundation
people.description:
James Harris Simons (1938–2024) was a mathematician, quantitative investor and philanthropist. He earned a mathematics degree at MIT and a doctorate at UC Berkeley, worked in codebreaking and academic mathematics, and chaired Stony Brook’s mathematics department from 1968 to 1978. His research with Shiing-Shen Chern produced the Chern–Simons theory used in mathematics and physics.

He left academia to establish Monometrics in 1978, renamed Renaissance Technologies in 1982. Renaissance developed investment strategies based on mathematical models; its Medallion Fund began in 1988. Simons retired as chief executive in 2010. With Marilyn Simons, he co-founded the Simons Foundation in 1994 and supported scientific research and mathematics education. He died on May 10, 2024. Autopilot’s namesake tracker follows the firm’s public filings rather than trades personally made by Simons.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Simons
people.educationNote: PhD in mathematics, University of California, Berkeley, 1961; undergraduate mathematics degree, MIT, 1958

people.name: Michael Burry
people.office: Investor; founder of Scion Capital and Scion Asset Management
people.description:
Michael James Burry is an American investor and physician known for his contrarian, research-intensive investing. He studied economics and pre-med at UCLA, earned an MD at Vanderbilt in 1997, and began medical training before moving into investment management. He founded Scion Capital in 2000 and became known for examining individual mortgage loans and betting against subprime mortgage securities before the financial crisis.

After closing Scion Capital in 2008, he returned to outside investment management through Scion Asset Management in 2013. He announced another closure in November 2025 and launched Cassandra Unchained on Substack. His career was described in Michael Lewis’s The Big Short and portrayed by Christian Bale in the 2015 film. Autopilot’s Burry Tracker follows his public commentary; it is a separate product rather than his own fund.
people.photoCredit: Tony Avelar / Bloomberg; Michael Burry
people.educationNote: MD, Vanderbilt University School of Medicine, 1997 (professional medical degree)

people.name: Ken Griffin
people.office: Founder, CEO and co-chief investment officer of Citadel
people.description:
Kenneth Cordele Griffin is an American investor and founder of Citadel and Citadel Securities. He began investing while at Harvard, where he graduated in 1989 with a BA in economics. After working with investor Frank Meyer in Chicago, he founded Citadel in 1990. Citadel operates investment-management strategies, while Citadel Securities is a separate market-making business founded in 2002.

Griffin has served as Citadel’s chief executive and co-chief investment officer. His public philanthropy includes education, economic opportunity and health sciences. Fund assets, company valuations, his personal earnings and his estimated net worth are separate measures. Autopilot’s Citadel Tracker follows the investment firm’s reported holdings; it is not operated by Griffin.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Griffin
people.educationNote: AB with honors in economics, Harvard College, 1989

people.name: Leopold Aschenbrenner
people.office: AI researcher; founder of Situational Awareness LP
people.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner is a German-born AI researcher and investor. He graduated from Columbia College in 2021 as valedictorian and later worked on AI safety and superalignment research at OpenAI. He co-authored research on weak-to-strong generalization before his departure from the company in 2024.

In June 2024 he published Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead, an essay series discussing AI progress, infrastructure and security. He subsequently founded Situational Awareness LP, an investment firm focused on AI-related opportunities. Public reporting in 2026 also describes major losses at the firm; its investment thesis should not be presented as a proven financial forecast. His exact birth date is not established by the sources used here.
people.photoCredit: Leopold Aschenbrenner / Autopilot tracker image

people.name: Steven A. Cohen
people.office: Founder of Point72 Asset Management; owner of the New York Mets
people.description:
Steven A. Cohen is an American investor, founder of S.A.C. Capital Advisors and Point72 Asset Management, and owner of the New York Mets. He earned an economics degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 1978 and began his career trading at Gruntal & Co. He established S.A.C. in 1992.

Point72 began in 2014 as a family office and later returned to managing outside capital. In 2016, the SEC settled a personal failure-to-supervise proceeding with Cohen and temporarily barred him from supervising outside money. That settlement must be distinguished from the separate criminal case against S.A.C. entities. Cohen acquired the Mets in 2020. His baseball ownership, investment career and regulatory record are separately sourced below.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Cohen_(businessman)
people.educationNote: BS in economics, University of Pennsylvania.

people.name: Jason Calacanis
people.office: Entrepreneur, angel investor and podcast host
people.description:
Jason McCabe Calacanis is an entrepreneur, angel investor, author and podcast host. A Fordham graduate, he built media businesses before becoming an early-stage technology investor. He co-founded Weblogs, Inc. with Brian Alvey; AOL acquired the company in 2005. He later developed the Mahalo search and education business.

His subsequent work includes the LAUNCH investment ecosystem, This Week in Startups and the All-In podcast. He wrote Angel, a book about early-stage technology investing, published in 2017. Autopilot’s Calacanis Tracker draws from published trading information and should be distinguished from his private startup investments.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Calacanis

people.name: Ray Dalio
people.description:
Ray Dalio is an American investor and author who founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975. He studied finance at C.W. Post, later part of Long Island University, and earned an MBA at Harvard Business School. He built Bridgewater from a small advisory business into a global institutional investment manager. Its major strategies included Pure Alpha and All Weather.

Dalio’s investment work emphasizes economic cycles, diversification and systematic decision-making. He also wrote Principles: Life & Work and books about debt cycles and changes in world power. Bridgewater documents his staged withdrawal from its CEO, CIO and chairman roles. His later work centers on writing, mentoring and philanthropy; he is not presented here as the current manager of Autopilot’s Dalio Tracker.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Dalio

people.name: Bill Ackman
people.office: Founder and CEO of Pershing Square
people.description:
William Albert Ackman is an American investor and founder of Pershing Square, known for concentrated portfolios and activist investments. He earned a BA at Harvard College in 1988 and an MBA at Harvard Business School in 1992. He co-founded Gotham Partners before establishing Pershing Square, whose official biography dates its founding to 2003; accounts of the capital-management fund’s launch often use 2004.

Ackman’s career has included public campaigns involving companies such as MBIA, Herbalife and Canadian Pacific, alongside major losses and gains in individual investments. His current corporate biography lists leadership at Pershing Square and Howard Hughes Holdings. He founded the Pershing Square Foundation in 2006. The Autopilot Ackman Tracker is a separate strategy based on public disclosures.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Ackman

people.name: Peter Thiel
people.office: Entrepreneur; co-founder of PayPal, Palantir and Founders Fund
people.description:
Peter Andreas Thiel is an entrepreneur and investor who co-founded PayPal, Palantir Technologies and Founders Fund. He studied philosophy at Stanford and earned a JD from Stanford Law School. After early legal and financial work, he helped build PayPal and led it as chief executive before its 2002 sale to eBay.

Thiel made an early outside investment in Facebook, co-founded Palantir and became a partner at Founders Fund. His public work also includes the Thiel Fellowship, the Thiel Foundation and the book Zero to One, written with Blake Masters. His investment firms, philanthropic initiatives and political activity are distinct parts of his career.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Thiel

people.name: Dave Portnoy
people.office: Founder and owner of Barstool Sports
people.description:
David Scott Portnoy is an American entrepreneur and media personality who founded Barstool Sports. He graduated from the University of Michigan in 1999 with a degree in education and initially worked in Boston before launching Barstool as a sports and betting publication. The business later developed into a digital media and podcast company.

Barstool went through ownership changes involving the Chernin Group and Penn Entertainment. Penn acquired full control in 2023, then sold the business back to Portnoy later that year. His public projects include One Bite pizza reviews, the Barstool Fund and the Davey Day Trader investing broadcasts. The Autopilot tracker follows public investing commentary, rather than constituting his own investment fund.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Portnoy
people.educationNote: Degree in education, University of Michigan, 1999.

people.name: David Tepper
people.office: Founder of Appaloosa Management; Carolina Panthers and Charlotte FC owner
people.description:
David Alan Tepper is an American investor, founder of Appaloosa Management and owner of the Carolina Panthers and Charlotte FC. Raised in Pittsburgh, he graduated from the University of Pittsburgh in 1978 and completed an MBA at Carnegie Mellon in 1982. He worked at Republic Steel before joining Goldman Sachs in 1985, where he became a senior high-yield trader.

He established Appaloosa in 1993 with a focus on distressed and other investment opportunities. He purchased the Panthers in 2018 after years as a minority Pittsburgh Steelers owner. His philanthropy includes university support, poverty relief and disaster response. An honorary doctorate is distinguished from his earned MBA.
people.photoCredit: Wikimedia Commons; portrait linked from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tepper
people.educationNote: BA in economics, University of Pittsburgh; MBA, Carnegie Mellon University.

people.name: Joseph Edelman
people.description:
Joseph Edelman is an American investor and founder of Perceptive Advisors, a firm focused on healthcare and biotechnology. He graduated from UC San Diego with a psychology degree in 1978, later earned an MBA at New York University, and moved from scientific interests into financial analysis.

After working as a biotechnology analyst and in investment management, he founded Perceptive Advisors in 1999. The firm built its strategy around evaluating scientific research, drug development and changes in biotechnology businesses. His later activities include philanthropy through the Edelman Family Foundation. The Autopilot Biotech All-Star Tracker uses public filings from Perceptive and Baker Brothers; Edelman does not thereby manage that tracker.
people.photoCredit: Joseph Edelman / Perceptive Advisors
people.educationNote: BS in psychology, University of California, San Diego; MBA, New York University.

people.name: Julian Baker
people.office: Co-founder of Baker Bros. Advisors; Madrigal chairman
people.description:
Julian C. Baker is an investor and co-founder of Baker Bros. Advisors, a biotechnology-focused investment adviser. He earned an AB at Harvard and worked in private equity at Credit Suisse First Boston from 1988 to 1993. He then managed investments at Tisch Financial Management from 1994 to 1999.

He co-founded Baker Bros. with his brother Felix in 2000. His corporate biography lists board work at several biotechnology companies and service as Madrigal’s chairman. His firm’s public filings are used in the independent Autopilot Biotech All-Star Tracker, alongside filings from Perceptive Advisors. A verified personal portrait and exact birth date remain unavailable in the reviewed sources.
people.educationNote: AB, Harvard University; Madrigal’s official director biography verifies the degree.

people.name: Felix Baker
people.office: Co-founder of Baker Bros. Advisors; biotechnology company director
people.description:
Felix J. Baker is a biotechnology investor and co-founder of Baker Bros. Advisors. Trained as a scientist at Stanford, he earned a bachelor’s degree in biology in 1991 and a doctorate in immunology in 1998; he also completed two years of medical school. He entered fund management in the 1990s and co-founded Baker Bros. with Julian Baker in 2000.

His work includes investment and board service across biotechnology companies, as well as university philanthropy and bioscience research support. Kodiak’s director biography documents his service there from 2015 and his committee responsibilities. The Biotech All-Star Tracker’s use of Baker Bros. filings does not mean that he personally manages or endorses it.
people.photoCredit: Felix J. Baker / Kodiak Sciences; director portrait
people.educationNote: BS in biology and PhD in immunology, Stanford University.

people.name: Alejandro Lopez-Lira
people.office: Assistant professor of finance, University of Florida; AI Finance Labs portfolio designer
people.description:
Alejandro Lopez-Lira is an assistant professor of finance at the University of Florida’s Warrington College of Business. His research studies asset pricing, machine learning and the use of language models in financial analysis. He earned finance graduate degrees at the University of Pennsylvania, completing his PhD in 2020.

With Yuehua Tang, he studied whether large language models could extract stock-return information from news headlines. He is also the author of The Predictive Edge, a book on generative AI and financial forecasting. On Autopilot, he designs portfolios published under Dr. Lira’s AI Finance Labs, including strategies using GPT and other language models. Model backtests, actual portfolio results and academic claims are separate types of evidence.
people.photoCredit: Dr. Lira's AI Finance Labs / Autopilot; creator-supplied image
people.educationNote: MA and PhD in finance, University of Pennsylvania, 2020; verified by the University of Florida faculty directory.

people.name: Travis Hoium
people.office: Investment analyst and founder of Asymmetric Investing
people.description:
Travis Hoium is an investment analyst, writer and founder of Asymmetric Investing. Before his financial-writing career he worked as a mechanical engineer at 3M and founded a virtual-reality company. He holds a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering and an MBA from the University of Minnesota.

His writing for The Motley Fool has covered renewable energy, technology and growth businesses. In March 2023 he launched Asymmetric Investing as a research publication focused on businesses with substantial long-term upside. His approach examines business models, disruption and valuation. The Autopilot portfolio is one public implementation of that research, rather than a guarantee of the targets in his newsletter.
people.photoCredit: Travis Hoium / The Motley Fool; author portrait
people.educationNote: Bachelor’s in mechanical engineering and MBA, University of Minnesota.

people.name: Adam Garcia
people.office: Founder and CEO of Elite Trade Club
people.description:
Adam Garcia is the founder and CEO of Elite Trade Club, a trading-research publication associated with Elite Trade Media. His public work focuses on stock-market research, technical setups and investor education. The publication identifies him through its author page.

Elite Trade Club’s Autopilot strategies include thematic approaches to technology infrastructure, energy-related market conditions and companies associated with Elon Musk. Those portfolios are published by the organization. They do not establish Garcia’s personal holdings, annual income or an investment-adviser qualification. No completed university degree or exact birth date was verified in the reviewed sources.
people.photoCredit: EliteTrade.Club / Autopilot; creator-supplied image

people.name: Gav Blaxberg
people.office: Founder and CEO of WOLF Financial
people.description:
Gav Blaxberg is the founder and CEO of WOLF Financial, a financial-media and marketing business. He studied finance at Drexel University and worked in private wealth management at Goldman Sachs and in private equity at Versa before developing a public finance-media career.

He built WOLF through live market discussions on X and later expanded into a creator network, company interviews and financial-brand campaigns. His work includes public speaking and live hosting at exchange and industry events. WOLF’s portfolio offerings on Autopilot are a separate part of that public business; network reach and client capital are not measures of his personal earnings.
people.photoCredit: Gav Blaxberg; official website portrait

people.name: Molly Cantillon
people.description:
Molly Cantillon is a technology entrepreneur and founder of NOX, a project building AI assistants and automated workflows. She studied computer science and mathematics at Stanford before leaving to build the company. Her Forbes profile describes previous work at LangChain and Replicate and early backing for NOX from OpenAI.

Her own site publishes software projects spanning AI assistance, satellite imagery, privacy-preserving polling and other experiments. She writes about using software agents to organize work and everyday tasks. Autopilot lists her as a portfolio creator, but the public source catalog does not expose a detailed strategy record for that listing. Stanford attendance is not represented as a completed degree.
people.photoCredit: Molly Cantillon / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

people.name: Antonio Marrazzo
people.description:
Antonio Marrazzo is a quantitative researcher and AI engineer who writes about systematic investment strategies. His public professional profile describes work at Lexfi developing financial-data tools and AI workflows, and quantitative research at Connective Capital Management. Earlier listed work includes Palmarium.ai, Accenture and statistics teaching at the University of Buenos Aires.

He publishes research on topics such as market regimes, volatility, liquidity and reactions to economic information. His profile also describes ongoing data-science study at Rice University and Fulbright involvement. Ongoing study is not recorded as a completed degree. Autopilot’s public landing page lists him as a creator, but its public strategy catalog does not expose details of his portfolio.
people.photoCredit: Antonio Marrazzo / Autopilot; creator-supplied profile image

contributions.title: Morrill Land-Grant Act of 1862
contributions.summary: Federal land grants funding state agricultural and mechanical colleges.
contributions.impactBasis: Ehrlich, Cook & Yin (Journal of Human Capital 2018): a difference-in-differences comparison with the UK finds the Morrill Act land-grant system produced sizeable educational and economic returns.

contributions.title: 44th President of the United States
contributions.summary: Held the office from January 20, 2009, to January 20, 2017, as the first African American president.

contributions.title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
contributions.summary: Health-insurance reform law signed on March 23, 2010; the defining domestic legislation of his presidency.
contributions.impactBasis: In the IGM Economic Experts Panel poll on the ACA's subsidies and Medicaid expansion, nearly 70% of panelists agreed that the health and well-being gains for the newly insured exceed the costs, while 52% said the subsidies would not reduce total health-care spending (most of the rest were uncertain).

contributions.title: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009
contributions.summary: Economic stimulus law providing supplemental appropriations for job creation, infrastructure, energy, unemployment assistance and state fiscal relief.
contributions.impactBasis: In the July 2014 IGM Economic Experts Panel poll, 67.5% of panelists agreed or strongly agreed that, counting the cost of raising taxes and future spending effects, the stimulus's benefits would exceed its costs (27.0% uncertain, 5.4% disagreed); 97.3% agreed unemployment was lower at the end of 2010 than without it.

contributions.title: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act
contributions.summary: Financial-regulation overhaul enacted after the 2008 financial crisis.
contributions.impactBasis: GAO's 42 bond-spread models found that in 2008-2009 all showed bank holding companies with $1 trillion in assets paid less for bond funding than those with $10 billion, but in 2011-2013 more than half showed the larger firms paying more; two of three rating agencies cut assumed government support, citing the Orderly Liquidation Authority, though GAO could not isolate the effect of government support.

contributions.title: Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act of 2009
contributions.summary: The first bill he signed into law; it changed the statute of limitations for equal-pay lawsuits.

contributions.title: Executive Order 13491, Ensuring Lawful Interrogations
contributions.summary: Signed two days after taking office; it governed the treatment of detainees in U.S. custody.

contributions.title: Nobel Peace Prize
contributions.summary: Awarded the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize; he delivered his acceptance speech at Oslo City Hall on December 10, 2009.

contributions.title: A Promised Land
contributions.summary: Presidential memoir published November 17, 2020, by Crown (U.S. and Canada) and Viking (other English-language markets); covers his life through May 2011. Earlier books: Dreams from My Father (1995) and The Audacity of Hope (2006).

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from Illinois
contributions.summary: Sworn in on January 3, 2005; resigned on November 16, 2008, to focus on the presidential transition.

contributions.title: McKinley Tariff Act
contributions.summary: Raised average import duties to about 50 percent; signed by President Harrison.
contributions.impactBasis: Irwin (J. Economic History 2000, NBER w6835) simulated the tinplate duties of the 1890 McKinley Tariff: the industry became established and flourished, but would have arisen about a decade later anyway, and protection does not pass a cost-benefit test. One industry, not a whole-economy verdict; the sign of the long-run effect is debated.

contributions.title: 42nd President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served two terms as president from January 20, 1993, to January 20, 2001.

contributions.title: Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993
contributions.summary: Guaranteed eligible employees up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave for family and medical reasons.

contributions.title: Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act
contributions.summary: Required federal background checks and a waiting period for handgun purchases from licensed dealers.

contributions.title: North American Free Trade Agreement Implementation Act
contributions.summary: Implemented the North American Free Trade Agreement among the United States, Canada and Mexico in U.S. law.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO (2003) estimated NAFTA raised U.S. exports to Mexico by 11.3% and imports by 7.7% by 2001, but concluded it increased annual U.S. GDP by only a few billion dollars, a few hundredths of a percent; the U.S. International Trade Commission estimated 0.1 to 0.5 percent.

contributions.title: Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act
contributions.summary: Omnibus crime law that funded additional police officers and prisons, created the federal assault weapons ban, and included the Violence Against Women Act.

contributions.title: Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act
contributions.summary: Welfare reform law that replaced Aid to Families with Dependent Children with Temporary Assistance for Needy Families block grants.
contributions.impactBasis: Blank's review in the Journal of Economic Literature found the 1990s welfare reforms changed economic behavior, with significant gains in work and earnings and lower poverty under the most promising 'new-style' programs; the work gains cannot be cleanly separated from the 1990s expansion and EITC increases.

contributions.title: Governor of Arkansas
contributions.summary: Served as the 40th and 42nd governor of Arkansas, from January 9, 1979, to January 19, 1981, and from January 11, 1983, to December 12, 1992.

contributions.title: My Life
contributions.summary: Autobiography published in 2004 by Alfred A. Knopf.

contributions.title: Citizen: My Life After the White House
contributions.summary: Second volume of memoirs, published in 2024, covering his post-presidency.

contributions.title: Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993
contributions.summary: Deficit-reduction law of tax increases and spending limits.
contributions.impactBasis: GAO (AIMD-94-79R) reports the Congressional Budget Office's estimate that the Act reduces the deficit by $433 billion over FY1994-98. An agency projection at enactment, not a measured outcome; its growth effects were contested and are not scored here.

contributions.title: Immigration Act of 1924 (Johnson-Reed)
contributions.summary: National-origins quotas that sharply cut immigration.
contributions.impactBasis: Abramitzky, Ager, Boustan, Cohen & Hansen (AEJ: Applied 2023): US-born workers in areas that lost immigrants because of the 1920s quota acts did not benefit relative to workers in less exposed areas, and mining shrank. Local labor markets only.

contributions.title: Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act
contributions.summary: Created merit-based federal hiring.
contributions.impactBasis: Aneja & Xu (AER 2024) find the staggered rollout cut Post Office delivery errors by about 20 percent and raised productivity, 1875-1905. A companion study of customs houses finds no cost-effectiveness gain, so the benefit is partial and agency-specific.

contributions.title: Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956
contributions.summary: Created the Interstate Highway System.
contributions.impactBasis: Fernald (AER 1999; Federal Reserve IFDP 592) finds the road build-out of the 1950s-60s gave a one-time boost to the level of productivity but no above-average return at the margin.

contributions.title: 43rd President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served two terms as president from January 20, 2001, to January 20, 2009.

contributions.title: Economic Growth and Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2001
contributions.summary: Across-the-board federal income tax cut law (the 2001 Bush tax cuts) that lowered individual rates and phased out the estate tax.
contributions.impactBasis: Gale and Potter (National Tax Journal, 2002) concluded the 2001 tax cut would reduce the size of the future economy, raise interest rates, make taxes more regressive and be fiscally unsustainable as written; other analysts emphasised its supply-side incentive effects, so the growth sign is disputed.

contributions.title: USA PATRIOT Act
contributions.summary: Expanded federal surveillance and law-enforcement powers after the September 11, 2001 attacks.

contributions.title: No Child Left Behind Act of 2001
contributions.summary: Reauthorized the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, adding annual standardized testing and accountability requirements for public schools.

contributions.title: United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003
contributions.summary: Authorized the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and global HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria funding; enacted in May 2003.
contributions.impactBasis: Bendavid et al. (JAMA 2012) found adult mortality odds 0.84 (95% CI 0.72-0.99) in PEPFAR focus countries versus non-focus African countries, with an estimated 740,800 deaths averted 2004-2008 (wide CI); a 3ie replication reproduced the result but found it borderline once covariates were added, and an earlier study found no significant effect.

contributions.title: Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act
contributions.summary: Created the Medicare Part D outpatient prescription drug benefit.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO (2014) found Part D spending in 2013 was roughly half of what it projected in 2003, with lower spending where more plan sponsors competed; the program is nonetheless an unfunded entitlement, and CBO estimated Medicaid net drug prices 27 to 38 percent below Part D's. Analysts dispute how much of the shortfall reflects competition rather than slower national drug spending.

contributions.title: Governor of Texas
contributions.summary: Served as governor of Texas from January 17, 1995, to December 21, 2000.

contributions.title: Decision Points
contributions.summary: Presidential memoir published November 9, 2010, by Crown Publishing Group.

contributions.title: 41: A Portrait of My Father
contributions.summary: Biography of his father, George H. W. Bush, published November 11, 2014, by Crown Publishers.

contributions.title: Portraits of Courage
contributions.summary: Book of his paintings of military veterans, published February 28, 2017, by Crown.

contributions.title: Funding Act of 1790
contributions.summary: Federal assumption and funding of Revolutionary War debt; chartered the Bank of the United States the next year.
contributions.impactBasis: Sylla (Founding Choices, NBER/University of Chicago Press 2011): after the 1790-92 funding, the national government left default and by 1793 collected enough revenue to fund operations and meet interest on the debt. An economic-history assessment of a program Hamilton designed and Washington signed.

contributions.title: Energy Policy and Conservation Act (CAFE standards)
contributions.summary: Created the Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards.
contributions.impactBasis: Greene, Greenwald & Ciez (Energy Policy 2020) find fuel savings exceeded the cost of improving fuel economy, 1975-2018. Attribution against gasoline prices and the safety trade-offs are debated.

contributions.title: Economic Cooperation Act of 1948 (Marshall Plan)
contributions.summary: About $13 billion of US aid to Western Europe, 1948-51.
contributions.impactBasis: De Long & Eichengreen (NBER 3899): the aid was too small to speed recovery directly, but its conditions pushed Europe toward markets and set the stage for rapid post-war growth. A historical assessment, not a counterfactual estimate, and economists disagree on the size of the effect.

contributions.title: Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act
contributions.summary: Raised US tariffs on about 20,000 imported goods.
contributions.impactBasis: Irwin (Review of Economics and Statistics 1998, NBER w5509) finds the tariff itself cut imports by 4-8 percent, more through deflation; Mitchener et al. (Economic Journal 2022) find 28-32% export losses to retaliating countries. Trade effects only; no net welfare estimate here.

contributions.title: 39th President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served one term as president from January 20, 1977, to January 20, 1981.

contributions.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2002
contributions.summary: Awarded the 2002 Nobel Peace Prize, unshared, for decades of efforts to find peaceful solutions to international conflicts, advance democracy and human rights, and promote economic and social development; the ceremony was held in Oslo on 2002-12-10.

contributions.title: Department of Energy Organization Act
contributions.summary: Created the Department of Energy as a Cabinet-level department, consolidating the Federal Energy Administration, the Energy Research and Development Administration, the Federal Power Commission and other energy programs.

contributions.title: Airline Deregulation Act
contributions.summary: Phased out federal control over airline fares, routes and market entry.
contributions.impactBasis: Morrison & Winston (Brookings, 1986) estimated the Airline Deregulation Act brought travelers about $6B a year in benefits and raised airline earnings by $2.5B a year, in the early post-1978 period. One policy, not a verdict on the whole record.

contributions.title: Department of Education Organization Act
contributions.summary: Established the Department of Education as a Cabinet department, separating education functions from the former Department of Health, Education, and Welfare (renamed Health and Human Services).

contributions.title: Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act
contributions.summary: Protected well over 100 million acres of Alaskan land as new national parks, refuges and other conservation units; signed after the 1980 election.

contributions.title: 76th Governor of Georgia
contributions.summary: Served one term as governor of Georgia from January 12, 1971, to January 14, 1975.

contributions.title: Keeping Faith: Memoirs of a President
contributions.summary: Presidential memoir published in 1982 covering the Iran hostage crisis, the Camp David talks and his relationships with world leaders.

contributions.title: Why Not the Best?
contributions.summary: Campaign autobiography published in 1975, his first book.

contributions.title: 46th President of the United States
contributions.summary: Held the office from January 20, 2021, to January 20, 2025.

contributions.title: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021
contributions.summary: Pandemic-relief reconciliation law enacted on March 11, 2021.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO and JCT estimated the American Rescue Plan Act as passed by the Senate would increase deficits by $1.844 trillion over 2021-2031 ($1.798 trillion in direct spending and a $46 billion revenue loss), before added interest costs on the debt.

contributions.title: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
contributions.summary: Bipartisan law authorizing federal-aid highways, highway safety, transit and other infrastructure programs.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO's August 2021 analysis of an illustrative $500 billion, 10-year increase in physical infrastructure spending (not specific to this law) found it would raise private-sector productivity; real GDP would average 0.04% higher over 2022-2051 if borrowing-financed, and the macroeconomic feedback would raise the net 30-year present-value cost of that spending by about one-fourth, versus cutting it by about one-third if offset by lower non-investment spending.

contributions.title: CHIPS and Science Act
contributions.summary: Semiconductor manufacturing and science-funding law, enacted on August 9, 2022 as a division of the vehicle bill H.R. 4346.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO's score of the CHIPS and Science Act estimates it would increase deficits by $79 billion over 2022-2032 (before later baseline updates), a small share of projected 10-year federal deficits; CBO's score does not value the policy's economic benefits.

contributions.title: Inflation Reduction Act of 2022
contributions.summary: Reconciliation law enacted on August 16, 2022, covering climate and energy investment, health-care provisions and tax changes.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO estimated the Inflation Reduction Act would reduce deficits by about $238 billion over 2022-2031 (about $738 billion in revenue and savings against $499 billion in spending and tax breaks), with $101 billion of net revenue from IRS enforcement funding that carries estimating uncertainty and tax-credit costs that depend on uptake.

contributions.title: Executive Order 13985, Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government
contributions.summary: Signed on his first day in office; revoked by President Trump on January 20, 2025.

contributions.title: Executive Order 14110, Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
contributions.summary: Signed on October 30, 2023; revoked by President Trump on January 20, 2025.

contributions.title: 47th Vice President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served under President Barack Obama from January 20, 2009, to January 20, 2017.

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from Delaware
contributions.summary: Served from January 5, 1973, to January 15, 2009.

contributions.title: Promise Me, Dad
contributions.summary: Memoir published November 14, 2017, by Flatiron Books.

contributions.title: Voting Rights Act of 1965
contributions.summary: Banned discriminatory voting practices and provided federal oversight of elections.
contributions.impactBasis: Cascio & Washington (QJE 2014, NBER w17776): after the Act, Black voter registration rose sharply in the South and state aid shifted toward localities with larger Black populations.

contributions.title: Wage and price controls (Executive Order 11615, Economic Stabilization)
contributions.summary: 90-day wage and price freeze, followed by phased controls through 1974.
contributions.impactBasis: Blinder & Newton (NBER 1981): the controls held prices 3-4% lower by early 1974, but catch-up after they were dismantled left only a 0-2% net gain and account for most of the double-digit burst in non-food, non-energy prices in 1974. Wider causes of the 1970s inflation are contested.

contributions.title: Embargo Act of 1807
contributions.summary: Prohibited American exports and most foreign trade, 1807-1809.
contributions.impactBasis: Irwin (Review of International Economics 2005, NBER w8692) estimates the welfare cost of the 1807-09 embargo at about 5-8% of 1807 GNP. Measures this one policy only.

contributions.title: McKinley Tariff Act
contributions.summary: Raised average import duties to about 50 percent; McKinley chaired the House Ways and Means Committee.
contributions.impactBasis: Irwin (J. Economic History 2000, NBER w6835) simulated the tinplate duties of the 1890 McKinley Tariff: the industry became established and flourished, but would have arisen about a decade later anyway, and protection does not pass a cost-benefit test. One industry, not a whole-economy verdict; the sign of the long-run effect is debated.

contributions.title: Segregation of the federal civil service (1913-1921)
contributions.summary: Racial segregation of workplaces in federal departments during Wilson's administration.
contributions.impactBasis: Aneja & Xu (QJE 2022): a difference-in-differences study of federal personnel records 1907-1921 finds the introduction of employment segregation raised the Black wage penalty by about 7 percentage points and lowered descendants' outcomes.

contributions.title: 45th Vice President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served under President Bill Clinton from January 20, 1993, to January 20, 2001.

contributions.title: High-Performance Computing Act of 1991
contributions.summary: Introduced by Senator Gore as S. 272 on January 24, 1991, and signed by President George H. W. Bush on December 9, 1991; it created the High-Performance Computing and Communications program and supported the National Research and Education Network.

contributions.title: Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 (tie-breaking vote)
contributions.summary: As Vice President and President of the Senate, Gore cast the deciding vote on the 1993 budget reconciliation measure (conference report passed 51-50 on August 6, 1993); President Clinton signed it on August 10, 1993.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO, as cited by GAO (1994), estimated the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 would reduce the deficit by $433 billion from 1994 through 1998.

contributions.title: Nobel Peace Prize
contributions.summary: Awarded the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize jointly with the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, for efforts to build up and disseminate greater knowledge about man-made climate change.

contributions.title: Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Album
contributions.summary: Won in 2009 for the audio edition of An Inconvenient Truth: The Planetary Emergency of Global Warming and What We Can Do About It.

contributions.title: Earth in the Balance
contributions.summary: Environmental book published in June 1992 by Houghton Mifflin, written while he was a U.S. Senator.

contributions.title: An Inconvenient Truth (book)
contributions.summary: Book published in 2006 by Rodale alongside the documentary film of the same name.

contributions.title: The Assault on Reason; Our Choice; The Future: Six Drivers of Global Change
contributions.summary: Later books published in 2007, 2009 and 2013 respectively.

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from Tennessee
contributions.summary: Served from January 3, 1985, to January 2, 1993, and earlier served in the U.S. House of Representatives from January 3, 1977, to January 3, 1985.

contributions.title: Generation Investment Management
contributions.summary: Co-launched the sustainable-investment firm in 2004 and serves as its chair.

contributions.title: 44th Vice President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served as Vice President under President George H. W. Bush from January 20, 1989 to January 20, 1993.

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from Indiana
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. Senate from January 3, 1981 to January 3, 1989.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative from Indiana's 4th district
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. House of Representatives from January 3, 1977 to January 3, 1981.

contributions.title: Job Training Partnership Act of 1982
contributions.summary: Introduced in the Senate by Quayle as S. 2036 on February 2, 1982 and co-authored with Senator Edward Kennedy; signed by President Reagan on October 13, 1982, it overhauled federal job training programs.

contributions.title: Standing Firm: A Vice-Presidential Memoir
contributions.summary: Memoir published by HarperCollins in May 1994.

contributions.title: Worth Fighting For
contributions.summary: Book published by W Publishing Group in July 1999.

contributions.title: 46th Vice President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served as Vice President under President George W. Bush from January 20, 2001 to January 20, 2009.

contributions.title: U.S. Secretary of Defense
contributions.summary: Served as Secretary of Defense from March 21, 1989 to January 20, 1993 under President George H. W. Bush.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative from Wyoming
contributions.summary: Served at-large in the U.S. House of Representatives from January 3, 1979 to March 20, 1989, including as House Minority Whip in 1989.

contributions.title: White House Chief of Staff
contributions.summary: Served as White House Chief of Staff under President Gerald Ford from November 21, 1975 to January 20, 1977.

contributions.title: Tie-breaking votes in the Senate
contributions.summary: Cast 8 tie-breaking votes as President of the Senate between 2001 and 2008, per the Senate's official tally.

contributions.title: Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003 (tie-breaking vote)
contributions.summary: Cast the tie-breaking vote on May 23, 2003 to pass the conference report on H.R. 2 by 51-50; it was approved as law on May 28, 2003.
contributions.impactBasis: CRS's review of the 2001-2003 tax cuts reports JCT projected a temporary GDP rise of 0.2% to 0.5% over five years followed by a 0.1% to 0.2% fall, and CRS finds all results relatively small and uncertain. CRS attributes about 2.3 points of GDP of the 2000-2004 budget shift to the tax cuts and notes national saving fell 4.6 points of GDP while private saving rose 1.4.

contributions.title: In My Time: A Personal and Political Memoir
contributions.summary: Memoir written with Liz Cheney, published by Threshold Editions in 2011.

contributions.title: Heart: An American Medical Odyssey
contributions.summary: 2013 book written with cardiologist Jonathan Reiner about his heart disease and 2012 heart transplant.

contributions.title: Exceptional: Why the World Needs a Powerful America
contributions.summary: Book written with Liz Cheney, published in 2015.

contributions.title: 48th Vice President of the United States
contributions.summary: Served as Vice President under President Donald Trump from January 20, 2017 to January 20, 2021.

contributions.title: 50th Governor of Indiana
contributions.summary: Served as Governor of Indiana from January 14, 2013 to January 9, 2017.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative from Indiana
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. House of Representatives from January 3, 2001 to January 3, 2013, representing Indiana's 2nd district and then its 6th district.

contributions.title: Reviving the National Space Council
contributions.summary: Executive Order 13803, signed by President Trump on June 30, 2017, re-established the National Space Council with the Vice President as its Chair; Pence chaired the revived council.

contributions.title: So Help Me God
contributions.summary: Memoir published by Simon & Schuster in November 2022.

contributions.title: Profile in Courage Award
contributions.summary: Received the John F. Kennedy Library Foundation's Profile in Courage Award on May 4, 2025 for his conduct during the certification of the 2020 presidential election on January 6, 2021.

contributions.title: Secretary of Homeland Security
contributions.summary: Confirmed 54-43 by the Senate and sworn in on 2 February 2021 as the first Latino and first immigrant to lead the Department of Homeland Security; served until 20 January 2025.

contributions.title: Deputy Secretary of Homeland Security
contributions.summary: Served as the department's deputy secretary from 23 December 2013 to 28 October 2016.

contributions.title: Director, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
contributions.summary: Led USCIS from 12 August 2009 to 23 December 2013; DHS credits him with developing and implementing the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program, creating the Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate and developing a relief program for orphaned youth after the 2010 Haiti earthquake.

contributions.title: U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California
contributions.summary: Served as U.S. Attorney from 21 December 1998 to 20 April 2001; DHS describes him as the youngest U.S. Attorney in the nation at the time.

contributions.title: Family Reunification Task Force
contributions.summary: Created a task force in May 2021 to reunite families separated at the southern border.

contributions.title: Impeachment by the House of Representatives (2024)
contributions.summary: The House passed H.Res. 863 impeaching him on 13 February 2024 by 214-213, after a first vote failed on 6 February. On 17 April 2024 the Senate ruled both articles unconstitutional and dismissed them without a trial on the merits.

contributions.title: 71st United States Secretary of State
contributions.summary: Led the State Department from January 2021 to January 2025 under President Biden. The State Department Office of the Historian records his nomination on 23 November 2020, Senate confirmation on 26 January 2021 and service ending 20 January 2025.

contributions.title: Deputy Secretary of State
contributions.summary: Served as Deputy Secretary of State under President Obama from 9 January 2015 until 19 January 2017.

contributions.title: U.S. response to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine
contributions.summary: As Secretary of State he was a principal voice of U.S. diplomacy on Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, including support for arms transfers to Ukraine and opposition to ceasefires that would freeze the conflict.

contributions.title: U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council
contributions.summary: Co-chaired the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council as Secretary of State, a forum for transatlantic coordination on trade and technology policy.

contributions.title: Withdrawal of U.S. forces from Afghanistan (2021)
contributions.summary: Diplomatic lead for the State Department during the 2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan, a policy that drew heavy criticism and congressional scrutiny.

contributions.title: Ally versus Ally: America, Europe, and the Siberian Pipeline Crisis
contributions.summary: Authored this 1987 monograph on the transatlantic dispute over the Siberian natural-gas pipeline.

contributions.title: Grand Officer of the National Order of the Legion of Honour (France)
contributions.summary: Awarded the French Legion of Honour at the rank of Grand Officer in 2025.

contributions.title: Secretary of Agriculture
contributions.summary: Sworn in as Secretary of Agriculture after a 72-28 Senate confirmation vote.

contributions.title: Acting Director, White House Domestic Policy Council
contributions.summary: Led the Domestic Policy Council on an acting basis from 2020-05-24 to 2021-01-20.

contributions.title: Director, Office of American Innovation
contributions.summary: Co-directed the White House Office of American Innovation with Jared Kushner from 2018-02-28 to 2020-05-24.

contributions.title: USDA relocation to regional offices
contributions.summary: Issued a July 2025 memorandum moving most remaining Washington, D.C. USDA employees to five regional offices.

contributions.title: National forest protections rollback
contributions.summary: Removed environmental protections for nearly 60% of national forest land in April 2025 and in June 2025 rescinded a rule that barred road construction and timber harvesting in some federal forest areas.

contributions.title: SNAP recertification request to Minnesota
contributions.summary: Asked Minnesota in December 2025 to recertify many SNAP recipients and froze the state's SNAP funding in January 2026; Minnesota sued.

contributions.title: Criminal justice reform work including the First Step Act
contributions.summary: Wikipedia reports she worked on criminal justice reform in the first Trump administration, including the First Step Act.

contributions.title: Chairman and CEO, Liberty Energy
contributions.summary: Held the chairman and chief executive positions at Liberty Energy (founded 2011 as Liberty Oilfield Services) from March 2011 (month-level date per his OGE Form 278e); he was still listed in both roles when he filed as a nominee in January 2025.

contributions.title: Director, Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City
contributions.summary: Served as a director of the Kansas City Fed from January 2020 (month-level date per his OGE Form 278e) to June 2024.

contributions.title: Cancellation of Department of Energy project funding
contributions.summary: The Department of Energy announced on October 1, 2025 that it was cancelling about $7.6 billion in funding for projects, as reported by Reuters.

contributions.title: Direction to FERC on large-load interconnection
contributions.summary: In October 2025 Wright directed the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to act on interconnecting large loads such as data centers to the grid, as reported by Reuters on October 24, 2025.

contributions.title: U.S.-Saudi civil nuclear cooperation agreement
contributions.summary: Co-signed a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia in Washington, D.C. on July 22, 2026, as reported by The Guardian.

contributions.title: 66th U.S. Secretary of State
contributions.summary: Served as Secretary of State in the George W. Bush administration from January 26, 2005 to January 20, 2009.

contributions.title: U.S. National Security Advisor
contributions.summary: Served as the 19th National Security Advisor from January 20, 2001 to January 26, 2005.

contributions.title: Transformational diplomacy
contributions.summary: Outlined the plan in a speech on January 18, 2006 to reshape U.S. diplomacy, including moving diplomats to priority regions and building partnerships with stable, democratic states.

contributions.title: Provost of Stanford University
contributions.summary: Served as Stanford's provost from 1993 to 1999.

contributions.title: Director of the Hoover Institution
contributions.summary: Became the eighth director of the Hoover Institution on September 1, 2020, the first woman to hold the position.

contributions.title: Extraordinary, Ordinary People: A Memoir of Family
contributions.summary: Memoir published in 2010.

contributions.title: No Higher Honor: A Memoir of My Years in Washington
contributions.summary: Memoir of her years as National Security Advisor and Secretary of State, published in 2011.

contributions.title: Democracy: Stories from the Long Road to Freedom
contributions.summary: Book published in 2017.

contributions.title: To Build a Better World: Choices to End the Cold War and Create a Global Commonwealth
contributions.summary: Book co-authored with Philip Zelikow, listed with a 2019 date on her Hoover profile.

contributions.title: Augusta National Golf Club membership
contributions.summary: Admitted on August 20, 2012 as one of the first two women members of the club.

contributions.title: Secretary of the Interior
contributions.summary: Sworn in as the 55th Secretary of the Interior after Senate confirmation on 2025-01-30.

contributions.title: Chair, National Energy Dominance Council
contributions.summary: Executive Order 14213 makes the Secretary of the Interior chair and the Secretary of Energy vice chair of the council.

contributions.title: Governor of North Dakota
contributions.summary: Served as the 33rd governor from 2016-12-15 to 2024-12-15 after winning in 2016 and being re-elected in 2020.

contributions.title: Arctic National Wildlife Refuge oil leasing
contributions.summary: As Secretary opened about 1.53 million acres of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil drilling.

contributions.title: North Dakota carbon-neutral-by-2030 goal
contributions.summary: Set a goal for North Dakota to be carbon neutral by 2030 and backed carbon dioxide pipelines as governor.

contributions.title: Great Plains Software
contributions.summary: Provided seed capital in 1983 for the Fargo software company, led it to an IPO, and it was acquired by Microsoft in 2001 for about $1.1 billion in stock.

contributions.title: 2024 Republican presidential campaign
contributions.summary: Announced a Republican presidential bid on 2023-06-07 and suspended the campaign on 2023-12-04.

contributions.title: Secretary of Veterans Affairs
contributions.summary: Confirmed by the Senate 77-23 on February 4, 2025 and sworn in as the 12th Secretary of Veterans Affairs on February 5, 2025.

contributions.title: Federal Law Enforcement Self-Defense and Protection Act of 2015
contributions.summary: Preserves the right of covered federal law enforcement officers to carry a government-issued firearm during a covered furlough.

contributions.title: Sidney Oslin Smith, Jr. Federal Building and United States Courthouse designation
contributions.summary: Designated the federal building and courthouse at 121 Spring Street SE in Gainesville, Georgia, as the Sidney Oslin Smith, Jr. Federal Building and United States Courthouse.

contributions.title: Zack T. Addington Post Office designation
contributions.summary: Designated the Postal Service facility at 430 Main Street in Clermont, Georgia, as the Zack T. Addington Post Office.

contributions.title: Intercountry Adoption Information Act of 2019
contributions.summary: Enacted law on intercountry adoption information, classified by Congress.gov under the International Affairs policy area.

contributions.title: U.S. House of Representatives, Georgia's 9th district
contributions.summary: Represented Georgia's 9th congressional district from January 3, 2013 to January 3, 2021.

contributions.title: Georgia House of Representatives, 27th district
contributions.summary: Served in the Georgia House of Representatives from January 3, 2007 to January 3, 2013.

contributions.title: U.S. Air Force Reserve chaplain
contributions.summary: Has served as a chaplain in the U.S. Air Force Reserve since 2002, was deployed to Balad Air Base in 2008, and was promoted to colonel in 2023.

contributions.title: 40th United States Secretary of Commerce
contributions.summary: Confirmed by the Senate on 2 March 2021 and sworn in on 3 March 2021; served until 20 January 2025.

contributions.title: CHIPS and Science Act implementation
contributions.summary: The CHIPS and Science Act was signed on 9 August 2022; the Commerce Department, through its CHIPS Program Office, administered about $39 billion in grants, loans and tax benefits for U.S. semiconductor manufacturing. Raimondo published the first CHIPS funding application on 28 February 2023.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO's score of the CHIPS and Science Act estimates it would increase deficits by $79 billion over 2022-2032 (before later baseline updates), a small share of projected 10-year federal deficits; CBO's score does not value the policy's economic benefits.

contributions.title: CHIPS manufacturing incentive awards
contributions.summary: Under her leadership Commerce announced large CHIPS awards in 2024, including Intel ($8.5 billion), TSMC ($6.6 billion), Samsung ($6.4 billion) and Micron ($6.1 billion); Bloomberg reported that $32.8 billion of the $39 billion fund had been allocated by May 2024.

contributions.title: 75th Governor of Rhode Island
