contributions.title: General Treasurer of Rhode Island
contributions.summary: Served as the state's 30th general treasurer from 4 January 2011 to 6 January 2015.

contributions.title: Rhodes Scholarship
contributions.summary: Was a Rhodes Scholar, earning a doctorate at the University of Oxford.

contributions.title: 67th U.S. Secretary of State
contributions.summary: Served as Secretary of State in the Obama administration from January 21, 2009 to February 1, 2013.

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from New York
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. Senate from January 3, 2001 until resigning on January 21, 2009 to become Secretary of State.

contributions.title: 2016 Democratic presidential nominee
contributions.summary: Formally nominated at the Democratic National Convention in Philadelphia on July 26, 2016; she lost the Electoral College to Donald Trump in November 2016.

contributions.title: Living History
contributions.summary: Memoir published by Simon & Schuster on June 9, 2003.

contributions.title: Hard Choices
contributions.summary: Memoir of her time as Secretary of State, published by Simon & Schuster on June 10, 2014.

contributions.title: What Happened
contributions.summary: Account of the 2016 presidential campaign, published by Simon & Schuster on September 12, 2017.

contributions.title: Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Album (1997)
contributions.summary: Won the 1997 Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Album for the audio recording of her book It Takes a Village.

contributions.title: Secretary of Commerce
contributions.summary: Leads the Department of Commerce following Senate confirmation by a 51-45 vote on 2025-02-18.

contributions.title: Establishing the United States Investment Accelerator
contributions.summary: The order directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish an office within the Department of Commerce to facilitate and accelerate investments above $1 billion in the United States.

contributions.title: The Gold Card
contributions.summary: The order directs creation of a Gold Card program led by Commerce, with State and Homeland Security coordinating, and gives the three secretaries 90 days to implement it.

contributions.title: Co-chair, Trump-Vance 2025 Transition
contributions.summary: Named by the Trump campaign as co-chair, with Linda McMahon, of the 2024 presidential transition effort covering personnel vetting and policy planning.

contributions.title: President and chief executive, Cantor Fitzgerald
contributions.summary: Joined Cantor Fitzgerald in 1983 and became president and chief executive in 1991, later serving as chairman and CEO until divesting his ownership in 2025.

contributions.title: 26th U.S. Secretary of Defense
contributions.summary: Confirmed by the Senate 98-1 and sworn in on January 20, 2017; his departure took effect January 1, 2019.

contributions.title: Resignation as Secretary of Defense
contributions.summary: Announced his resignation by letter on December 20, 2018 after the decision to withdraw troops from Syria; President Trump moved his departure forward from February 28, 2019 to January 1, 2019.

contributions.title: Commander, U.S. Central Command
contributions.summary: Served as the 11th commander of CENTCOM from August 11, 2010 to March 22, 2013, then retired from the Marine Corps.

contributions.title: NATO Supreme Allied Commander Transformation and Commander, U.S. Joint Forces Command
contributions.summary: Held both commands concurrently from 2007; led Allied Command Transformation until 2009 and U.S. Joint Forces Command until 2010.

contributions.title: Command of 1st Marine Division in Iraq
contributions.summary: As a major general commanded the 1st Marine Division during the initial attack and stability operations in Iraq.

contributions.title: Call Sign Chaos: Learning to Lead
contributions.summary: Memoir and argument for an internationalist foreign policy, published in 2019 and reviewed by The New York Times on August 30, 2019; co-written with Bing West.

contributions.title: Warriors & Citizens: American Views of Our Military
contributions.summary: Co-edited volume published by the Hoover Institution in August 2016.

contributions.title: Defense Distinguished Service Medal and other U.S. decorations
contributions.summary: Decorations include the Defense Distinguished Service Medal with oak leaf cluster, Navy Distinguished Service Medal, Defense Superior Service Medal, Legion of Merit and Bronze Star with Combat V.

contributions.title: Davies Family Distinguished Fellow, Hoover Institution
contributions.summary: Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University, which he left to serve as Secretary of Defense and later rejoined.

contributions.title: United States Trade Representative (20th)
contributions.summary: Senate-confirmed (56-43, 2025-02-26) as the 20th U.S. Trade Representative, succeeding Katherine Tai.

contributions.title: Acting Director, Office of Government Ethics
contributions.summary: Appointed acting director of the Office of Government Ethics on 2025-03-26; Eric Ueland succeeded him as acting director in August 2025.

contributions.title: Acting Special Counsel, U.S. Office of Special Counsel
contributions.summary: Appointed acting special counsel of the United States on 2025-03-26; Charles Baldis was appointed Special Counsel in September 2026.

contributions.title: USMCA joint review launched with Mexico
contributions.summary: USTR and Mexico announced the launch of the review process under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement.

contributions.title: 60 Section 301 investigations on forced labor
contributions.summary: USTR initiated 60 Section 301 investigations relating to failures to take action on forced labor.

contributions.title: U.S.-Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade
contributions.summary: Greer oversaw the signing of the U.S.-Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade.

contributions.title: Section 301 determination on Brazil
contributions.summary: USTR issued a Section 301 determination on Brazil's acts, policies and practices.
contributions.impactBasis: The determination underpins a tariff action on Brazilian goods (reported as 25 percent on most products). The IGM Economic Experts Panel in 2018 found no respondent agreed that new US tariffs on steel and aluminum would improve Americans' welfare, and Amiti, Redding and Weinstein (NBER) find the 2018-19 US tariffs were almost entirely borne by US firms and consumers; the evidence is on earlier tariff rounds, and the determination also targets non-tariff practices (ethanol access, IP, digital trade) whose effects are not quantified.

contributions.title: Joint ministerial statement on global excess capacity
contributions.summary: Fourteen economies joined the United States in signing a joint ministerial statement addressing global excess capacity.

contributions.title: 78th United States Secretary of the Treasury
contributions.summary: Sworn in as the first woman to lead the Treasury Department on 26 January 2021; served until 20 January 2025. Treasury describes her as the first person in American history to have led the Council of Economic Advisers, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury Department.

contributions.title: Chair of the Federal Reserve
contributions.summary: Chaired the Federal Reserve Board of Governors from 3 February 2014 to 3 February 2018, the first woman in the role, after serving as Vice Chair from October 2010.

contributions.title: Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve
contributions.summary: Served as Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve Board from 4 October 2010 to 3 February 2014.

contributions.title: President, Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
contributions.summary: Led the San Francisco Fed from 14 June 2004 to 4 October 2010, a period in which she identified a housing bubble and helped manage the financial crisis.

contributions.title: Chair, Council of Economic Advisers
contributions.summary: Chaired President Clinton's Council of Economic Advisers from 18 February 1997 to 3 August 1999.

contributions.title: 15% global minimum corporate tax
contributions.summary: As Treasury Secretary she advocated a 15% global minimum corporate tax, which more than 130 countries agreed to in 2021.
contributions.impactBasis: An OECD Secretariat working paper (not official OECD views) estimates the 15% global minimum tax would roughly halve profit shifting and cut the share of multinational profit taxed below 15% by about 80% (from 36% to 7%), while raising global corporate tax revenue by $155-192 billion a year; it also notes possible effects on the allocation of investment.

contributions.title: Price cap on Russian oil
contributions.summary: Helped design the $60-per-barrel price cap on Russian oil announced in 2022.

contributions.title: Efficiency Wage Models of the Labor Market
contributions.summary: Co-edited this 1986 volume with George Akerlof; her research on efficiency wages with Akerlof examined why firms often pay above the minimum needed to hire workers.

contributions.title: Wilbur Cross Medal
contributions.summary: Received Yale's Wilbur Cross Medal in 1997.

contributions.title: Director of National Intelligence
contributions.summary: Sworn in on August 3, 2026 as the ninth DNI after Senate confirmation 51-47 on July 28, 2026; he succeeded Tulsi Gabbard, who resigned effective June 30, 2026 citing her husband's cancer diagnosis, and Bill Pulte served as acting director in the interim.

contributions.title: U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York
contributions.summary: Took office as acting U.S. Attorney on April 22, 2025 and served until his resignation on July 29, 2026.

contributions.title: Chairman of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
contributions.summary: Served as SEC Chairman from May 4, 2017 to December 23, 2020, after Senate confirmation 61-37 on May 2, 2017.

contributions.title: Regulation Best Interest
contributions.summary: As SEC Chairman, presented the rulemaking package in which the Commission adopted Regulation Best Interest requiring broker-dealers to act in retail customers' best interest when recommending securities.
contributions.impactBasis: The SEC's economic analysis expects Regulation Best Interest to reduce agency costs between broker-dealers and retail customers through disclosure, care and conflict-mitigation obligations (an information-asymmetry fix), but states that benefits and costs are difficult to quantify with meaningful precision and estimates only compliance costs (e.g. a $42.84 million initial cost for the Disclosure Obligation). Academic commentators and state regulators' reviews dispute how much it changed broker conduct, and no controlled post-adoption study was found.

contributions.title: U.S. Attorney General
contributions.summary: Sworn in as the 84th Attorney General on February 9, 2017 and resigned November 7, 2018.

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from Alabama
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. Senate from January 3, 1997 until February 8, 2017, when he left to become Attorney General.

contributions.title: Prison Rape Elimination Act of 2003
contributions.summary: Initial Senate sponsor of S. 1435, signed by President George W. Bush on September 4, 2003; described as the first federal law intended to deter sexual assault of prisoners.

contributions.title: Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act of 2000
contributions.summary: Introduced S. 768 on April 13, 1999; the act, signed by President Clinton on November 22, 2000, placed military contractors under U.S. criminal jurisdiction.

contributions.title: Zero-tolerance border prosecution policy
contributions.summary: On April 6, 2018 directed federal prosecutors to adopt a zero-tolerance policy for all offenses of improper entry into the United States; on May 7, 2018 he publicly announced that those who crossed unlawfully would be prosecuted and that children of adults prosecuted would be separated from them.

contributions.title: Attorney General of Alabama
contributions.summary: Served as the 44th Attorney General of Alabama from January 16, 1995 to January 3, 1997.

contributions.title: U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Alabama
contributions.summary: Appointed by President Reagan in 1981 and served until March 23, 1993.

contributions.title: 68th U.S. Secretary of State
contributions.summary: Served as Secretary of State in the Obama administration from February 1, 2013 to January 20, 2017.

contributions.title: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. Senate from January 2, 1985 until resigning on February 1, 2013 to become Secretary of State.

contributions.title: Chairman, Senate Committee on Foreign Relations
contributions.summary: Chaired the Senate Foreign Relations Committee from 2009 to 2013.

contributions.title: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (Iran nuclear deal)
contributions.summary: As Secretary of State he was a lead U.S. negotiator of the agreement between Iran and the P5+1, reached in Vienna on July 14, 2015.

contributions.title: Paris Agreement signing for the United States
contributions.summary: Signed the Paris climate agreement for the United States at the United Nations in New York on April 22, 2016, the day it opened for signature.

contributions.title: Enhanced Partnership with Pakistan Act of 2009 (Kerry-Lugar)
contributions.summary: Senate bill S. 1707, sponsored by Kerry and Richard Lugar, authorized about $1.5 billion a year in non-military aid to Pakistan; approved October 15, 2009.

contributions.title: Special Presidential Envoy for Climate
contributions.summary: First holder of the post, from January 20, 2021; he stepped down on March 6, 2024.

contributions.title: Presidential Medal of Freedom
contributions.summary: Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Biden on May 3, 2024.

contributions.title: Every Day Is Extra
contributions.summary: Memoir published in 2018.

contributions.title: Vietnam War military decorations
contributions.summary: Received the Silver Star, the Bronze Star with Combat V, three Purple Hearts and the Combat Action Ribbon for U.S. Navy service in Vietnam.

contributions.title: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency
contributions.summary: Assumed office as CIA Director on January 23, 2025, following Senate confirmation.

contributions.title: Director of National Intelligence
contributions.summary: Served as DNI from May 26, 2020 to January 20, 2021.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative, Texas's 4th congressional district
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. House of Representatives from January 3, 2015 to May 22, 2020.

contributions.title: Strengthening State and Local Cyber Crime Fighting Act of 2017
contributions.summary: H.R. 1616 amended the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize the National Computer Forensics Institute; signed by the President on November 2, 2017.

contributions.title: United States-Israel Advanced Research Partnership Act of 2016
contributions.summary: H.R. 5877 amended the Homeland Security Act of 2002 and the United States-Israel Strategic Partnership Act of 2014 to promote cooperative homeland security research and antiterrorism programs relating to cybersecurity; became law December 16, 2016.

contributions.title: Mayor of Heath, Texas
contributions.summary: Served as mayor from June 14, 2004 to May 14, 2012.

contributions.title: Acting U.S. Attorney, Eastern District of Texas
contributions.summary: Served as acting U.S. Attorney from May 21, 2007 to May 9, 2008.

contributions.title: Secretary of Labor
contributions.summary: Became the 31st Secretary of Labor after Senate confirmation by a 47-41 vote on 2026-09-30, with the oath administered by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

contributions.title: Acting Secretary of Labor
contributions.summary: Led the department as acting secretary after Lori Chavez-DeRemer's resignation.

contributions.title: Deputy Secretary of Labor
contributions.summary: Oversaw the department's daily operations after Senate confirmation in March 2025.

contributions.title: Commissioner, U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
contributions.summary: Served as an EEOC commissioner from September 2020 to August 2024, including as vice chair until January 2021.

contributions.title: Acting Director, U.S. Office of Government Ethics
contributions.summary: Designated acting director of the Office of Government Ethics in June 2026 while continuing at the Labor Department.

contributions.title: Wage and Hour Division, Department of Labor
contributions.summary: Served from 2017 to 2020 as senior policy advisor, deputy administrator and acting administrator of the Wage and Hour Division.

contributions.title: Opinion letter and PAID programs revived
contributions.summary: As Deputy Secretary he revived the Wage and Hour opinion letter program and the Payroll Audit Independent Determination (PAID) program.

contributions.title: Administrator of the Small Business Administration (28th)
contributions.summary: Confirmed by the Senate 52-46 on 2025-02-19 and took office as the 28th SBA Administrator.

contributions.title: United States Senator from Georgia
contributions.summary: Appointed by Governor Brian Kemp to the seat vacated by Johnny Isakson and served until 2021-01-20.

contributions.title: Bill to extend the Paycheck Protection Program covered period
contributions.summary: Would have extended the covered period for the Paycheck Protection Program.
contributions.impactBasis: Evidence is for the PPP as a whole, not the extension's margin: Autor et al. (Journal of Economic Perspectives, 2022) estimate $169K to $258K per job-year retained, only 23 to 34 percent of dollars reaching workers who would otherwise have lost jobs, and about three-quarters of funds accruing to the top household-income quintile. The program also stabilised many firms during the 2020 shutdowns, and the estimates rest on identification assumptions.

contributions.title: Bill authorizing VA health trainees to provide telemedicine
contributions.summary: Would authorize certain Department of Veterans Affairs postgraduate health employees and trainees to provide treatment via telemedicine (introduced with Sen. Sinema).

contributions.title: Bill moving veteran-owned small business verification to the SBA
contributions.summary: Would transfer responsibility for verifying veteran- and service-disabled-veteran-owned small businesses to the Small Business Administration.

contributions.title: Bill to codify the Minority Business Development Agency
contributions.summary: Would codify the Minority Business Development Agency of the Department of Commerce (introduced with Sens. Crapo and Rubio).

contributions.title: Bill defining sex for Title IX athletics
contributions.summary: Would provide that compliance with Title IX in athletics be determined by recognizing sex based on reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

contributions.title: Bill increasing criminal penalties under the National Voter Registration Act
contributions.summary: Would amend the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to increase criminal penalties under the Act.

contributions.title: United States Secretary of Homeland Security
contributions.summary: Led the Department of Homeland Security as its 8th Secretary from January 25, 2025. Trump announced her removal on March 5, 2026 and Markwayne Mullin was sworn in as her successor on March 24, 2026.

contributions.title: Governor of South Dakota
contributions.summary: 33rd Governor of South Dakota and the state's first female governor, in office from January 5, 2019 until she resigned to join the Cabinet on January 25, 2025.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative for South Dakota's at-large district

contributions.title: South Dakota House of Representatives, District 6
contributions.summary: Served in the South Dakota House from January 9, 2007 to January 3, 2011; the article states she was prime sponsor of 11 bills that became state law.

contributions.title: Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas
contributions.summary: Appointed Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas, a Western Hemisphere security initiative, in March 2026 after leaving the Department of Homeland Security.

contributions.title: Not My First Rodeo
contributions.summary: Memoir published in 2022 by Twelve.

contributions.title: No Going Back

contributions.title: Repeal of the 2009 greenhouse gas endangerment finding

contributions.impactBasis: EPA's Regulatory Impact Analysis counts about $1.3 trillion in avoided vehicle compliance costs (2027-2055) but assigns no value to higher greenhouse-gas damages or non-GHG health effects. Resources for the Future's modelling of the light-duty standards, including social-cost-of-carbon damages of $1.5 trillion (3% discount rate, 2026-2050), estimates a net societal loss of about $801 billion; FactCheck.org reports EPA's own central fuel-price scenario shows a $180 billion net cost, while some scenarios show net savings.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative, New York's 1st congressional district
contributions.summary: Served in the U.S. House of Representatives from January 3, 2015 to January 3, 2023.

contributions.title: New York State Senator, 3rd district

CBO's distributional analysis finds resources fall for the lowest income decile (about $1,200 a year, 3.1 percent of income, mainly Medicaid and SNAP changes) and rise for the highest decile (about $13,600 a year, 2.7 percent), and its dynamic estimate of the House-passed version put real GDP 0.5 percent higher on average over 2025-2034 with 10-year rates about 14 basis points higher.

contributions.title: Emergency supplemental appropriations, April 2024
contributions.summary: As Speaker, brought the April 2024 foreign-aid supplemental (H.R. 815) to the House floor; it was signed on April 24, 2024.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO scored the Ukraine Security Supplemental division (H.R. 8035) at about $60.8 billion in budget authority and about $60.9 billion in outlays through 2033, designated as emergency requirements; the Israel and Indo-Pacific divisions were scored in separate estimates. The one-time emergency spending adds to deficits but is small relative to the multi-year baseline.

contributions.title: Chair, House Republican Study Committee
contributions.summary: Chaired the Republican Study Committee from January 3, 2019 to January 3, 2021.

contributions.title: Vice Chair, House Republican Conference
contributions.summary: Served as vice chair of the House Republican Conference from January 3, 2021 until becoming Speaker on October 25, 2023.

contributions.title: Red River National Wildlife Refuge Boundary Modification Act
contributions.summary: Sponsored H.R. 6427, which modifies the boundary of the Red River National Wildlife Refuge.

contributions.title: Save the Liberty Theatre Act of 2021
contributions.summary: Sponsored H.R. 3197, which directs the Interior Department to convey certain parcels to the City of Eunice, Louisiana.

contributions.title: Contract with America
contributions.summary: Co-wrote with Dick Armey the 1994 Republican legislative platform, signed by nearly all House Republican candidates, which the new majority brought to House votes in early 1995.

contributions.title: Speaker of the House
contributions.summary: Elected the 50th Speaker on January 4, 1995 and re-elected January 7, 1997, the first Republican Speaker in four decades; his speakership ended January 3, 1999.

contributions.title: Congressional Accountability Act of 1995
contributions.summary: Applied a set of federal workplace laws to Congress; an early item of the Republican-led 104th Congress, signed January 23, 1995.

contributions.title: Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996
contributions.summary: Welfare-reform law passed by the Republican House under Speaker Gingrich and signed by President Clinton on August 22, 1996.
contributions.impactBasis: Rebecca Blank's review of the economics literature on 1990s welfare reform (Journal of Economic Literature, 2002) found that the reforms changed behavior and that new-style programs produced meaningful gains in work and earnings, although caseload declines also reflected the strong economy and findings on poverty and well-being vary.

contributions.title: Taxpayer Relief Act of 1997
contributions.summary: 1997 tax law including a capital gains tax cut, enacted alongside the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 (Pub. L. 105-33); Gingrich is credited with setting its agenda as Speaker. Signed August 5, 1997.

contributions.title: Time Man of the Year (1995)
contributions.summary: Named Time magazine's 1995 Man of the Year for his role in ending the four-decade Democratic majority in the House.

contributions.title: House Minority Whip
contributions.summary: Served as House Republican Whip from March 20, 1989 to January 3, 1995 before becoming Speaker.

contributions.title: Winning the Future
contributions.summary: Nonfiction book published in 2005; among dozens of books he has written, including To Save America (2010) and March to the Majority (2023).

contributions.title: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017
contributions.summary: As Speaker he pushed the Republican tax overhaul through the House; the bill (H.R. 1, introduced by Rep. Kevin Brady) was signed by President Trump on December 22, 2017.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO's April 2018 estimate found the 2017 tax act raises the level of real GDP by about 0.7 percent on average over 2018-2028, with the effect fading as temporary provisions expire and a 43 percent foreign share of the gain, while adding about $1.9 trillion to deficits over 2018-2028; 88 percent of IGM Forum experts agreed in 2017 that debt-to-GDP would be substantially higher and only 2 percent agreed growth would be substantially higher. CBO's 2018 household-income analysis found after-tax income rose in every quintile with the largest reductions at the top.

contributions.title: Speaker of the House
contributions.summary: Elected the 54th Speaker on October 29, 2015 with 236 votes to fill the vacancy left by John Boehner's resignation; re-elected January 3, 2017 and served to January 3, 2019.

contributions.title: Chair, House Budget Committee
contributions.summary: Chaired the House Committee on the Budget in the 112th and 113th Congresses (2011-2015).

contributions.title: Chair, House Ways and Means Committee
contributions.summary: Chaired the House Committee on Ways and Means in the 114th Congress until his election as Speaker in October 2015.

contributions.title: Republican nominee for Vice President (2012)
contributions.summary: Announced on August 11, 2012 as Mitt Romney's running mate; the Romney-Ryan ticket lost the November 2012 election.

contributions.title: Young Guns: A New Generation of Conservative Leaders
contributions.summary: Co-authored with Eric Cantor and Kevin McCarthy; published by Threshold Editions in 2010.

contributions.title: Fox Corporation board
contributions.summary: Joined the board of Fox Corporation in March 2019 after leaving Congress.

contributions.title: Setting Every Community Up for Retirement Enhancement (SECURE) Act of 2019 (H.R. 1994)
contributions.summary: Introduced the retirement-savings bill H.R. 1994, which passed the House on May 23, 2019 and became law in December 2019 as part of the FY2020 appropriations act.

contributions.title: Chair, House Committee on Ways and Means
contributions.summary: Chaired the Ways and Means Committee from January 3, 2019 to January 3, 2023; ranking member since January 3, 2023.

contributions.title: Suspending Normal Trade Relations with Russia and Belarus Act
contributions.summary: Sponsored H.R. 7108, which became law on 2022-04-08.

contributions.summary: Sponsored H.R. 7691, which became law on 2022-05-21.

It is a one-time addition to deficits rather than a recurring commitment, so the long-run fiscal effect is small but negative.

contributions.title: Johanna's Law reauthorization (H.R. 2941)

It continues FY2022 appropriations through December 3, 2021, avoiding a lapse on October 1, 2021. The avoided loss is small relative to GDP and temporary in scope, so the benefit is scored modestly.

The saving is small against the multi-trillion-dollar deficit baseline.

This act provides FY2026 appropriations for multiple divisions (defense, labor-HHS-education, transportation-HUD, financial services, state/national security), removing the funding-lapse risk for those agencies for the fiscal year. contributions.summary: Signed Senate Bill 47 creating a Kentucky medical cannabis program.

contributions.title: Sports wagering legalization (House Bill 551)
contributions.summary: Signed House Bill 551 legalizing sports wagering in Kentucky.
contributions.impactBasis: Baker, Balthrop, Johnson, Kotter and Pisciotta (NBER WP 33108; Journal of Financial Economics 2026) find that online sports-betting legalization raises betting without displacing other gambling or consumption, reducing household savings, with effects concentrated among financially constrained households (more credit-card debt, less available credit, more overdrafts). The study covers states that legalized before Kentucky and does not net out tax revenue or consumer enjoyment.

contributions.title: Tennessee Education Savings Account Pilot Program (HB 939)
contributions.summary: Signed the 2019 education options act that enacted the Tennessee Education Savings Account Pilot Program.
contributions.impactBasis: The only randomized evaluation of a statewide voucher for low-income students in a comparable setting, the Louisiana Scholarship Program (Abdulkadiroglu, Pathak and Walters, AEJ: Applied Economics 2018), found participation lowered math scores by 0.4 standard deviations and also reduced reading, science and social studies achievement; results elsewhere are mixed, so the sign for Tennessee's capped 15,000-student program is uncertain.

contributions.title: Permitless carry firearms bill (HB 786)
contributions.summary: Signed the 2021 firearms bill (HB 786), titled "Firearms and Ammunition" on the legislature site and widely reported as Tennessee's permitless carry law.

contributions.title: Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security (ELVIS) Act (HB 2091)
contributions.summary: Signed the act that replaced the Personal Rights Protection Act of 1984 and defines voice as a protected personal right.

contributions.title: Governor of Washington
contributions.summary: Sworn in as governor on January 15, 2025.

contributions.title: Executive Order 25-02: Assessing Regulatory Efficiency and Addressing Washington's Affordable Housing Crisis
contributions.summary: Directed a review of regulations affecting housing construction on his first day in office.

contributions.title: Executive Order 25-01: Strategic Convening to Protect Access to Reproductive Health Care
contributions.summary: Convened a strategic roundtable on protecting access to reproductive health care.

contributions.title: Attorney General of Washington
contributions.summary: Served as the state's attorney general from January 16, 2013 to January 15, 2025.

contributions.title: King County Council
contributions.summary: Served on the King County Council from January 1, 2004 and chaired it from November 2009 until January 2013.

contributions.title: Governor of Idaho
contributions.summary: Sworn in as the 33rd governor of Idaho, succeeding Butch Otter.

contributions.title: Lieutenant Governor of Idaho
contributions.summary: Served as the 42nd lieutenant governor of Idaho under Gov. Butch Otter for ten years before becoming governor.

contributions.title: House Bill 436 income tax rate revision and rebate
contributions.summary: Signed a bill revising Idaho's individual and corporate income tax rates and providing for an income tax rebate.
contributions.impactBasis: The bill's statement of purpose and fiscal note (prepared by its sponsors, per its own disclaimer) lists a one-time $350 million rebate in FY2022 and $251 million per year of ongoing income-tax relief from FY2023 by lowering brackets, partly offset by $94 million per year from the Tax Relief fund. No independent dynamic or growth estimate was found.

contributions.title: Fairness in Women's Sports Act (House Bill 500)
contributions.summary: Signed a law banning transgender women from playing on women's athletic teams.

contributions.title: Vulnerable Child Protection Act (House Bill 71)
contributions.summary: Signed a law banning puberty blockers, hormone therapy and gender-affirming surgery for people under 18, effective 2024.

contributions.title: Election Integrity Act of 2021 (SB 202)
contributions.summary: Rewrote Georgia election procedures, including early in-person voting, absentee ballot ID requirements and legislative authority over local election officials.

contributions.title: Living Infants Fairness and Equality (LIFE) Act (HB 481)
contributions.summary: Prohibited most abortions after a fetal heartbeat is detected; federal courts blocked it in 2019 and voided it in 2020, and the injunction was later overturned after Dobbs.

contributions.title: Constitutional carry (SB 319)
contributions.summary: Allowed most Georgia residents eligible for a carry license to carry a concealed handgun without a permit.

contributions.title: Georgia Secretary of State
contributions.summary: Served as the state's 27th secretary of state from January 8, 2010 to November 8, 2018, after appointment by Governor Sonny Perdue and election in 2010 and 2014.

contributions.title: Georgia Pathways to Coverage (Medicaid partial-expansion waiver)
contributions.summary: Georgia Medicaid demonstration with a work requirement, launched July 2023.
contributions.impactBasis: GAO-25-108160: administrative spending was $54.2 million of $80.3 million total demonstration spending (about two-thirds) in the first 4.5 years, with enrollment far below the state's first-year projection. Fiscal efficiency of this one program only.

contributions.title: Lieutenant Governor of Rhode Island
contributions.summary: Served as lieutenant governor from January 6, 2015 until becoming governor on March 2, 2021.

contributions.title: Succeeded to the governorship
contributions.summary: Sworn in as the 76th governor of Rhode Island on March 2, 2021, when Gina Raimondo resigned to become U.S. Secretary of Commerce.

contributions.title: Executive moratorium on the death penalty
contributions.summary: Issued Executive Order N-09-19 instituting a reprieve for all people sentenced to death in California, repealing the lethal injection protocol and closing the San Quentin death chamber.

contributions.title: COVID-19 state of emergency
contributions.summary: Declared a state of emergency after California's first COVID-19 death and later issued a statewide stay-at-home order.

contributions.title: Phase-out of gasoline-powered new vehicles
contributions.summary: Signed an executive order requiring all new passenger vehicles sold in California to be zero-emission by 2035.
contributions.impactBasis: The implementing rule (CARB Advanced Clean Cars II) was estimated by CARB at $210.35 billion in costs and $301.41 billion in benefits over 2026-2040, a net benefit of $91.1 billion and a benefit-cost ratio of 1.43, with benefits including avoided health damage and climate-pollution reductions. These are the regulator's own estimates and depend on fuel-price, vehicle-cost and social-cost-of-carbon assumptions.

contributions.title: California Proposition 50 (2025)
contributions.summary: Secured legislative approval in August 2025 of a constitutional amendment allowing congressional redistricting; voters approved it in November 2025.

contributions.title: Mayor of San Francisco
contributions.summary: Served as the 42nd mayor of San Francisco from January 2004 to January 2011, after seven years on the Board of Supervisors.

contributions.title: Project Homekey (motel and hotel conversion for homeless housing)
contributions.summary: State program converting hotels and motels into permanent housing.
contributions.impactBasis: California State Auditor (report 2023-102.1): Homekey appears cost-effective compared with building new affordable housing units (about $144,000 per unit against $380,000-$570,000). Cost per unit only; resident outcomes are not measured.

contributions.title: Texas Heartbeat Act (SB 8)
contributions.summary: Signed the abortion law that applies after detection of an unborn child's heartbeat and authorizes a private civil right of action.

contributions.title: Weather emergency and power outage preparedness (SB 3)
contributions.summary: Signed the act relating to preparing for, preventing, and responding to weather emergencies and power outages, effective immediately.

contributions.title: Education savings account program (SB 2)
contributions.summary: Signed the act relating to the establishment of an education savings account program.
contributions.impactBasis: The Legislative Budget Board fiscal note projects a net General Revenue cost of about $1.0 billion over 2026-27 rising to $3.07 billion in FY2028 and $3.98 billion in FY2030, partly offset by Foundation School Fund savings of $258 million (FY2028) to $806 million (FY2030). TEA's participation estimate assumes 175,000 current private-school students apply in FY2027 versus 24,500 public-school students leaving, i.e. most of the subsidy goes to students not switching schools.

contributions.title: Attorney General of Texas
contributions.summary: Served as the 50th attorney general of Texas from December 2, 2002 to January 5, 2015, the longest tenure in the office's history.

contributions.title: U.S. Representative for Montana's at-large district
contributions.summary: Won the 2017 special election and served in the U.S. House until January 3, 2021.

contributions.title: Constitutional carry bill
contributions.summary: Signed a constitutional carry firearms bill in his first weeks in office.

contributions.summary: Signed a ban on transgender athletes in girls' public school sports.

contributions.title: Ban on gender-affirming care for minors

contributions.summary: Became chair of the Republican Governors Association in November 2025.

contributions.summary: Served in the Michigan House from 2001 to 2006 and the Michigan Senate from 2006 to 2015, as Senate Minority Leader from 2011 to 2015.

contributions.title: Executive Order 1: Medicaid expansion implementation
contributions.summary: Signed her first executive order directing implementation of Medicaid expansion in Maine.
contributions.impactBasis: KFF's review of nearly 200 studies (Feb 2020-Mar 2021) found Medicaid expansion improved coverage, access, some mortality measures and individual financial stability, with the federal government paying 90% of costs. A Maine DHHS study (Rhodes, Maine Policy Review 2024) found Maine's 2019 expansion cut hospital uncompensated-care costs by 26% a year, about $126 million over 2020-21.

contributions.title: Conversion therapy ban for minors
contributions.summary: Signed a bill banning conversion therapy for minors, making Maine the 17th state to do so according to The Advocate.
contributions.reference: Signed May 29, 2019 (bill number not stated in source)

contributions.title: Attorney General of Maine
contributions.summary: Served as Maine Attorney General from January 2009 to January 2011 and again from January 2013 to January 2019.
contributions.reference: Maine Attorney General 2009-01-06 to 2011-01-06 and 2013-01-07 to 2019-01-02

contributions.title: Universal preschool and Department of Early Childhood (HB22-1295)
contributions.summary: Created the Colorado Department of Early Childhood and a statewide universal preschool program.
contributions.impactBasis: Colorado's program has no causal outcome evaluation yet (the state commissioned a process evaluation). The closest causal evidence is Gray-Lobe, Pathak and Walters (NBER WP 28756; QJE 2022), where lotteries into Boston's universal public preschool raised college attendance, SAT-taking and high-school graduation and reduced disciplinary incidents including juvenile incarceration, with no detectable effect on state test scores.

contributions.title: Standardized health benefit plan, the Colorado Option (HB21-1232)

contributions.title: AlphaGo

contributions.title: AlexNet

No significant change in homicide or overall suicide rates; firearm suicides among age 55+ fell 0.92 per 100,000 (CI -1.43 to -0.42), mainly in waiting-period states (-1.03) and not background-check-only states (-0.17). Measures the 1994 implementation only; authors note secondary-market effects untestable.

contributions.title: Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008

contributions.impactBasis: Berger and Roman (JFQA 2017): TARP was associated with higher net job creation and lower business and personal bankruptcies in local markets. Measures local real activity, not program cost or moral hazard; the literature on TARP and bank lending is mixed.

contributions.title: Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act of 2009

contributions.title: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009

contributions.impactBasis: IGM U.S. Economic Experts Panel, "Economic Stimulus (revisited)", 29 July 2014 (37 responses): 97% agreed or strongly agreed unemployment was lower at end-2010 than without the stimulus; 67.5% agreed that benefits would exceed costs, 27% were uncertain. An opinion survey, not an outcome estimate; CBO's model-based range for peak GDP effect was 0.7-4.1% at a cost of $836B vs $787B scored.

contributions.impactBasis: Bordo and Duca (NBER WP 24501, 2018): small-loan share of C&I lending fell about 9 points since 2010, which the authors attribute mostly to the post-enactment regulatory regime. A working paper measuring costs only, not the financial-stability benefit.

contributions.title: Economic Stimulus Act of 2008
contributions.summary: Sent tax rebate payments of up to $600 per person to most households, plus business expensing incentives, to boost demand in the 2008 downturn.
contributions.impactBasis: Parker, Souleles, Johnson and McClelland (NBER WP 16684; AER 2013) used Consumer Expenditure Survey questions and random payment timing: households spent about 12-30% of payments on nondurables within 3 months, 50-90% including durables (mainly vehicles); responses larger for older, lower-income, homeowning households. Measures household consumption only, not multiplier effects, lasting growth or fiscal cost.

contributions.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1)
contributions.summary: Signed budget reconciliation law that made the 2017 individual tax rates permanent, added deductions for tips and overtime, reduced Medicaid and SNAP spending, increased defense and border enforcement funding and raised the debt limit by $5 trillion.
contributions.impactBasis: CBO and JCT estimate Pub. L. 119-21 raises deficits by $3.4 trillion over 2025-2034 ($4.1 trillion with $718 billion of added debt service) and debt held by the public by 9.5 percentage points of GDP by 2034. CBO's distributional letter finds the lowest income decile loses about $1,200 a year (3.1% of income, mainly Medicaid and SNAP) while the top decile gains about $13,600 (2.7%); CBO's dynamic analysis of the House-passed version put real GDP about 0.5% higher on average over 2025-2034, driven by labor supply, investment and demand.

contributions.title: Regulating Imports with a Reciprocal Tariff

contributions.impactBasis: Yale Budget Lab (Nov. 2025) estimated the 2025 tariff package nets $2.3 trillion over 2026-35 (about half from the IEEPA tariffs), raises the price level 1.2% in the short run, and leaves long-run GDP 0.3% smaller (0.1% without IEEPA), with the lowest income decile bearing 2.4% of income versus 0.8% for the top decile. contributions.title: Professional profile and background
contributions.summary:
Alejandro Lopez-Lira is an assistant professor of finance at the University of Florida’s Warrington College of Business. His research studies asset pricing, machine learning and the use of language models in financial analysis. He earned finance graduate degrees at the University of Pennsylvania, completing his PhD in 2020.

With Yuehua Tang, he studied whether large language models could extract stock-return information from news headlines. He is also the author of The Predictive Edge, a book on generative AI and financial forecasting. On Autopilot, he designs portfolios published under Dr. Lira’s AI Finance Labs, including strategies using GPT and other language models. Model backtests, actual portfolio results and academic claims are separate types of evidence.

Travis Hoium is an investment analyst, writer and founder of Asymmetric Investing. Before his financial-writing career he worked as a mechanical engineer at 3M and founded a virtual-reality company. He holds a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering and an MBA from the University of Minnesota.

His writing for The Motley Fool has covered renewable energy, technology and growth businesses. The Autopilot portfolio is one public implementation of that research, rather than a guarantee of the targets in his newsletter.

matters.title: Senate resolution of censure over removal of federal deposits from the Bank of the United States
matters.summary: On March 28, 1834 the Senate voted 26 to 20 to adopt a resolution stating the president had assumed authority and power not conferred by the Constitution and laws. The Senate expunged the censure on January 16, 1837.
matters.penalty: Formal Senate censure resolution (expunged from the Journal by Senate order on 1837-01-16)

matters.title: Impeachment by the House and Senate trial (1868)
matters.summary: Impeached by the House in February 1868; the Senate trial began March 5. Votes on three articles fell one vote short of the two-thirds needed to convict, and the Senate acquitted him on May 26, 1868.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives / U.S. Senate

matters.title: FEC civil penalty against Obama 2008 presidential campaign for reporting violations (late/unfiled contribution reports)
matters.summary: Following an FEC audit, the 2008 Obama campaign committee agreed to a civil penalty for reporting violations involving roughly 1,300 donations totalling over $1.8 million.
matters.penalty: $375,000 civil penalty against the campaign committee (not Obama personally)

matters.title: FEC MUR 6127: personal-use allegations against Obama for America and Obama Victory Fund
matters.summary: The Commission dismissed the allegations against Obama Victory Fund and dismissed the personal-use allegations against Obama for America with letters of caution; civil penalties were agreed only by third-party vendors.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6127: OBAMA FOR AMERICA
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6127 ("OBAMA FOR AMERICA") named Barack Obama as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: FEC MUR 6035: NORTHERN TRUST COMPANY
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6035 ("NORTHERN TRUST COMPANY") named Barack Obama as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: House impeachment and Senate acquittal, 1998-1999
matters.summary: On 1998-12-19 the House adopted two articles of impeachment (H.Res. 611: the First Article 228-206 and the Third Article 221-212) and did not adopt two others. On 1999-02-12 the Senate voted 45 guilty-55 not guilty on the first article and 50-50 on the second; a two-thirds majority was required, so he was acquitted and remained in office.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives; U.S. Senate

matters.title: Civil contempt of court in Jones v. Clinton
matters.summary: U.S. District Judge Susan Webber Wright held Mr. Clinton in civil contempt (memorandum opinion of 1999-04-12) for false and misleading testimony in his January 1998 deposition in the Paula Jones case, and referred the matter to the Arkansas Supreme Court's Committee on Professional Conduct. On 1999-07-29 she ordered him to pay $90,686 in sanctions and expenses; the 2001 Arkansas agreed order records that he paid over $90,000.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Arkansas

matters.title: Paula Jones civil suit settled
matters.summary: Paula Jones's sexual-harassment suit against Mr. Clinton was dismissed by the district court, Jones appealed, and the case was settled on 1998-11-13 for $850,000 while the appeal was pending.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Arkansas; U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
matters.penalty: $850,000 settlement

matters.title: Supreme Court bar suspension; resignation from the bar
matters.summary: On 2001-10-01 the Supreme Court of the United States suspended Mr. Clinton from practice before it and issued a rule returnable in 40 days requiring him to show cause why he should not be disbarred. His lawyer announced on 2001-11-09 that he had resigned from the Court's bar.
matters.authority: Supreme Court of the United States
matters.penalty: Suspended from practice before the Supreme Court; resigned from its bar

matters.title: Whitewater / Madison Guaranty independent counsel investigation
matters.summary: The Office of Independent Counsel (established 1994-08-05 to continue the regulatory counsel's work) investigated whether President and Mrs. Clinton knowingly participated in criminal conduct related to Madison Guaranty, Capital Management Services and the Whitewater Development Corporation. On 2000-09-20 Independent Counsel Robert Ray announced that the evidence was insufficient to prove to a jury beyond a reasonable doubt that either did so, and closed the investigation of those matters.
matters.authority: Office of Independent Counsel (Robert W. Ray)

matters.title: Impeached by the House (Articles I and III of H.Res. 611: grand jury perjury, obstruction of justice)
matters.summary: The House adopted the first article by 228-206 and the third article by 221-212 on 19 December 1998 (House Clerk roll calls 543 and 545).

matters.title: Senate impeachment trial: acquitted on both articles
matters.summary: On 12 February 1999 the Senate voted 45 guilty-55 not guilty on Article I and 50-50 on Article II; two-thirds was required, so he was acquitted and remained in office.

matters.title: Civil contempt in Jones v. Clinton and sanctions
matters.summary: Judge Wright held Clinton in civil contempt for willfully false testimony in his Jones deposition and on 29 July 1999 imposed fines/expenses. Court opinion text itself was not retrievable; contempt date from secondary reports.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Arkansas (Judge Susan Webber Wright)
matters.penalty: $90,686 in fees and expenses ordered paid, plus $1,202 for the judge's travel (per CBS News report)

matters.title: Hayes-era commission investigation of the New York Custom House under Collector Arthur
matters.summary: A commission appointed by President Hayes examined the New York Custom House. It reported patronage-driven appointments, salary kickbacks and overstaffing. The Miller Center states there is no evidence Arthur took bribes personally, and that he routinely collected salary assessments from employees for the Conkling party machine.
matters.authority: Special commission appointed by President Rutherford B. Hayes; Arthur suspended as Collector in 1878
matters.penalty: Suspended and replaced as Collector of the Port of New York (1878); no criminal or civil charge found

matters.title: New York Attorney General civil fraud action against Donald Trump and the Trump Organization
matters.summary: The New York Attorney General sued in September 2022 under Executive Law 63(12). After a bench trial, Justice Arthur Engoron ruled in February 2024 that the defendants were liable and ordered more than $450 million in disgorgement and pre-judgment interest plus a three-year bar on Trump serving as an officer or director of a New York company. On 21 August 2025 the Appellate Division, First Department, vacated the disgorgement award as an excessive fine under the Eighth Amendment, upheld the injunctive relief, and the justices were divided on the liability findings. Both sides appealed to the New York Court of Appeals; Trump's brief was filed in April 2026 and the State's was due 23 June 2026; no Court of Appeals decision was located as of the verification date.
matters.authority: Supreme Court of New York, New York County (Justice Engoron); Appellate Division, First Department; Court of Appeals (appeal pending)
matters.penalty: February 2024 money judgment of more than $450 million vacated on 21 August 2025; three-year officer/director bar and other injunctive relief upheld

matters.title: New York County criminal case: falsifying business records (People v. Trump)
matters.summary: Indicted by the Manhattan District Attorney on 34 counts of falsifying business records in the first degree (announced 4 April 2023). A jury convicted on all 34 counts on 30 May 2024; Justice Juan Merchan sentenced him on 10 January 2025 to an unconditional discharge. The appeal is pending before the Appellate Division, First Department (the District Attorney filed its response on 29 July 2026). Separately, the Second Circuit in November 2025 told the federal district court to reconsider removal; Judge Alvin Hellerstein again denied removal on 28 August 2026 (his third denial) and Trump's lawyers said they would appeal.
matters.authority: New York Supreme Court, New York County (Justice Merchan); Appellate Division, First Department (appeal pending); U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. (removal)
matters.penalty: Unconditional discharge (sentence of 10 January 2025)

matters.title: E. Jean Carroll v. Trump (2022 action): jury verdict for sexual abuse and defamation
matters.summary: In May 2023 a federal jury in the Southern District of New York found Trump liable for sexually abusing and later defaming E. Jean Carroll and awarded $5 million; judgment was entered 11 May 2023. The Second Circuit affirmed on 30 December 2024 (rehearing en banc denied 13 June 2025). The Supreme Court denied certiorari on 29 June 2026 and denied rehearing on 17 August 2026.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y.; U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit; U.S. Supreme Court (No. 25-573)
matters.penalty: $5 million jury award

matters.title: E. Jean Carroll v. Trump (2019 action): jury award for defamation
matters.summary: Carroll sued in November 2019 over statements Trump made in June 2019. After the 2023 verdict in her second action, the district court granted partial summary judgment on liability, and on 26 January 2024 a jury awarded $83.3 million ($18.3 million compensatory, $65 million punitive). The Second Circuit affirmed on 8 September 2025 and denied rehearing en banc on 29 April 2026. Trump's certiorari petition (No. 26-141) was filed 28 July 2026 and is pending; the response is due 30 October 2026.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y.; U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit; U.S. Supreme Court (No. 26-141, pending)
matters.penalty: $83.3 million jury award

matters.title: Trump v. Clinton: Rule 11 sanctions for a dismissed lawsuit
matters.summary: Trump's 2022 suit against Hillary Clinton and others in S.D. Fla. was dismissed in September 2022. On 19 January 2023 Judge Donald Middlebrooks imposed sanctions of about $938,000 on Trump and his attorneys, writing that the suit was frivolous and brought in bad faith for an improper purpose. Trump appealed; the Eleventh Circuit decided the appeal in a published opinion in 2025 (reported at 161 F.4th 671), described in secondary sources as rejecting the appeal.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, S.D. Fla. (Judge Middlebrooks); Eleventh Circuit
matters.penalty: About $938,000 in sanctions (figure varies slightly by report)

matters.title: Federal election-subversion prosecution (United States v. Trump, D.D.C.)
matters.summary: Special Counsel Jack Smith's office filed a four-count indictment on 1 August 2023 concerning efforts to overturn the 2020 election results; Trump pleaded not guilty. After the 2024 election the Government moved to dismiss under Justice Department policy on prosecuting a sitting president, and on 25 November 2024 Judge Tanya Chutkan granted the unopposed motion and dismissed the superseding indictment without prejudice.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, District of Columbia (Judge Chutkan)

matters.title: Federal classified-documents prosecution (United States v. Trump, S.D. Fla.)
matters.summary: Trump was indicted in 2023 on 40 counts relating to retention of classified documents after leaving office and obstruction of efforts to retrieve them; he pleaded not guilty. On 15 July 2024 Judge Aileen Cannon dismissed the indictment, ruling the Special Counsel's appointment unconstitutional. The Special Counsel appealed and then dropped the appeal as to Trump after the November 2024 election; the Eleventh Circuit dismissed the remaining appeal as to the co-defendants on 11 February 2025.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, S.D. Fla. (Judge Cannon); Eleventh Circuit

matters.title: Fulton County, Georgia racketeering prosecution over the 2020 election
matters.summary: A Fulton County grand jury indicted Trump and 18 others in August 2023 under Georgia's racketeering statute over efforts to overturn the 2020 election result in Georgia; Trump pleaded not guilty. After the original prosecutor was disqualified, the successor prosecutor Peter Skandalakis moved to dismiss, and on 26 November 2025 Judge Scott McAfee dismissed the case in its entirety.
matters.authority: Superior Court of Fulton County, Georgia (Judge McAfee)

matters.title: First House impeachment and Senate trial (2019-2020)
matters.summary: On 18 December 2019 the House of Representatives agreed to Article I (abuse of power, 230-197) and Article II (obstruction of Congress, 229-198). On 5 February 2020 the Senate voted 48-52 on Article I and 47-53 on Article II, finding him not guilty on both.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives; U.S. Senate

matters.title: Second House impeachment and Senate trial (2021)
matters.summary: On 13 January 2021 the House of Representatives impeached him 232-197 on a single article of impeachment. On 13 February 2021 the Senate voted 57 guilty to 43 not guilty, short of the two-thirds required, and he was acquitted.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives; U.S. Senate

matters.title: Civil contempt in the New York Attorney General's subpoena enforcement
matters.summary: On 25 April 2022 Justice Arthur Engoron held Trump in civil contempt for failing to comply with the Attorney General's subpoena and imposed $10,000 per day. On 11 May 2022 the court set conditions for purging the contempt including payment of $110,000 to the Attorney General. On 14 February 2023 the Appellate Division, First Department, upheld the contempt fine.
matters.authority: Supreme Court of New York, New York County (Justice Engoron); Appellate Division, First Department
matters.penalty: $110,000 contempt fine

matters.title: Criminal contempt of the gag order in the New York hush-money trial
matters.summary: On 30 April 2024 Justice Juan Merchan found Trump in criminal contempt for nine violations of his 26 March 2024 gag order and fined him $1,000 per violation ($9,000). On 6 May 2024 the court found a further violation and fined him another $1,000, for a cumulative $10,000.
matters.authority: Supreme Court of New York, New York County (Justice Merchan)
matters.penalty: $10,000 in total ($1,000 per violation)

matters.title: Donald J. Trump Foundation action by the New York Attorney General
matters.summary: The Attorney General sued the Foundation and its directors in June 2018. In November 2019 the New York Supreme Court (Justice Saliann Scarpulla) ordered Trump to pay $2 million in damages under settlements in which he admitted misusing Foundation funds; the Foundation dissolved under court supervision in December 2018 and its remaining assets went to charities.
matters.authority: Supreme Court of New York, New York County (Justice Scarpulla); New York Attorney General
matters.penalty: $2 million in damages paid to charities

matters.title: Trump University lawsuits (New York Attorney General and two federal class actions)
matters.summary: The New York Attorney General and two class actions in San Diego alleged Trump University misled students. On 18 November 2016 a $25 million settlement of the three actions was announced with no admission of wrongdoing, including about $4 million for the State's case. U.S. District Judge Gonzalo Curiel gave final approval on 31 March 2017.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, S.D. Cal. (Judge Curiel); New York Attorney General
matters.penalty: $25 million total settlement

matters.title: First impeachment by the House (abuse of power; obstruction of Congress), acquitted by the Senate
matters.summary: The House impeached on two articles, abuse of power and obstruction of Congress (H. Res. 755). The Senate trial ran January 16 to February 5, 2020, and ended in acquittal.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives / U.S. Senate

matters.title: Second impeachment by the House (incitement of insurrection), acquitted by the Senate
matters.summary: The House impeached on one article, incitement of insurrection (H. Res. 24). The Senate trial ran February 9 to 13, 2021, and ended in acquittal.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives / U.S. Senate

matters.title: New York criminal case: 34 counts of falsifying business records
matters.summary: A New York State Supreme Court jury convicted on 34 counts of falsifying business records in the first degree, per the District Attorney's release of May 30, 2024. Sentence and appeal status were not confirmed from a fetched official page.
matters.authority: New York County District Attorney / New York State Supreme Court
matters.penalty: Sentencing not confirmed from a fetched official page

matters.title: New York Attorney General civil fraud judgment
matters.summary: The court ruled for the Attorney General and ordered the defendants to pay over $450 million, with officer/director and loan bans. The Attorney General later reported that the First Department affirmed liability on August 21, 2025; further review status was not confirmed.
matters.authority: New York State Supreme Court (Justice Engoron), action by NY Attorney General
matters.penalty: Over $450 million in total, including $363.8 million disgorgement and pre-judgment interest; 3-year officer/director ban; 3-year bar on New York bank loans
