matters.title: Iran-Contra independent counsel investigation of Bush's knowledge as Vice President
matters.summary: The independent counsel investigated Bush's knowledge of the Iran-Contra affair, including late-disclosed diary notes. No charges were filed; the final report states no grand jury subpoena was sought because a prosecution was not considered likely, and that the statute of limitations had passed on most relevant acts.

matters.title: 1976 Maine operating-under-the-influence charge
matters.summary: In 1976 Mr. Bush was arrested near Kennebunkport, Maine, for driving under the influence of alcohol, a Class D misdemeanor. According to the 2000-11-02 report, he pleaded guilty, paid a $150 fine and his Maine driving privileges were temporarily suspended; the arrest became public in November 2000.
matters.penalty: $150 fine; temporary suspension of Maine driving privileges

matters.title: Watergate special prosecutor inquiry into allegation that union contributions were diverted to Ford's personal use
matters.summary: In 1976 an unidentified informant told the FBI that Ford had misused union political contributions. The matter went to the Watergate special prosecutor. TIME reported nobody was charged, Ford denied it, and the FBI had found no substantiation. A Ford Library document index is said to include an October 13, 1976 closing letter finding no violation of law, but the scanned letter could not be read, so the closure is not verified here.

matters.title: Credit Mobilier stock inquiry (Poland Committee)
matters.summary: Garfield was named by Oakes Ames among members offered Credit Mobilier stock and testified before the House committee in January 1873. The committee's February 1873 report found he had bought 10 shares and received $329 in dividends but judged him innocent of wrongdoing; no sanction followed.

matters.title: House select committee inquiry into alleged improper influence on Congress (Covode Committee)
matters.summary: On March 5, 1860 the House created a select committee to examine whether the President had used money, patronage or other improper means to influence Congress. Buchanan sent a formal protest on March 28, 1860 objecting to the inquiry. No impeachment followed.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives (Select Committee to Investigate Alleged Corruptions in Government)

matters.title: Congressional inquiries into the White House furniture fund and Monroe's accounts
matters.summary: Two inconclusive House inquiries in 1822 and 1823 examined the White House furniture fund, managed by an official later found to be in arrears. Monroe requested a full inquiry, authorized in 1825; no deficiencies in the fund were found and the House issued no findings.

matters.title: Special counsel inquiry into National Bank of Georgia loans to the Carter peanut warehouse
matters.summary: Attorney General Griffin Bell appointed a special counsel in March 1979 to examine whether bank loans to the Carter family warehouse business were diverted to the 1976 campaign. The counsel concluded in October 1979 that no money had been diverted and no criminal charges were brought; the report remains sealed.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Justice (special counsel Paul J. Curran)

matters.title: Committee for Jimmy Carter v. FEC (matching-funds certification dispute)
matters.summary: The 1976 primary campaign committee sued after the FEC certified $88,293.92 of $185,749 in requested matching funds. The case settled with the FEC certifying $65,650.01 for qualified legal expenses; the committee agreed to request no further funds and terminate.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court for D.C. / Federal Election Commission

matters.title: Special Counsel investigation of retained classified documents
matters.summary: Attorney General Garland appointed Robert K. Hur as Special Counsel on 2023-01-12 to investigate classified documents found at the Penn Biden Center and Mr. Biden's Delaware residence. The Special Counsel's report dated 2024-02-05 concluded that 'no criminal charges are warranted' and that the evidence 'does not establish Mr. Biden's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt'; it states the same conclusion would apply absent Department of Justice policy on a sitting president.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Justice, Special Counsel's Office (Robert K. Hur)

matters.title: House censure motion over Haverhill disunion petition
matters.summary: Southern members introduced resolutions to censure Representative Adams after he presented a petition seeking dissolution of the Union; the House voted 106 to 93 to table the censure motion on 7 February 1842, ending the effort.

matters.title: House impeachment resolution (Botts) 1843
matters.summary: Rep. John M. Botts introduced an impeachment resolution proposing a nine-member investigating committee. A motion to table failed 104-119, and the House then rejected the resolution 84 to 127. Hinds' Precedents gives no separate date for the votes.

matters.title: Watergate: named unindicted co-conspirator by federal grand jury
matters.summary: In March 1974 the grand jury named Nixon an unindicted co-conspirator because Special Prosecutor Jaworski advised that a sitting President could not be indicted. He was not charged.
matters.authority: Watergate grand jury / Special Prosecutor Leon Jaworski

matters.title: House Judiciary Committee articles of impeachment (Watergate)
matters.summary: The committee drew up five articles of impeachment and approved three in summer 1974. Nixon resigned the presidency on 9 August 1974; the House never voted on the articles.

matters.title: Presidential pardon by Gerald Ford (Proclamation 4311)
matters.summary: Ford granted Nixon a full, free and absolute pardon for all federal offenses committed or possibly committed from 20 January 1969 through 9 August 1974.

matters.title: Joint Committee on Internal Revenue Taxation review of Nixon's tax returns
matters.summary: A 1974 review of Nixon's returns, including a deduction for donated pre-presidential papers, found a deficiency of about $476,431 in taxes and interest. Nixon said he would make good on it.
matters.authority: Joint Committee on Internal Revenue Taxation / IRS
matters.penalty: About $476,431 in claimed unpaid taxes and interest per the Joint Committee staff

matters.title: Iran-Contra independent counsel investigation (Walsh)
matters.summary: The final report found no credible evidence that Reagan violated any criminal statute and could not prove he authorized or knew of the diversion; it said he set the stage for others' illegal activities. He was not charged.
matters.authority: Office of Independent Counsel Lawrence E. Walsh

matters.title: Barnes v. Roosevelt libel suit
matters.summary: New York Republican leader William Barnes sued Roosevelt for $50,000 over a statement calling him a corrupt political boss. The trial began April 19, 1915 in Syracuse; the jury returned a unanimous verdict for Roosevelt, the defendant. This was a civil case in which Roosevelt was the defendant (verdict for defendant).
matters.authority: Onondaga County Supreme Court, Syracuse, New York (civil)

matters.title: Livingston v. Jefferson (Batture Sainte Marie trespass suit)
matters.summary: Edward Livingston sued Jefferson personally for trespass over federal seizure of land at New Orleans ordered during his presidency. Chief Justice Marshall and Judge Tyler dismissed it in 1811 on local-action (jurisdiction) grounds, without a ruling on the merits. Filed date is year only (1810).
matters.authority: U.S. Circuit Court for the District of Virginia (civil)

matters.title: Murder indictments after the 1804 duel with Alexander Hamilton
matters.summary: Burr was indicted for murder in New York and New Jersey after the July 1804 duel in which Alexander Hamilton was fatally wounded. He never stood trial on either indictment.
matters.authority: New York and New Jersey grand juries

matters.title: Treason trial in Richmond, Virginia (1807)
matters.summary: Burr was tried for treason in connection with his alleged western expedition. The trial ran August 3 to September 1, 1807, and the jury returned a not-proved verdict on September 1, 1807.
matters.authority: U.S. Circuit Court, Richmond, Virginia (Chief Justice John Marshall presiding)

matters.title: Attorney General declines independent counsel for 1996 fund-raising activities
matters.summary: Attorney General Janet Reno announced on 1997-12-02 that she would not appoint an independent counsel to investigate fund-raising activities by President Clinton and Vice President Gore, saying under the statute as written she 'had no alternative'.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Justice (Attorney General Janet Reno)

matters.title: Settlement of Tompkins's War of 1812 wartime accounts with the United States
matters.summary: Treasury accounting officers reported a balance of $35,190 in Tompkins's favor on his wartime advances as New York governor; President Monroe reconsidered and in April 1824 put the balance due to him at $60,238.46, leaving to Congress the question of interest on his commission. The record concerns a disputed account settlement in which the balance was found owing to Tompkins.
matters.authority: U.S. Treasury accounting officers; President Monroe; U.S. Congress

matters.title: Nigerian bribery charges over Bonny Island LNG joint venture
matters.summary: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission charged Mr. Cheney, eight others and Halliburton in December 2010 in connection with an alleged cash-for-contract scheme involving a four-company joint venture building a liquefied natural gas plant on Bonny Island. Nigeria announced in December 2010 that it had dropped the charges in exchange for $250 million; Mr. Cheney's lawyer called the allegations 'entirely baseless' and said the U.S. Justice Department and SEC had found no impropriety by him as Halliburton's CEO.
matters.authority: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, Federal Republic of Nigeria

matters.title: Crédit Mobilier scandal: Senate (Morrill) committee inquiry into Wilson's dealings with Oakes Ames
matters.summary: A Senate committee examined Wilson's dealings with Crédit Mobilier promoter Oakes Ames. It found the dealings did not benefit or taint him, but mildly reprimanded him for vehemently and erroneously insisting he had known nothing of the company.
matters.penalty: Mild reprimand in the committee report; no expulsion or other sanction recommended

matters.title: FEC MUR 7998 (complaint naming Fox News, JD Vance for Senate, Ohioans for JD, Protect Ohio Values PAC)
matters.summary: The FEC voted 6-0 to dismiss the complaint as an exercise of prosecutorial discretion and close the file; no penalty was assessed.
matters.penalty: None assessed

matters.title: FEC MUR 8009 (alleged in-kind contributions from Protect Ohio Values PAC to JD Vance for Senate)
matters.summary: The Commission failed 1-5 to find reason to believe, then voted 5-1 to dismiss all four allegations (Deep Root Analytics services and Medium posts); recorded as Dismissed-Other. Certification date not stated on the page (General Counsel report dated 2024-03-18).
matters.penalty: None

matters.title: Expulsion from the U.S. Senate for joining the Confederacy
matters.summary: The Senate expelled Breckinridge on the finding that he had joined the enemies of the country and was in arms against the government after accepting a Confederate army commission.
matters.penalty: Expelled from the Senate by a 36-0 vote

matters.title: Expelled from the U.S. Senate
matters.summary: The Senate voted 36 to 0 on December 4, 1861 to expel Breckinridge for support of the Confederate rebellion, after he had left Washington and accepted a Confederate commission.
matters.penalty: Expelled from the Senate

matters.title: House investigation of Calhoun's conduct as Secretary of War (Elijah Mix contract)
matters.summary: At Calhoun's own request the House granted an investigation of allegations connected to the Elijah Mix contract during his time as Secretary of War. The outcome is not stated on the cited page; secondary descriptions say the committee report of 13 Feb 1827 cleared him, but that was not verified from a fetched primary source.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives select committee (19th Congress)

matters.title: FEC MUR 7582: CANDIDE GROUP, LLC
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 7582 ("CANDIDE GROUP, LLC") named Kamala Harris as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: Justice Department review of classified documents found at his Indiana home
matters.summary: After about a dozen documents marked classified were found at his Indiana home in January 2023 and turned over to the FBI, the FBI and the Justice Department's National Security Division investigated their handling. A Justice Department letter to his attorney, reported 2023-06-02, stated that 'no criminal charges will be sought'.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Justice (FBI and National Security Division)

matters.title: Senate Rules Committee review of vice-presidential nomination and personal gifts to aides and associates
matters.summary: Disclosures in 1974 of large personal gifts and loans to officials and associates prompted questions during Senate confirmation hearings. The Rules Committee issued its report on 3 Dec 1974 and unanimously reported out the nomination; Rockefeller pledged no such gifts in future except to help friends in extreme need.
matters.authority: U.S. Senate Committee on Rules and Administration

matters.title: Crédit Mobilier scandal: House select committee inquiry into stock and dividend payments
matters.summary: Colfax appeared before the House select committee in January 1873 after allegations that Oakes Ames had given him Crédit Mobilier stock. Documents showed a $1,200 check from Ames. Colfax said he had not bought the stock. No formal finding of guilt or innocence was made.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives (Poland select committee; Judiciary Committee)
matters.penalty: None. No formal adjudication; the House Judiciary Committee did not proceed on an impeachment resolution and his term ended in March 1873.

matters.title: Federal income tax evasion charge; nolo contendere plea and resignation as Vice President
matters.summary: On 10 October 1973 Agnew pleaded nolo contendere to one count of income tax evasion in federal court, was sentenced to three years of probation and fined $10,000, and resigned as Vice President the same day.
matters.penalty: Three years of probation and a $10,000 fine; resigned as Vice President

matters.title: Disbarment by Maryland Court of Appeals
matters.summary: The Maryland Court of Appeals disbarred Agnew on 2 May 1974.
matters.penalty: Disbarred

matters.title: Maryland civil suit over kickbacks received while in state office
matters.summary: After a four-day civil trial the judge ruled that Agnew violated his public trust and fiduciary duties to Maryland and must repay the state $248,735.
matters.authority: Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County, Maryland (Judge Bruce Williams)
matters.penalty: Ordered to repay $248,735 (kickbacks plus interest) to the state of Maryland

matters.title: Federal income tax evasion charge; nolo contendere plea and resignation
matters.summary: Agnew entered a plea of nolo contendere to a tax evasion count after a federal investigation in Baltimore; the judge described the plea as the full equivalent of a guilty plea. He resigned the vice presidency the same day.
matters.authority: U.S. District Court, District of Maryland (Judge Walter E. Hoffman); U.S. Department of Justice
matters.penalty: Three years probation and a $10,000 fine; resigned the vice presidency

matters.title: 1984 presidential primary delegate-committee / excess labor contributions (FEC enforcement)
matters.summary: The Mondale presidential campaign agreed with the FEC to return $379,640 to the Treasury and pay a civil fine of $18,500 over excess union contributions in the 1984 Democratic primaries. Related FEC matter MUR 1722 (delegate committees; respondents include Mondale for President Committee) was opened 4 June 1984 and closed 3 December 1984.
matters.penalty: Return $379,640 to the Treasury and pay a $18,500 civil fine (campaign committee)

matters.title: House impeachment articles; Senate dismissal without trial
matters.summary: The House adopted H.Res.863 impeaching Mayorkas, then Secretary of Homeland Security, on February 13, 2024 by 214-213. On April 17, 2024 the Senate sustained points of order that the two articles did not allege impeachable offenses (Article II point of order sustained 51-49) and voted 51-49 to adjourn the Court of Impeachment sine die; no trial was held.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives; U.S. Senate

matters.title: DHS Inspector General review of EB-5 visa program actions while USCIS Director
matters.summary: The DHS Office of Inspector General investigated whether Mayorkas, then Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, gave special treatment to politically connected applicants in the EB-5 investor visa program. Its report, publicly released and reported March 24, 2015, found that his communications with outside stakeholders, combined with favorable actions that departed from the regulatory framework, created 'an appearance of favoritism and special access'; it took no position on whether his decisions were wise and did not establish his motives.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General

matters.title: Rhode Island Ethics Commission complaint over IGT contract extension
matters.summary: A Rhode Island Republican Party complaint alleged the governor's handling of an IGT lottery contract extension violated the state ethics code. In August 2019 the commission dismissed one claim and investigated another; in April 2020 it voted 7-1 that probable cause of a knowing and willful violation did not exist and dismissed the complaint.

matters.title: FBI investigation of personal e-mail system used as Secretary of State
matters.summary: On 5 July 2016 FBI Director James Comey stated the FBI was referring its investigation to the Department of Justice and expressed the view that no charges were appropriate. On 6 November 2016 Comey wrote to Congress that a review of additional e-mails had not changed the FBI's July conclusions. No charges were filed.
matters.authority: Federal Bureau of Investigation / U.S. Department of Justice

matters.title: Independent counsel Whitewater investigation
matters.summary: An independent counsel investigation of the Clintons' Arkansas business dealings, begun in 1994, ended with a final report released 20 March 2002 by Independent Counsel Robert Ray stating there was not enough evidence to charge Hillary Clinton with any crime. The report said evidence was insufficient to prove to a jury beyond a reasonable doubt that either Clinton committed a criminal offense.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6932: HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6932 ("HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: FEC MUR 6015: HILLARY CLINTON FOR PRESIDENT
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6015 ("HILLARY CLINTON FOR PRESIDENT") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 5995: HILLARY CLINTON FOR PRESIDENT
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 5995 ("HILLARY CLINTON FOR PRESIDENT") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 5987: HILLARY CLINTON FOR PRESIDENT
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 5987 ("HILLARY CLINTON FOR PRESIDENT") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 5225: HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR US SENATE COMMITTEE
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 5225 ("HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR US SENATE COMMITTEE") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 5185: HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR US SENATE COMMITTEE
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 5185 ("HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR US SENATE COMMITTEE") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 4960: HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR US SENATE EXPLORATORY COMMITTEE, INC.
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 4960 ("HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR US SENATE EXPLORATORY COMMITTEE, INC.") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 4926: HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR U.S. SENATE EXPLORATORY COMMITTEE
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 4926 ("HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON FOR U.S. SENATE EXPLORATORY COMMITTEE") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 4924: HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 4924 ("HILLARY RODHAM CLINTON") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 4911: WILLIAM JEFFERSON CLINTON
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 4911 ("WILLIAM JEFFERSON CLINTON") named Hillary Clinton as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: Allegation of false statements in 2017 confirmation hearing testimony (Special Counsel's Office)
matters.summary: Sessions's lawyer stated on 21 March 2018 that the Special Counsel's Office told him Sessions was not under investigation for false statements or perjury in his confirmation hearing testimony. The statement is relayed by his counsel, not an official release.
matters.authority: Special Counsel's Office (as relayed by Sessions's attorney)

matters.title: FEC MUR 6021: DNC & KERRY FOR PRESIDENT 2004 INC.
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6021 ("DNC & KERRY FOR PRESIDENT 2004 INC.") named John Kerry as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 6822: complaint against Ratcliffe for Congress (reporting/contribution limits)
matters.summary: A complaint alleged contribution-limit and reporting violations by Ratcliffe for Congress, its treasurer and another respondent. The Commission voted 5-1 to dismiss the allegations and closed the file.

matters.title: Justice Department inquiry into 2020 stock sales
matters.summary: The Justice Department reviewed stock transactions by Sen. Loeffler and her husband made in early 2020 around the coronavirus briefings. The AP reported on May 26, 2020 that she was notified she was no longer under investigation; her spokesman said she did nothing wrong.

matters.title: Senate Ethics Committee complaint over 2020 stock trades
matters.summary: Complaints by Common Cause and Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington were filed in late March 2020. On June 16, 2020 the Committee told Sen. Loeffler it did not find evidence that her actions violated federal law, Senate Rules, or standards of conduct and dismissed the matter.
matters.authority: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics

matters.title: Legislative audit committee finding on daughter's appraiser licence
matters.summary: The legislative committee's report found Noem's daughter received preferential treatment in obtaining her real estate appraiser licence after the governor's office became involved. Noem denied wrongdoing.
matters.authority: South Dakota Legislature, Government Operations and Audit Committee

matters.title: Government Accountability Board complaint over daughter's appraiser licence
matters.summary: The state ethics board found sufficient information that Noem may have engaged in misconduct when intervening in her daughter's application; it said appropriate action could be taken but did not specify it. Final disposition was not confirmed in sources read.

matters.title: State aircraft use complaint
matters.summary: A complaint alleging personal and political use of state aircraft was dismissed by the board, which said 'state business' lacked a legal definition and that defining it was the Legislature's responsibility.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6985: transfers between state and federal committees
matters.summary: The Commission found reason to believe in March 2017 that Zeldin violated 52 U.S.C. 30125(e)(1)(B) over transfers to state and local committees; the matter was ultimately resolved as 'Dismissed-Other' with no penalty.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6985: LEE ZELDIN
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6985 ("LEE ZELDIN") named Lee Zeldin as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: FEC MUR 6439: alleged coordination between WWE and 2010 Senate campaign
matters.summary: The Connecticut Democratic State Central Committee filed a complaint with the FEC (received December 6, 2010) alleging that WWE's promotional activities were coordinated with Linda McMahon's 2010 Senate campaign. McMahon, her committee, Vince McMahon and WWE were respondents. On September 13, 2011 the Commission voted 6-0 to close the file, finding no reason to believe as to most allegations and dismissing the remaining Make-A-Wish ad allegations as a matter of prosecutorial discretion.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6586: complaint over WWE letter to newspaper columnists
matters.summary: A May 31, 2012 complaint to the FEC alleged that WWE was providing corporate assistance to Linda McMahon's 2012 Senate candidacy through a letter threatening a libel suit over newspaper commentaries. McMahon, her committee and WWE were respondents. The Commission voted 5-0 to find no reason to believe any respondent violated the Act and closed the file; closure was certified December 17, 2013.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6586: LINDA MCMAHON FOR SENATE 2012 INC
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6586 ("LINDA MCMAHON FOR SENATE 2012 INC") named Linda McMahon as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 6439: LINDA MCMAHON FOR SENATE 2010, ET AL
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6439 ("LINDA MCMAHON FOR SENATE 2010, ET AL") named Linda McMahon as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: DoD Inspector General review of Secretary of Defense hospitalizations and notification of duties transfer
matters.summary: The Inspector General reviewed how functions and duties were handled during Austin's December 2023, January 2024 and February 2024 hospitalizations. It found no adverse consequences to DoD operations but said risks to national defense were increased unnecessarily, found Congress and the White House were not notified in a timely manner, and made 20 recommendations. Austin was not charged or sanctioned.

matters.title: DoD Inspector General evaluation of the handling of Secretary Austin's 2023-2024 hospitalizations and delegation of authority
matters.summary: The DoD Inspector General found no adverse consequences to Defense Department operations but concluded that risks to national defense were unnecessarily increased. It found that notification of the Deputy Secretary, Congress and the White House was not timely and made 20 recommendations, including defining 'medically incapacitated'.
matters.authority: Department of Defense Office of Inspector General

matters.title: Labor Department OIG investigation of conduct while Secretary of Labor
matters.summary: The DOL Office of Inspector General opened an investigation on January 6, 2026 after an anonymous complaint. Its September 3, 2026 report concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed she failed to comply with DOL policy prohibiting workplace harassment, developed an inappropriately close and unprofessional relationship with a member of her protective detail (the OIG did not conclude a romantic or sexual relationship was established), combined personal and official travel inconsistently with travel regulations, possessed alcohol on federal property without authorization, directed employees to perform personal tasks, and failed to report gifts. She resigned on April 20, 2026, the day before a scheduled OIG interview, and was not interviewed; the report was provided to the Acting Secretary.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General

matters.title: Florida Commission on Ethics complaint over party credit card and employment
matters.summary: A 2010 complaint to the Florida Commission on Ethics alleged that Rubio, then Speaker of the Florida House, misused a Republican Party of Florida credit card for personal expenses and used his position to obtain employment. The Commission dismissed the complaint on July 27, 2012.

matters.title: Florida Commission on Ethics complaint over state party credit card use and job referrals
matters.summary: The Florida Commission on Ethics dismissed a 2010 complaint filed by a Democratic donor alleging misuse of a state party credit card and use of position to obtain jobs for himself.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6888: REPUBLICAN NATIONAL COMMITTEE, ETAL
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6888 ("REPUBLICAN NATIONAL COMMITTEE, ETAL") named Marco Rubio as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: House Ethics Committee review of outside income and endorsements by family businesses
matters.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics referred allegations on Dec. 23, 2013 that Rep. Mullin endorsed goods or services of companies he or his family owned, received outside earned income above limits and served as a director or officer of those companies for compensation. The Committee announced an investigation on Mar. 24, 2014. Its Aug. 10, 2018 report found he made a good faith effort to seek the Committee's guidance and substantially complied with it, found that an accounting error led to $40,000 being received contrary to its advice, required that the $40,000 be returned to the company, and took no further action.

matters.title: Committee adopted a report and took no further action on his dealings with his family businesses; matter closed on publication and repayment.
matters.summary: Official record: Statement of the Chairwoman and Ranking Member of the Committee on Ethics Regarding Representative Markwayne Mullin
matters.penalty: Repayment of $40,000 to Mullin Plumbing West Division

matters.title: OCE referral 13-2392: In 2013, Representative Markwayne Mullin regularly hosted a weekly radio talk show and appeared in numerous radio, television, and internet commercial
matters.summary: In 2013, Representative Markwayne Mullin regularly hosted a weekly radio talk show and appeared in numerous radio, television, and internet commercials for Mullin Plumbing, Inc. and affiliated companies. Committee action: Committee Report Issued Finding Violation with Sanctions (initial: 18A (Unresolved)).

matters.title: House Ethics Committee review of outside business income and endorsements (Mullin Plumbing)
matters.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics referred allegations about outside earned income, endorsements and compensated board roles tied to his family plumbing business. The Committee found he made good-faith efforts to seek its guidance and substantially complied, did not fully follow part of the advice because of an accounting error, directed repayment of $40,000, and closed the matter.
matters.penalty: Required to repay $40,000 to his family business (Mullin West) that was paid to him in 2013

matters.title: FEC MUR 7978: Mullin for America
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 7978 ("Mullin for America") named Markwayne Mullin as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: FEC MUR 6542: MULLIN FOR CONGRESS
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6542 ("MULLIN FOR CONGRESS") named Markwayne Mullin as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: House of Representatives holds Attorney General Garland in contempt of Congress over Hur interview audio recordings
matters.summary: On 12 June 2024 the House voted 216-207 to hold Garland in contempt for not producing audio of Special Counsel Hur's interview with President Biden after subpoenas. The President had asserted executive privilege on DOJ Office of Legal Counsel advice. DOJ's OLC later reaffirmed (9 Jan 2025) that non-production on a privilege assertion cannot constitutionally be the basis of contempt action.
matters.authority: U.S. House of Representatives (Judiciary and Oversight Committees)
matters.penalty: None imposed; DOJ did not refer the citation to a grand jury

matters.title: House resolution holding Attorney General Garland in contempt of Congress (Hur interview audio subpoena)
matters.summary: The House passed H. Res. 1292 216-207 recommending that Garland be held in contempt of Congress for not complying with a Judiciary Committee subpoena. He, with the President's executive privilege claim, declined to provide the audio; the vote was along party lines and the Department of Justice did not prosecute.
matters.penalty: None; contempt referral not prosecuted by the Department of Justice

matters.title: Office of Special Counsel Hatch Act finding on 2020 Republican National Convention speech
matters.summary: The U.S. Office of Special Counsel issued a report on November 9, 2021 concluding that Pompeo, while Secretary of State, violated the Hatch Act with his 2020 Republican National Convention speech and changed State Department policy governing such activity; he was one of at least 13 senior Trump administration officials the report found to have violated the Act. NBC News reported no disciplinary action or penalty against him.

matters.title: Florida Commission on Ethics complaints over Trump Foundation contribution
matters.summary: Complaints filed with the Florida Commission on Ethics (including one filed by CREW on July 6, 2016) alleged that Bondi, then Florida Attorney General, solicited a $25,000 Trump Foundation contribution to a political committee supporting her re-election in 2013 while her office was reviewing complaints about Trump University. The commission rejected several complaints against her; earlier the same month a Florida prosecutor found insufficient evidence to support a bribery complaint. The Trump Foundation, not Bondi, paid a $2,500 IRS excise tax on the contribution.

matters.title: DOT Inspector General audit of Secretary's executive travel on DOT aircraft
matters.summary: Audit of Secretaries' use of DOT aircraft, 2017 to June 2023, opened after congressional requests. It found the Office of the Secretary complied with federal regulations for all 15 trips reviewed; the only recommendations concerned FAA flight-hour rate updates. News reports note only three of Buttigieg's trips were justified on cost-effectiveness grounds, others on security or scheduling.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Transportation Office of Inspector General

matters.title: Department of Defense Inspector General evaluation of the Secretary's use of Signal for official business
matters.summary: The DoD Office of Inspector General evaluated the March 2025 Signal group chat about Yemen strikes. According to reporting on the report delivered to Congress on 2 December 2025, it concluded he violated Department regulations by using a personal phone and the Signal app for official business and that the information could have endangered U.S. troops had it been intercepted; it did not determine whether he had declassified the information, which he has authority to do. He declined an interview and gave a written response; his spokesman called the review a total exoneration and he states no classified information was shared.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Defense Office of Inspector General

matters.title: 1983 heroin possession arrest in Rapid City, South Dakota
matters.summary: Kennedy was arrested in September 1983 after heroin was found in his luggage at the Rapid City airport. He pleaded guilty to a felony charge of heroin possession and was sentenced to two years of probation and community service, which he completed.
matters.penalty: Two years of probation and community service

matters.title: Vieques Navy range trespass conviction
matters.summary: Kennedy was arrested in April 2001 in a protest against U.S. Navy bombing exercises on Vieques, Puerto Rico. On July 6, 2001 a U.S. District Court judge sentenced him to 30 days in jail for trespassing after a conviction.
matters.penalty: 30 days in jail

matters.title: OGE notice that Treasury Secretary had not timely complied with ethics agreement divestitures
matters.summary: On 2025-08-11 OGE notified Senate Finance Chairman Crapo that Bessent had failed to timely comply with certain terms of his ethics agreement (deadline 2025-04-28; certification due 2025-05-05) and that the agreement needed further amendment. OGE said it would continue to monitor compliance. Bessent later said (Dec 2025, per press) he had divested the remaining holdings; no OGE confirmation was found.
matters.authority: U.S. Office of Government Ethics (letter to Senate Finance Committee)

matters.title: OGE declined to certify 2018 financial disclosure (Stormchaser Partners interest)
matters.summary: OGE said it was unable to certify the Secretary's 2018 public financial disclosure because his wife's ownership of Stormchaser Partners LLC attributed an interest to him. Treasury ethics advice had allowed him to reacquire an interest he agreed to divest. OGE reported the concern was resolved after he revised his ethics agreement.

matters.title: Treasury IG inquiry into handling of House request for Trump tax returns
matters.summary: At Rep. Richard Neal's request the IG examined how Treasury processed requests for the President's tax returns and concluded the process was proper. The inquiry did not assess the legal opinions Treasury relied on.

matters.title: Treasury OIG review of government aircraft use for official trips, including August 2017 Kentucky trip
matters.summary: Treasury's Inspector General reviewed whether travel, ethics and appropriation laws were observed for Mnuchin's government-aircraft trips. The OIG senior lawyer found no violation of law in seven official trips, while recommending that future requests justify government air travel in greater detail.
matters.authority: Treasury Office of Inspector General (reported by Reuters)

matters.title: Whistleblower complaint concerning handling of a classified report and a referral decision at ODNI
matters.summary: An intelligence community employee filed a complaint alleging a classified report's distribution was limited, and a potential crime not referred to DOJ, for political reasons. The IG's office under prior leadership found the first allegation not credible and administratively closed it in June 2025. The IG delivered it to the Gang of Eight on 2026-02-02; the IG said he would likely determine it does not meet the urgent-concern definition. Gabbard's office said there was no wrongdoing. No finding of misconduct against Gabbard was issued.

matters.title: House criminal contempt of Congress vote over census citizenship-question subpoenas
matters.summary: The House voted 230-198 to hold Attorney General Barr and Commerce Secretary Ross in criminal contempt for not complying with Oversight Committee subpoenas about the 2020 census citizenship question.

matters.title: DOJ declined to prosecute the House contempt citation against Barr and Ross
matters.summary: Deputy Attorney General Jeffrey Rosen informed Speaker Pelosi by letter that DOJ would not prosecute the contempt citation.

matters.title: DOJ Inspector General review of the Roger Stone sentencing recommendation
matters.summary: The OIG (report 24-081) described the handling as highly unusual and found no evidence that DOJ leadership engaged in misconduct or violated department policy; it noted no rule bars an attorney general's involvement. Barr declined to be interviewed.
matters.authority: DOJ Office of the Inspector General

matters.title: Bar disciplinary complaint by 27 DC lawyers over Mueller report handling and Lafayette Square
matters.summary: Disciplinary counsel rejected the complaint by email in August 2020 without opening an investigation; the complainants learned of it in May 2021.

matters.title: House vote holding Attorney General Barr in criminal contempt of Congress (2020 census documents)
matters.summary: The House voted to hold Attorney General Barr and Commerce Secretary Ross in contempt of Congress over subpoenaed documents about the census citizenship question. The Justice Department did not prosecute; Barr and the Department disputed the contempt.

matters.title: FEC MUR 8197: complaint concerning Schiff for Senate contributions and reporting
matters.summary: A complaint by Steven S. Lamb concerning contributions and reporting named Schiff for Senate, its treasurer, the City of Pasadena and Adam Schiff. The Commission voted 5-0 to dismiss in exercise of prosecutorial discretion and closed the file; notifications were sent 2025-03-05.

matters.title: H. Res. 521 (118th Cong.): censure of Rep. Adam Schiff
matters.summary: The House adopted H. Res. 521 (118th Cong.) for censure: Alleged misleading of the American public.
matters.penalty: Censure adopted by the House, 2023-06-21; vote 213-209, 6 present

matters.title: FEC MUR 8197: Schiff for Senate
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 8197 ("Schiff for Senate") named Adam Schiff as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismiss Pursuant to Prosecutorial Discretion".

matters.title: FEC complaint over alleged use of state committee funds in federal Senate bid (MUR 8332)
matters.summary: Americans for Public Trust alleged soft-money violations by Alsobrooks for Senate and related respondents. The Commission voted 4-0 to dismiss the complaint under prosecutorial discretion and close the file as to all respondents; no penalty.

matters.title: FEC complaint over county-funded advertising during Senate campaign (MUR 8189)
matters.summary: Complaint named Alsobrooks for Senate, Alsobrooks, her treasurer and Prince George's County Government. The Commission voted 4-0 to dismiss the allegations; no penalty listed.

matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 8189 ("Alsobrooks for Senate") named Angela Alsobrooks as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.summary: A complaint alleged the King campaign, Americans Elect and others violated the ban on corporate contributions (2 U.S.C. 441b(a)). The Commission voted 5-1 to find no reason to believe King or his campaign violated the provision, and closed the file.

matters.title: FEC MUR 6660: ANGUS KING FOR US SENATE CAMPAIGN
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 6660 ("ANGUS KING FOR US SENATE CAMPAIGN") named Angus King Jr. as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 5711: complaint alleging soft-money solicitation limits violated
matters.summary: The California Republican Party complained that Boxer, Feinstein, Pelosi and Angelides violated 2 U.S.C. 441i(e) and 441a(a). The Commission voted 5-0 to find no reason to believe Boxer violated the cited provisions and closed the file; resolved date is the posted Statement of Reasons.

matters.title: Senate Ethics Committee dismisses Vitter complaint against Reid and Boxer
matters.summary: Sen. David Vitter asked the committee to investigate Reid and Boxer over draft language on health-care contributions. The committee's chief counsel dismissed it, saying mere allegations without supporting evidence do not warrant an investigation. Dates are approximate (article date 2013-09-25).
matters.authority: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics

matters.title: House Ethics Committee review of OCE referral on use of House floor image in campaign email
matters.summary: On OCE referral, the Committee found no evidence Luján conducted campaign activity or solicited contributions from the House floor; it found his campaign consultant's use of a House proceedings image was an inadvertent, technical rule violation and took no action against him.

matters.title: Committee concluded the evidence was insufficient to warrant further action, voted to dismiss the matter and published its report.
matters.summary: Official record: Statement of the Chairwoman and Ranking Member of the Committee on Ethics Regarding Representative Ben Ray Luján

matters.title: OCE referral 17-8362: In June 2016, Representative Luján requested that his congressional campaign committee issue communications during a "sit-in" demonstration.
matters.summary: In June 2016, Representative Luján requested that his congressional campaign committee issue communications during a "sit-in" demonstration. Committee action: Committee Report Issued Dismissing (initial: Committee Report Issued Dismissing).

matters.title: FEC MUR 6888: complaint alleging coordinated communications (2014 Senate campaign)
matters.summary: The FEC notified the campaign of a complaint on 28 Oct 2014; on 25 Feb 2016 it found no reason to believe Sasse and his committee violated 52 U.S.C. 30116 or 30118 and closed the file.

matters.title: Florida Auditor General operational audit of University of Florida President Office expenses (Report 2025-107)
matters.summary: Audit of expenses during Sasse's tenure as UF president (2023-24). Findings included that records did not demonstrate how $6.4 million of consulting services benefited the University, event procurement and travel control gaps, and no documented reasonableness for continuing his compensation after he moved to a professor/adviser role. No legal charge or sanction against Sasse.

matters.title: FEC MUR 8287: complaint re excessive/coordinated contributions (Joshua Super PAC et al.)
matters.summary: Respondents included Bernie Moreno for Senate (his campaign committee). The Commission voted on 12 Feb 2025 to dismiss and close the file effective 17 Mar 2025.

matters.title: Federal bribery, foreign agent and obstruction case (SDNY)
matters.summary: Convicted by a jury in July 2024 following a nine-week trial of bribery, foreign agent and obstruction of justice offenses; sentenced to 11 years in prison on January 29, 2025.
matters.authority: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York (U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y.)
matters.penalty: 11 years in prison

matters.title: Federal bribery case involving Salomon Melgen (D.N.J.)
matters.summary: A November 2017 trial ended in a mistrial; after the court's January 24, 2018 order acquitting on some counts, the Justice Department moved to dismiss the remaining charges on January 31, 2018.
matters.authority: U.S. Department of Justice / U.S. District Court, District of New Jersey

matters.title: Senate Ethics Committee review of gifts from Salomon Melgen
matters.summary: The committee issued a public letter of admonition on April 26, 2018 finding he accepted gifts of significant value from Dr. Melgen contrary to Senate rules and ordered repayment of gifts not yet reimbursed; no further sanction requiring Senate floor action.
matters.authority: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics
matters.penalty: Public letter of admonition (severe admonishment); ordered to repay impermissible gifts

matters.title: FEC MUR 7168: complaint alleging excessive contributions (FACT / Whitaker complaint)

By a 4-1 vote the FEC found no reason to believe any respondent violated 52 U.S.C. 30116(f) or 30118(a) and closed the file.
matters.penalty: None

matters.title: Senate Ethics Committee complaint over 2007 D.C. Madam phone-records allegations

matters.authority: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics

matters.title: CREW complaint: salary-increase hold on Interior Secretary Salazar
matters.summary: The Committee dismissed the complaint, finding no substantial credible evidence of a legal or rules violation while noting the conduct was inappropriate.
matters.authority: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics
matters.penalty: None

matters.title: CREW complaint alleging solicitation of prostitution
matters.summary: The Committee dismissed the complaint without prejudice, making no factual findings, because the alleged conduct preceded his Senate candidacy and service.
matters.authority: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics
matters.penalty: None (dismissed without prejudice)

matters.title: Colorado Independent Ethics Commission complaint over Democratic Governors Association conference

Meeks did not disclose the Ahmad loan as a liability on his 2007 and 2008 Financial Disclosure Statements (later amended), found the evidence did not establish it was an impermissible gift, and found no evidence the omission was knowing or willful; it concluded no further action was necessary and closed the investigation. AP later reported that the ethics committee left the tax question to the IRS and that the IRS said in 1999 that tax laws had not been broken.

matters.summary: Official record: Statement of the Committee on Ethics Regarding Certain Investigative Matters Involving Allegations of Personal Use of Campaign Funds

matters.title: OCE referral 23-9812: Rep. Wesley Hunt’s campaign committee, Hunt for Congress, reported campaign disbursements that may not be legitimate and verifiable campaign expenditu
matters.summary: Rep. Wesley Hunt’s campaign committee, Hunt for Congress, reported campaign disbursements that may not be legitimate and verifiable campaign expenditures attributable to bona fide campaign or political purposes. Committee action: Dismissed (initial: 18A (Unresolved)).

matters.title: FEC MUR 7710: Hunt for Congress
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 7710 ("Hunt for Congress") named Wesley Hunt as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: FEC MUR 8241: William Timmons for Congress
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 8241 ("William Timmons for Congress") named William Timmons as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismiss Pursuant to Prosecutorial Discretion".

matters.title: Committee adopted the investigative subcommittee's report on the Carib News conferences; members were found not to have knowingly violated House rules.
matters.summary: Official record: Statement of the Chair and Ranking Republican Member Regarding Its Report in the Matter of the Carib News Foundation Multi-National Business Conferences in 2007 and 2008

matters.title: Committee filed a report concluding no knowing violation by the Members and decided no further action was required.
matters.summary: Official record: Statement of the Chairman and Ranking Member of the Committee on Ethics Regarding Officially-Connected Travel to Azerbaijan in 2013

matters.title: OCE referral 15-8048: In May 2013, Representative Clarke traveled to Baku, Azerbaijan and Turkey.
matters.summary: In May 2013, Representative Clarke traveled to Baku, Azerbaijan and Turkey. Committee action: Procedural Objection (initial: Procedural Objection).

matters.title: Tennessee Ethics Commission opinion on Alliance Defending Freedom trip gift
matters.summary: The Ethics Commission found that accepting a trip to the 2024 ADF summit was an indirect gift from a lobbyist's organization under state law; the governor's office sought the opinion and the costs were repaid. Date of ruling not shown on the fetched page (reported in 2024).
matters.penalty: Directed to reimburse the organization for trip cost; reported as repaid. No fine reported.

matters.title: Registry of Election Finance complaint about 2018 campaign finance
matters.summary: The Registry dismissed a June 2018 complaint about then-gubernatorial nominee Bill Lee (reported 23 Aug 2018; dismissal on the preceding Wednesday).

matters.title: Registry of Election Finance sworn complaint about campaign funding via businesses and trusts (2018)
matters.summary: A sworn complaint alleged that Bill Lee, then the Republican nominee for governor, used his businesses to support his campaign without disclosure and beyond limits, and exceeded donation limits through trusts. The Registry's 22 Aug 2018 meeting agenda lists 'Bill Lee' under sworn complaints, and a local radio report says the Registry dismissed the complaint on a Wednesday; the dismissal date is not stated in the report.

matters.title: Complaints over transfer of $1.2 million in campaign contributions to governor campaign
matters.summary: The commission unanimously dismissed two complaints, finding Ferguson, then attorney general, followed the disclosure rules in effect when he moved $1.2 million from past campaigns into his governor campaign.

matters.title: Public Disclosure Commission complaints over transfer of surplus campaign funds
matters.summary: The commission unanimously dismissed two complaints about more than $1.2 million moved from surplus accounts into the 2024 gubernatorial campaign; the campaign had amended its reports to follow the commission's guidance. No violation was found.

matters.title: Washington PDC case 137263: transfers of surplus campaign funds to 2024 governor campaign
matters.summary: Complaints alleged Ferguson failed to identify names and required information of contributors who approved using Attorney General campaign contributions for his 2024 Governor campaign (RCW 42.17A.235 and .240). The Commission accepted a stipulation signed by the campaign and PDC staff and dismissed the allegations with no finding of a violation; the campaign had filed amended reports under new PDC guidance.
matters.penalty: None

matters.title: Executive Ethics Board case 2025-061: guest on State Patrol aircraft
matters.summary: The Board's results page lists an agreed Stipulation and Order for the Office of the Governor (RCW 42.52.070 and 42.52.160): the Governor agreed he may have violated the Ethics in Public Service Act by allowing a private citizen to travel on the Washington State Patrol aircraft assigned for official use by the Governor's Office.
matters.penalty: $4,000 civil penalty, $2,000 suspended if no further violations for two years

matters.title: FEC MUR 7583: KEMP FOR GOVERNOR, INC.
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 7583 ("KEMP FOR GOVERNOR, INC.") named Brian Kemp as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: Rhode Island GOP ethics complaint over $228 Capital Grille lunch paid by lobbyist
matters.summary: Complaint by the Rhode Island Republican Party alleged a gift over $25 from a lobbyist for a firm seeking a state contract. The Commission opened an investigation and on 23 Jan 2024 voted 6-0 to dismiss, finding the governor acted reasonably and in good faith.

matters.title: Rhode Island Ethics Commission complaint over a January 2023 lunch paid by a lobbyist
matters.summary: The state Republican Party complained that a lobbyist for a redevelopment firm paid for a lunch with the governor. The Commission voted unanimously to dismiss, finding no knowing and willful violation; staff noted the lunch value exceeded the gift limit.

matters.title: Rhode Island Ethics Commission complaint over lobbyist-paid Capital Grille lunch
matters.summary: The state Republican Party complained that Governor McKee allowed lobbyist Jeff Britt to pay for a January 2023 lunch, above the $25 gift limit. The commission opened an investigation, then voted 6-0 on 23 Jan 2024 that there was no probable cause of a knowing and willful violation and dismissed the complaint with prejudice. The investigative report found he acted reasonably and in good faith.

matters.title: Ethics Commission fine over undisclosed Taiwan trip (as Lieutenant Governor)
matters.summary: As Lieutenant Governor, McKee failed to report an April 2017 trip to Taiwan paid for by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. After a complaint by the former state GOP chairman and a private meeting with the commission, he was fined $250. He said he had made a mistake and later also acknowledged two other unreported trips.
matters.penalty: $250 fine

matters.title: FPPC settlement over late behested payment reports (2019-2024)
matters.summary: Newsom agreed to a settlement over 18 behested payment reports filed late; the FPPC characterized the failures as negligent.

matters.title: FPPC fine over 36 late behested payment reports (2024-2025)
matters.summary: The FPPC approved a 3-0 consent-calendar fine over 36 behested payment reports filed late; the reports were filed before the Enforcement Division received referrals.

matters.title: FPPC stipulation: late behested payment reports and sub-vendor disclosure (Newsom for Governor 2018 and Gavin Newsom)
matters.summary: Stipulation, decision and order (FPPC Case Nos. 2021-00299 and 2021-00644) naming Gavin Newsom and his 2018 candidate committee as respondents: late behested payment reports for payments over $5,000 (2019-2024) and a late sub-vendor payment disclosure. Total penalty $13,000. FPPC found no evidence of intent to conceal and described the violations as negligent; all reports were filed before Enforcement Division contact.

matters.title: FPPC enforcement decision: 18 late behested payment reports (FPPC No. 25/1196)
matters.summary: FPPC enforcement decision listing Gavin Newsom as respondent for failing to timely file 18 behested payment reports under Government Code section 84224; penalty $31,500.

matters.title: Misdemeanor assault of Guardian reporter Ben Jacobs
matters.summary: Then congressman-elect Gianforte pleaded guilty to misdemeanor assault of a reporter and was sentenced on June 12, 2017.
matters.authority: Gallatin County Justice of the Peace Court, Montana
matters.penalty: 40 hours community service, 20 hours anger management counseling, $385 fine; no jail; 180 days to petition to remove conviction

matters.title: Misdemeanor assault of a reporter (Gallatin County Justice Court)
matters.summary: Gianforte pleaded guilty to misdemeanor assault of Guardian reporter Ben Jacobs, from a May 24, 2017 incident, and was sentenced by Justice of the Peace Rick West.
matters.penalty: 40 hours community service, 20 hours anger management counseling, $385 fine, no jail time

matters.title: Written warning from Montana FWP for wolf-trapping certification rule
matters.summary: FWP issued a written warning after a wolf was trapped in February 2021 before the required wolf-trapping education course was completed; FWP described it as an education opportunity.
matters.penalty: Written warning only

matters.title: LaBreche v. Gianforte (COPP 2015-CFP-010): candidacy timing complaint
matters.summary: Complaint alleged Greg Gianforte acted as a 2016 gubernatorial candidate before filing his statement of candidacy. The Commissioner found insufficient evidence of a violation and dismissed the complaint in full.

matters.title: Luckey v. Gianforte (COPP 2020-CFP-031): missing 'paid for by' attribution
matters.summary: Commissioner declared the attribution complaint to have merit (campaign mailer lacked the required 'Paid for by' line); the campaign halted distribution and corrected the material within the statutory period, so no violation was held and the complaint was dismissed.

matters.title: Luckey v. Gianforte and Montana First Action (COPP 2020-CFP-032A/032B): alleged coordination
matters.summary: Complaint alleged the Gianforte campaign coordinated with the political committee Montana First Action and accepted prohibited or excess contributions. The Commissioner dismissed the complaint in October 2020, while recommending the campaign file a firewall policy.

matters.title: Luckey v. Gianforte (COPP 2020-CFP-044): primary and general election funds
matters.summary: Commissioner found sufficient facts that the 2020 gubernatorial campaign spent general-election contributions before the primary and transferred $180,729.09 of primary funds to the general account without first applying them to primary obligations, ordered corrective action within 14 days, and found a civil fine or prosecution justified, referring the matter to the Lewis and Clark County Attorney. Decision dated October 2020 (day not legible; file created 19 Oct 2020). The COPP docket lists the final resolution only as 'settlement/litigation in process'; no settlement amount was found on the site.

matters.title: Luckey v. Gianforte (COPP 2020-CFP-048A): alleged coordination with Republican Governors Association
matters.summary: Complaint alleged the campaign coordinated with the Republican Governors Association and failed to report the activity. Dismissed by the Commissioner in July 2021 (day not legible).

matters.title: Busse for Montana v. Gov. Gianforte and Jake Eaton (COPP-2024-ETH-008): state postcards
matters.summary: Ethics complaint alleged Department of Revenue postcards benefited the Governor's campaign. The Commissioner found the activity permitted as an official duty and dismissed the complaint as frivolous or unsupported.

matters.title: Busse for Montana v. Gianforte (COPP-2024-CFP-029): campaign expenditure reporting
matters.summary: Commissioner dismissed several allegations and found sufficient evidence for others (travel expenditure detail), but determined prosecution was not justified. Dismissal contingent on corrective action issued 3 Oct 2024; the campaign amended four C-5 reports; final order of dismissal 10 Feb 2025.

matters.title: Busse for Montana v. Gianforte (COPP-2024-CFP-037): rally and ad reporting
matters.summary: Complaint concerned reporting of a Bozeman rally appearance, ad attribution and ad expenditure details. All allegations dismissed in full.

matters.title: Busse for Montana v. Gianforte (COPP-2024-CFP-039): attribution lacking last name
matters.summary: Complaint alleged campaign materials omitted the candidate's last name in the attribution. Commissioner found a technical, de minimis issue and dismissed the complaint in full.

matters.title: Busse for Montana v. Gov. Gianforte (COPP-2024-ETH-011): campaign use of public photograph
matters.summary: Ethics complaint over use of a state-event photograph in campaign material. Dismissed for failure to state a potential violation of the Ethics Code; no costs assessed.

matters.title: FEC MUR 7249: GREG GIANFORTE
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 7249 ("GREG GIANFORTE") named Greg Gianforte as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "Dismissed-Other".

matters.title: Complaints over campaign-funded charter flight to Florida and recall-period contribution limits
matters.summary: The Michigan Department of State resolved two campaign finance complaints against Whitmer and her committee without finding a violation: use of committee funds for a chartered flight was held permissible on safety grounds (and the committee was repaid fair market value), and contributions above normal limits during recall efforts were allowed under a longstanding 1983 interpretation.
matters.authority: Michigan Department of State (Bureau of Elections)
matters.penalty: None; Whitmer reimbursed her campaign committee the fair market value of the flights

matters.title: Campaign finance complaints over chartered flight and recall-period donations
matters.summary: The Department of State resolved two complaints against Whitmer and her campaign committee, finding the flight use permissible and no violation in donations accepted during recall efforts.
matters.authority: Michigan Department of State, Bureau of Elections
matters.penalty: None; Whitmer reimbursed the committee for the flights' market value

matters.title: Campaign finance complaint: campaign-funded chartered flight
matters.summary: A complaint concerned campaign committee funds used to pay for a chartered flight for the Governor's non-state travel. The Department concluded the use was permissible because its purpose was the Governor's physical safety amid credible and ongoing threats; the Governor later reimbursed the committee for the market value of first-class flights for herself and her family. The Department found no legal violation.
matters.authority: Michigan Department of State, Bureau of Elections

matters.title: Campaign finance complaint: donations above contribution limits during recall efforts
matters.summary: A complaint concerned the Whitmer for Governor committee accepting donations above the usual contribution limits during recall efforts. The Department found no evidence of a violation because the practice is permitted under a 1983 interpretive statement and 1984 declaratory ruling; it said it would welcome a request to revisit that policy.
matters.authority: Michigan Department of State, Bureau of Elections

matters.title: Excess 2010 gubernatorial campaign contributions (State Ethics Commission case)
matters.summary: A 2014 complaint alleged McMaster accepted over $50,000 in excess contributions in his 2010 governor campaign. The Ethics Commission issued an order in March 2016; he paid a $5,100 fine and refunded excess contributions in January 2017. His attorney said the violation was unintentional.
matters.penalty: $5,100 fine; repayment of excess 2010 contributions (reported as $73,000 by FITSNews; Post and Courier reported a $69,200 refund to 51 donors)

matters.title: State Ethics Commission order on 2010 campaign contributions
matters.summary: Following a 2014 complaint, the commission ordered McMaster to refund excess contributions to his 2010 governor bid and pay a fine; dates approximate (order March 2016 per Post and Courier).
matters.penalty: $5,100 fine and refund of excess 2010 contributions ($69,200 to 51 donors per his attorney)

matters.title: State Ethics Commission complaint C2014-143: excess 2010 campaign contributions (as Lieutenant Governor)
matters.summary: The Commission's resolved-complaints archive lists 'MCMASTER, HENRY D.' as Case 2014-143. Its 16 Sept 2015 open-session minutes record a 7-0 vote denying his motion to dismiss. The Post and Courier reported that an order issued in March (2016) required him to refund excess contributions from his 2010 governor campaign and pay a $5,100 fine, which was paid before he became governor.
matters.penalty: $5,100 fine; refund of about $69,200 in excess contributions to 51 donors

matters.title: Inaugural committee paid event debt ~10 months after legal deadline
matters.summary: Mills' January 2019 inaugural committee ran about $63,000 over its estimate and kept collecting donations past the legal cutoff to pay the City of Augusta. The commission fined the committee $2,000 on Dec. 18, 2019 after the debt was paid; the committee's attorney had argued for no more than $500.
matters.authority: Maine Commission on Governmental Ethics and Election Practices
matters.penalty: $2,000 fine against the inaugural committee (maximum was $10,000)

matters.title: Office of Congressional Ethics referral on promotional video and menswear photo shoot
matters.summary: While a U.S. Representative, Polis appeared in a Riot Games video and in a photo shoot with a district menswear company whose photos were used in advertising. OCE referred whether this implicated endorsement or official-resource rules; the Ethics Committee took no further action and closed the matter.
matters.authority: U.S. House Committee on Ethics (referral from Office of Congressional Ethics)

matters.title: Committee released a report concluding the video and event did not violate House rules and voted to dismiss the matter.
matters.summary: Official record: Statement of the Chairman and Ranking Member of the Committee on Ethics Regarding Representative Jared Polis

matters.title: OCE referral 15-6333: Representative Jared Polis appeared in a video produced and distributed by the video game company Riot Games, in which he is seen playing the company'
matters.summary: Representative Jared Polis appeared in a video produced and distributed by the video game company Riot Games, in which he is seen playing the company's League of Legends video game. Committee action: Committee Report Issued Dismissing (initial: Committee Report Issued Dismissing).

matters.title: House Ethics Committee review of Riot Games video and Ninox clothing event
matters.summary: After an OCE referral, the Committee reviewed whether Polis's appearance in a Riot Games video and a clothing event with Ninox violated rules on endorsements or use of official resources. It found no violation, dismissed the matter and took no further action.
matters.authority: U.S. House Committee on Ethics (referral from Office of Congressional Ethics)

matters.title: Colorado Secretary of State complaint on personal financial disclosure (BridgeHealth)
matters.summary: Complaint alleging Polis failed to disclose his BridgeHealth Medical investment on his candidate disclosure form was dismissed because it did not allege a violation of Colorado campaign finance law.

matters.title: FEC MUR 5981: FRIENDS OF JARED POLIS COMMITTEE
matters.summary: The Federal Election Commission's Matter Under Review 5981 ("FRIENDS OF JARED POLIS COMMITTEE") named Jared Polis as a respondent; the Commission's disposition for that respondent was "No Reason to Believe".

matters.title: Cook County Inspector General report on Gold Coast mansion property tax appeals
matters.summary: A confidential report dated Sept. 28, 2018 concluded the county was a victim of a scheme to defraud via sworn affidavits supporting a vacancy factor on the Pritzkers' Astor St. property; toilets were removed in 2015. Pritzker called it a politically leaked report and repaid the amount; his lawyer denied wrongdoing. No charges are reported in the sources reviewed.
matters.authority: Cook County Office of the Inspector General
matters.penalty: Repaid about $330,000 in property tax relief (reported)

matters.title: Cook County Inspector General findings on Gold Coast mansion property tax refunds
matters.summary: A confidential memo from Inspector General Patrick Blanchard, made public in October 2018, concluded the county fell victim to a scheme to defraud in tax reductions on a Pritzker-owned Gold Coast mansion after toilets were removed before an appraisal inspection. It recommended recovering refunds of $132,747.18 (2012-14) and $198,684.85 savings (2015-16). Pritzker said he followed the rules and repaid the amount.
matters.authority: Cook County Office of the Independent Inspector General
matters.penalty: Inspector General recommended recovery of more than $330,000; Pritzker repaid about $330,000 in October 2018

matters.title: Cook County inspector general report on property tax appeals for a Gold Coast Chicago mansion (pre-office)
matters.summary: A report by the Cook County inspector general, dated Sept. 28, 2018, concluded the county had been the victim of a scheme to defraud, executed in part through affidavits, in reassessment appeals for a Pritzker-owned Gold Coast property (toilets removed before an inspection, assessed value cut from about $6.3 million to about $1.1 million). Pritzker said 'We followed the rules' and later agreed to repay the savings.
matters.authority: Cook County Office of the Independent Inspector General
matters.penalty: Report recommended the county seek to recover $331,432.03 in property tax savings; on 2018-10-02 Pritzker's campaign said he would repay about $330,000. No criminal charges reported in the pages read.

matters.title: Louisiana Board of Ethics charges over undisclosed free flights
matters.summary: Charged by the board in 2023 over a free 2021 flight to Hawaii on a donor's plane while attorney general and other unreported trips; settled by consent opinion in September 2025 with a $900 fine and disclosure of nearly 20 free trips valued at over $13,000, avoiding a hearing before administrative judges.
matters.penalty: $900 fine

matters.title: Louisiana Board of Ethics consent opinion over unreported free flights
matters.summary: The board charged Landry in 2023 with failing to report a 2021 Hawaii trip on a donor's plane while attorney general. In September 2025 the board approved a consent settlement under which he paid a $900 fine and disclosed other free flights.
matters.penalty: $900 fine; disclosure of previously unreported complimentary trips

matters.title: Louisiana Board of Ethics consent opinion: undisclosed free flights while Attorney General (Docket 2022-455)
matters.summary: The Board of Ethics charged Landry in 2023 with failing to report a June 2021 flight to Hawaii on a donor's private plane while he was attorney general. On Sept. 5, 2025 the board approved a consent opinion under which Landry paid a $900 fine and disclosed other free travel; the board also issued an advisory opinion that the governor must report free travel and lodging. AP report of the board's action; the ethics.la.gov consent opinion pages returned errors and could not be read.
matters.penalty: $900 fine; publicly disclosed about 19 instances of complimentary travel worth $13,540

matters.title: Civil suit by former employee against Pillen Family Farms (immigration-status hiring, records)
matters.summary: A former HR employee alleged the company hired workers without proof of immigration status and altered records to avoid taxes. The case was dismissed with prejudice; plaintiff agreed not to refile. It was unclear whether a settlement was reached. Pillen's lawyers denied wrongdoing.
matters.authority: Civil court (Nebraska); suit filed against Pillen Family Farms, not Pillen personally

matters.title: Ethics complaints over use of sheriff badge and uniform in 2022 campaign materials
matters.summary: The commission concluded its investigation via settlement: it found Lombardo did not purposefully violate ethics law by using his old badge in campaign commercials. Date is that of the news report.
matters.penalty: $5,000 to the state General Fund

matters.title: Nevada Commission on Ethics: use of sheriff's uniform/badge images in 2022 gubernatorial campaign (Case Nos. 21-062C, 21-082C)
matters.summary: While Clark County Sheriff and a declared candidate for governor, Lombardo's campaign used four images showing him in uniform or wearing his badge. The Commission opened Case 21-062C on or about Sept 15, 2021 (a second complaint, 21-082C, followed Oct 21, 2021). After a July 25, 2023 hearing it voted 4-2 that there were four willful violations of NRS 281A.400(7) (none of 281A.400(2)) and issued an opinion on Aug 31, 2023 with a $20,000 fine and censure. Lombardo sought judicial review; the Nevada Supreme Court reversed a dismissal on June 18, 2025. On Sept 23, 2025 the Commission approved (5-3) a stipulated agreement treating the conduct as one non-willful violation, with a $5,000 payment, which also resolved his court case. Lombardo maintains he acted with a good faith belief the conduct was lawful.
matters.penalty: $5,000 civil penalty paid to the State General Fund under a stipulated agreement; earlier (Aug 31, 2023) opinion had imposed a $20,000 fine and public censure for four willful violations of NRS 281A.400(7), which the agreement resolved

matters.title: Financial disclosure: unreported Honolulu condominium interest (as state senator)
matters.summary: Commission found Green had not reported his interest in a condominium on financial disclosure statements from 2011 onward; he cited a misunderstanding of reporting rules. Resolved by a $300 penalty; commission said further action was not in the public interest. Conduct predates his governorship.
matters.penalty: $300 administrative penalty

matters.title: Hawaii State Ethics Commission settlement over financial disclosure statements (as state senator)
matters.summary: The commission resolved its review of Green's financial disclosure statements by settlement; he had not reported his interest in an Honolulu condominium unit. The penalty was reduced because he cooperated. The reported resolution was not an admission of a violation.
matters.penalty: $300 administrative penalty

matters.title: Wake County criminal-libel investigation over 2020 campaign TV ad
matters.summary: A complaint by opponent Jim O'Neill about Stein's 2020 'Survivor' ad led to a Wake County investigation under a 1931 criminal-libel statute that Stein challenged as unconstitutional. After the 4th Circuit ruled for Stein, the DA closed the investigation on Feb 9, 2023. No charges were filed.
matters.authority: Wake County District Attorney's Office (Lorrin Freeman)

matters.title: Wake County DA investigation of 2020 campaign ad under NC criminal libel statute closed
matters.summary: Following a 2020 complaint by opponent Jim O'Neill about Stein's 'Survivor' campaign ad, the state elections board referred findings to the Wake County DA, and a grand jury reportedly asked for indictments against Stein and two campaign aides in 2022. The 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals found the 1931 law likely unconstitutional (Feb. 8, 2023); on Feb. 9, 2023 the DA closed the investigation and prosecution, citing the two-year statute of limitations. No charges were filed.

matters.title: Pay-to-play allegation: Sunshine Residential Homes rate increase after $100,000 inaugural donation
matters.summary: The Arizona Attorney General's office declined to file criminal charges against Gov. Hobbs over allegations tied to a group-home provider that donated $100,000 to her inaugural celebration and later received a rate increase. Hobbs denies wrongdoing. A separate review by the Maricopa County Attorney and the state auditor general was reported as ongoing.

matters.title: Attorney General review of Sunshine Residential Homes contributions and Department of Child Safety rate increases; prosecution declined
matters.summary: The Arizona Attorney General issued findings on an investigation into allegations that Sunshine Residential Homes, LLC obtained Department of Child Safety rate increases in exchange for political contributions to Governor Hobbs. The Attorney General declined prosecution, stating the investigation found no evidence of the quid pro quo needed for a bribery charge, and urged legislation on contractor donations. KJZZ (Aug 24, 2026) reported no charges against the governor and a separate Auditor General probe continuing.

matters.title: FEC MUR 7519: ARIZONA DEMOCRATIC PARTY
